akhfash:2-2.t: As for the saying of [Allah] the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ﴾, ﴿أَجَلٌ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and is not [conjoined] to [the object of] ﴿قَضَىۤ﴾.

akhfash:6-6.t: [Allah the Exalted said] ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّكُمْ﴾: it is as if He informed the Prophet ﷺ and then addressed him together with them, as He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾, bringing the third-person form while He was addressing [them], because he is the one addressed.

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ﴾: the lām of ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ﴾ has fatḥa because, given the meaning of "كَتَبَ" (He prescribed), it is as if He said "by Allah, He will surely gather you". Then He substituted, saying ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, i.e. He will surely gather those who have lost themselves.

akhfash:14-14.t:
[And He said] ﴿أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾ as a naʿt (adjective). Some read ﴿فاطرُ﴾ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ [i.e. a new start], i.e. He is the Originator.
And some read ﴿وهو يُطْعِمُ ولا يَطْعَم﴾, and some read ﴿ولا يُطْعَمُ﴾; and ﴿يَطْعَمُ﴾ is the [proper] way, because you only say "هُوَ يُطْعَمُ" (he is fed) of one who eats, so you inform [us] that He does not eat anything. And ﴿يُطْعَمُ﴾ is only read because people agree on it. [Translator's note: the passage is as written; the two statements about ﴿يَطْعَمُ﴾ and ﴿يُطْعَمُ﴾ appear inconsistent, possibly through copying errors.]
And He said ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾, i.e. and it was said to me: "do not be". ﴿أُمِرْتُ﴾ became a substitute for that, because when he said ﴿أُمِرْتُ﴾ he informed [us] that it had been said to him.

akhfash:23-23.t:
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا﴾ as a ṣifa (qualifier). Some read ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ in the sense of "O our Lord". As for ﴿واللهِ﴾, it is genitive as an oath; if there were no wāw in it, you would put it in the accusative and say "اللهَ رَبَّنا". Some of them use the genitive without the wāw because this name is so frequently used, but this is poor by analogy. The like of it has come irregularly, in their saying [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-ninth shāhid]:
* وَبَلَدٍ عامِيَّةٍ أَعْماؤُهُ *
(And many a land whose blind wastes are trackless.)
[And] it is only "رُبَّ بَلَدٍ" (many a land). And he said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and ninetieth shāhid]:
نَهَيْتُكَ عَنْ طِلابِكَ أُمَّ عَمْرٍو * بِعاقِبَةٍ وَأَنْت إِذٍ صَحِيحُ
(I forbade you from pursuing Umm ʿAmr in good time, while you were then healthy.)
He means "حِينَئِدٍ" (at that time): he dropped "حينَ" and left it implied. And the wāw became a substitute for "رُبَّ" in "وَبَلَدٍ". They may also put "بَلْ" in this position. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-first shāhid]:
ما بالُ عَيْنٍ عَنْ كَراها قَدْ جَفَتْ * مُسْبِلَةً تَسْتَنُّ لَمّا عَرَفَتْ
داراً لِلَيْلى بَعْدَ حَوْلٍ قَدْ عَفَتْ * بَلْ جَوْزِ تَيْهاءَ كَظَهْرِ الحَجَفَتْ
(What is the matter with an eye that has shunned its sleep, flowing and pouring when it recognised an abode of Laylā, effaced after a year? — Nay, many a middle of a trackless desert like the back of a leather shield.)
[this is] according to those who say "طَلَحَتْ" [i.e. pronounce the feminine ending as tāʾ in pause].

akhfash:25-25.t:
[And] He said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِيۤ آذَانِهِمْ وَقْراً﴾. The singular of "الأَكِنَّة" is "الكِنان" (covering). "الوَقْر" in the ear is [with fatḥa], and "الوِقْر" on the back (a load) is with kasra. Yūnus said: "I asked Ruʾba", and he said: "وَقِرَتْ أُذُنُهُ", "تَوْقَرُ", when there is "الوَقْر" (deafness) in it. Abū Zayd said: "I heard the Arabs say 'أُذُنٌ مَوْقُورَةٌ' (a deafened ear)", so this one says "وُقِرَتْ". The poet said [in the ramal metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-second shāhid]:
وَكلامٍ سَيِّىءٍ قَدْ وُقِرَتْ * أُذُنِي مِنْهُ وَما بِي مِنْ صَمَمْ
(And many an evil word from which my ear has been made deaf, though I have no deafness.)
And He said ﴿أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾. Some claim that its singular is "أُسْطُورَة" and some "إِسّطارَة"; but I consider it only one of the plurals that have no singular, like "عَبادِيد" (scattered groups), "مَذاكِير" and "أَبابِيل" (flocks). Some said the singular of "الأَبابيل" is "إبِّيل", and some said "إِبَّوْل", like "عِجَّوْل"; but I did not find the Arabs knowing a singular for it. As for "الشَّماطِيط" (scattered pieces), they claim its singular is "شِمْطاط". All of these have a singular, except that it is not used and has not been spoken, because this pattern occurs only as a plural. I heard the eloquent Arabs say "أَرْسَلَ إِبِلَهُ أَبابيلَ" (he sent off his camels in flocks), meaning "groups", and no singular has been spoken for it.

akhfash:26-26.t: As for His saying: ﴿وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾, it is from "نَأَيْتُ", "يَنْأَى", "نَأْياً" (to keep far away).

akhfash:27-27.t: And He said: ﴿وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — accusative because it is the answer to a wish, and what follows the wāw is like what follows the fāʾ. And if you wish, you put it in the nominative and treat it like an oath, as if they said "and we will not — by Allah — deny the signs of our Lord, and we will be — by Allah — among the believers". This is when this line is cut off from the first. The nominative is the [proper] way of speech, and that is how we read the verse. [And] when one puts it in the accusative, he makes it a wāw of conjunction, as though they had wished not to deny and to be [among the believers]. And this — Allah knows best — is not the case, because they did not wish for faith; they only wished to be sent back, and they declared that they would not deny and would be among the believers.

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿أَلاَ سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ﴾, because it is from "وَزَرَ", "يَزِرُ", "وِزْراً" (to bear a burden). One also says "وُزِرَ", so "هُوَ مَوْزُورٌ" (he is burdened). Yūnus claimed that both are said.

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾ with kasra on "إِنَّ" because of the entry of the additional lām after it.

akhfash:34-34.t: And He said ﴿وَلَقدْ جَآءَكَ مِن نَّبَإِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾, as you say "قَدْ أَصَابَنا من مَطَرٍ" (some rain has fallen on us) and "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ حَديث" (there has been some talk).

akhfash:35-35.t:
And He said ﴿نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: "النَفَق" is not from "النَفقَة" (expenditure) but from "النَّافِقاء" (the jerboa's burrow exit); He means a way into the earth.
And He said ﴿فَإِن ٱسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾ and did not say "then do it"; that is because He left it implied. The poet said [in the khafīf metre; this is the one hundred and thirty-second shāhid]: [Translator's note: the number is as written; the sequence here would lead one to expect the one hundred and ninety-third.]
فَبِحَظٍّ مِمّا نَعِيشُ ولا تَذْ * هَبْ بِكِ التُرَّهاتِ في الأَهْوالِ
(So [live] with a share of what we live on, and let not vain fancies carry you off into perils.)
He left "فَعِيشى" (so live) implied.

akhfash:38-38.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلاَّ أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾: He means the plural of "أمة" (community).

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُم إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ أَتَتْكُمْ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ﴾: what follows the tāʾ in His saying ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُم﴾ came only for address, and the tāʾ was left with fatḥa as it is for the singular. It is like the kāf of "رُوَيْدَكَ زَيْداً" (go easy on Zayd) when you say "أَرْوِدْ زَيْداً". This kāf has no [grammatical] position to be called genitive, nominative or accusative; it is only [a sign] of address, like the kāf of "ذاك". Like that is the Arabs' saying "أَبْصِرْكَ زَيْداً": they put in the kāf for address, and it is only "أَبْصِرْ زيداً" (look at Zayd).

akhfash:46-46.t: And He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾: He referred it to "hearing", or to what was taken from them.

akhfash:52-52.t: And He said ﴿فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: the first is accusative as an answer to His saying ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ﴾, and the other is accusative by His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ﴾ and ﴿أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوۤءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾. His saying ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾, i.e. He prescribed that whoever does [evil]… And His saying ﴿فَأِنَّهُ﴾ [with kasra] is as a new start, i.e. then for him is forgiveness and mercy, for He is Forgiving, Merciful. Some read ﴿فأنَّهُ﴾ [with fatḥa], meaning by it the noun and leaving the khabar (predicate) implied; he meant "فَأنَّ" (then [it is a fact] that…).

akhfash:55-55.t: And He said ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [with tāʾ], because the people of the Ḥijāz say "هِيَ السَّبِيلُ" (the way, feminine). Some read ﴿ولتستبين﴾* meaning [you,] the Prophet ﷺ. And some read ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ﴾ [with yāʾ] in the dialect of the Banū Tamīm.

akhfash:56-56.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذاً﴾, and some read ﴿ضَلَلْتُ﴾; they are two dialect forms. Whoever says "ضَلِلْتُ" says "تَضَلُّ", and whoever says "ضَلَلْتُ" says "تَضِلُّ". We read it with the fatḥa*. [Translator's note: both quotations are written identically; the second was evidently meant to be «ضَلِلْتُ».]

akhfash:59-59.t: And He said ﴿وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ رَطْبٍ وَلاَ يَابِسٍ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: genitive by [conjunction to what follows] ﴿مِنْ﴾; if you wish, you put it in the nominative [by conjunction to the subject of] "تسقط"; and if you wish, you make it a new start (mubtadaʾ) and cut it off from the first.

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾, and He said in another place ﴿وَخِيفَةً﴾. "الخُفْيَة" is concealment, and "الخِيفَة" is from fear and dread.

akhfash:65-65.t: And He said ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾, because it is from "لَبَسَ", "يَلْبِسُ", "لَبْساً" (to confuse).

akhfash:70-70.t:
And He said ﴿أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾; it is from "أبْسَلَ", "إبْسالاً" (to give over to destruction).
[And] He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُواْ﴾.

akhfash:71-71.t:
As for His saying ﴿حَيْرَانَ لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ﴾: every "فَعْلان" that has a [feminine] "فَعْلى" is a diptote, both as definite and as indefinite.
As for His saying ﴿إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾, the alif in ﴿ائْتِنا﴾ is a connecting alif (alif waṣl), but after it is a radical hamza, which is the one in "أتَى"; it is the yāʾ in your saying "إيتِنا". But it was not pronounced with hamza when the connecting alif appeared, because the connecting alif has a hamza when one begins with it, and they disliked the meeting of two hamzas.
And He said ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, meaning: we have only been commanded so that we submit to the Lord of the worlds — as He said ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. I have been commanded only that.

akhfash:72-72.t: Then He said ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاةَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ﴾, i.e. and we have been commanded: establish the prayer and fear Him. Or the verb is connected by the lām [in the preceding ﴿لِنُسْلِمَ﴾], and the meaning is "I have been commanded to be", just as it is connected by the lām in His saying ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾.

akhfash:73-73.t:
And He said ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾. He said: ﴿يَوْم﴾ is in iḍāfa (genitive construct) with His saying ﴿كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾, and it is accusative, and it has no overt khabar — and Allah knows best; it is according to what I have explained to you.
And likewise ﴿يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّوَرِ﴾. Some read ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَحُ في الصُّورِ﴾ and some read ﴿يَنْفُخُ﴾ ﴿عَالِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَادَةِ﴾.

akhfash:74-74.t:
And He said ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾ with fatḥa [i.e. genitive of a diptote] if you make ﴿آزَرَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from ﴿أَبيهِ﴾. It has also been read in the nominative as a vocative, as if he said "O Āzar"*. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-third shāhid]:
إِنَّ عَلَيَّ اللهَ أَنْ تُبايِعا * تُقْتَلَ صُبْحاً أَوْ تَجِيىءَ طائَعا
(I owe it to Allah that you shall swear allegiance — be killed at dawn or come obediently.)
He substituted "تُقْتَلَ صُبْحاً" for "تُبَايِعَ".

akhfash:76-76.t:
And He said ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾, and some read ﴿أَجَنَّ﴾. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-fourth shāhid]:
فَلَمّا أَجَنَّ اللَّيْلُ بِتْنا كَأَنَّنا * علىكَثْرَةِ الأَعْداءِ مُحْتَرِسَانِ
(When the night grew dark we spent the night as though, with the many enemies, we were two on guard.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-fifth shāhid]:
* أَجَنَّكَ اللَّيلُ وَلَمَّا تَشْتَفِ *
(The night has covered you before you were satisfied.)
He made "الجَنّ" the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "جَنَّ". It may also be right that it is "أَجَنَّ" and that this is its maṣdar, as one says "العَطاء" and "الإعطاء" (giving). As for His saying ﴿أَكْنَنتُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, they say for its passive participle "مَكْنُونٌ", and some say "مُكَنّ". You say "كَنَنْتُ الجاريَةَ" (I kept the girl sheltered) when you protected her, and "كَنَنْتُها مِن الشَّمْسِ" and also "أَكْنَنْتُها مِن الشَّمْسِ" (I shielded her from the sun). And they say "هِيَ مَكْنُونَة" and "مُكَنَّةٌ". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-sixth shāhid]:
قَدْ كُنْتُ أُعْطِيهُمُ مالِي وَأَمْنَحُهُمْ * عِرْضِي وَعِنْدَهُمُ في الصَّدْرِ مَكْنُونُ
(I used to give them my wealth and grant them my honour, while they had [rancour] concealed in the breast.)
because [the tribe of] Qays say "كَنَنْتُ العِلْمَ" (I concealed the knowledge), so it is "مَكْنُونْ"; and the Banū Tamīm say "أَكْنَنْتُ العِلْمَ", so it is "مُكَنُّ"; and "كَنَنْتُ الجارِيَةَ", so she is "مَكْنُونَةٌ". In the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, and He said ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ﴾. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-seventh shāhid]:
قَدْ كُنَّ يَكْنُنَّ الوُجُوهَ تَسَتُّراً * فَاليومَ حينَ بَدَوْنَ للنُّظّارِ
(They used to keep their faces hidden, veiling themselves; but today, when they have appeared to the onlookers…)
And Qays recite it "قَدْكُن يُكْنِنَّ".
And He said ﴿فلمَّآ أَفَلَ﴾: it is from "يَأْفِل", "أُفُولاً" (to set).

akhfash:78-78.t:
As for his saying of the sun ﴿هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾, it may be on [the sense of] "this rising thing is my Lord";
or on [the sense] that the sun appeared while they used to mention the lord in their speech, so he said to them ﴿هَـٰذَا رَبّي﴾. This is only a parable he struck for them so that they would know, when it disappeared, that the like of it ought not to be a god, and to guide them to the oneness of Allah and that nothing is like Him. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-eighth shāhid]:
مَكَثْتَ حَوْلاً ثُمَّ جِئْتَ قاشِراً * لا حَمَلَتْ مِنْكَ كِراعٌ حافِرا
(You stayed a whole year, then came [as] a calamity; may no shank of yours ever bear a hoof.)

akhfash:84-85.t: He said ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾, meaning: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾; and likewise ﴿وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:86-86.t: Some read ﴿وَالْيَسَع﴾ and some read ﴿وَاللَّيْسعَ﴾; we read it with the light [lām].

akhfash:90-90.t: And He said ﴿فَبِهُدَاهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ﴾. Everything from the verbs with final yāʾ or wāw, in the jussive position, is paused on with hāʾ, so that it is pronounced as it was.

akhfash:92-92.t: And He said ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ مُّصَدِّقُ ٱلَّذِي﴾ — nominative as a ṣifa (qualifier); it may be made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) for ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾.

akhfash:93-93.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَخْرِجُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾: we see that He means "they say ﴿أَخْرِجُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾" — and Allah knows best. In His saying ﴿بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ there was an indication of that, because He had informed [us] that they wanted something from them.

akhfash:96-96.t:
And He said ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أَصْبَحَ". Some read ﴿فالِقُ الأَصْباحِ﴾, the plural of "الصُّبْح" (morning).
And He said ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾, i.e. by reckoning; He dropped the bāʾ as He dropped it from His saying ﴿أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ﴾, i.e. He knows best about (بمن) the one who strays. "الحُسْبان" is the plural of "الحِساب", like "شِهاب" and "شُهْبَان"; and like it is "الشَمْسُ والقَمرُ بِحُسْبانٍ", i.e. by reckoning.

akhfash:98-98.t: And He said ﴿أَنْشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾: we see that He means: of them is one settled and of them is one deposited — and Allah knows best. And it is [also] read ﴿مُسْتَقَرّ﴾. [Translator's note: the gloss has «مُسْتَقِرٌّ» (with kasra) for the first reading; the text writes the second reading the same as the verse as quoted.]

akhfash:99-99.t:
And He said ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِراً﴾, meaning "الأَخْضَر" (green), as in the Arabs' saying "أرِنيِها نَمِرَةً أُرِكَها مَطِرَةً" (show me it [the cloud] spotted, and I will show it to you rainy).
And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾, then He said ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾, i.e. "and We brought forth by it gardens of grapes".
Then He said ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ﴾. The singular of "القِنْوان" is "قِنْوٌ" (date cluster), and likewise "الصِّنْوان", whose singular is "صِنْوٌ".

akhfash:100-100.t:
And He said ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾ as a badal (substitute), as He said ﴿إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ صِرَاطِ ٱللَّهِ ﴾. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundredth shāhid]:
ذَرِينِي إِنَّ أمرَكِ لَن يُطاعا * وَمَا ألفَيْتِني حِلْمِي مُضاعا
(Leave me, for your command will not be obeyed, and you have not found me — my forbearance — lost.)
And he said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and first shāhid]:
إِنِّي وَجَدْتُكَ يا جُرْثُومُ مِنْ نَفَرٍ * جُرْثُومَةِ اللُّؤْمِ لا جُرْثُومَةِ الكَرَمِ
(I have found you, O Jurthūm, to be of a clan whose root is baseness, not the root of nobility.)
[And another said] [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and fifty-fifth shāhid]:
إِنَّا وَجَدْنا بَنِي جِلاّنَ كُلَّهم * كساعِد الضُّبِّ لا طُولٌ ولا عِظَمُ*
(We found the Banū Jillān, all of them, like the forearm of a lizard — neither length nor bulk.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is the two hundred and second shāhid]:
ما لِلجِمالِ مَشْيِها وَئيدا * أَجَنْدَلاً لاَ يَحْمِلْنَ أَمْ حَدِيدا
(What is the matter with the camels, their walking so slowly? Is it stones they carry, or iron?)
And one also says "ما للجمالِ مشيُها وَئيدا" [with the nominative], as was said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and third shāhid]:
فكيفَ تَرَى عَطِيَّةَ حِينَ تَلْقَى * عِظاماً هامُهُنَّ قُرآسِيات
(So how do you see ʿAṭiyya when he meets great ones whose heads are massive?)

akhfash:105-105.t: And His saying ﴿وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾, i.e. you studied with the People of the Book; ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ﴾ means: thus. Some read ﴿دَرَسْتَ﴾, and that is how we read it, because it accords better with the Book. And some read ﴿دَرَسَتْ﴾. [Translator's note: the first reading was evidently «دَارَسْتَ», as the gloss shows; the text writes it as ﴿دَرَسْتَ﴾.]

akhfash:108-108.t: And He said ﴿فَيَسُبُّواْ ٱللَّهَ عَدُوّاً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾, heavy, doubled; and ﴿عَدْواً﴾ light, the origin being from "العُدْوان" (aggression). Some read ﴿عَدُوّاً﴾ without knowledge, i.e. they reviled Him in this state; but "العَدُوّ" is a collective, as He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ﴾ and as He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾. We read ﴿عَدْواً﴾ because it is more frequent in the reading and better in meaning, since you say "[عُدا] عَدْواً علينا" (he committed aggression against us), like "ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْباً" (he struck him a striking).

akhfash:109-109.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. Some read ﴿أَنَّها﴾, and that is how we read it, and it was explained as "لعلها" (perhaps it), as the Arabs say "اِذْهَبْ إِلى السوق أَنَّكَ تشتري لي شيئاً" (go to the market — perhaps you will buy me something), i.e. perhaps you. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and ninety-ninth shāhid]:
قُلْتُ لِشَيْبانَ اذْنُ من لِقائِهِ * أَنَّا نُغَذِّي القَوَمَ مِن شِوائِه
(I said to Shaybān: draw near to meet it — perhaps we will feed the people from its roast.)
in the sense of "لَعَلَّنا" (perhaps we).

akhfash:111-111.t: He said ﴿وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلاً﴾, i.e. group by group; "القُبُل" is the plural of "القَبيل" (group). One also says "قِبَلا", i.e. face to face. And He said ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلاً﴾, i.e. face to face. You say "لا قِبَلَ لي بهذا", i.e. I have no power [for this]*. And you say "لِي قِبَلَك حقٌ" (I have a claim on you), i.e. with you.

akhfash:113-113.t: [And] He said ﴿وَلِتَصْغَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: it is from "صَغَوْتُ", "يَصْغا" (to incline), like "مَحَوْتُ", "يُمْحا".

akhfash:119-119.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ أَلاَّ تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾, meaning — and Allah knows best — "what [reason] do you have for not eating?". Likewise ﴿وَمَا لَنَآ أَلاّ نُقَاتِلَ﴾ means: "what [reason] do we have for abandoning fighting?". If ﴿أَنْ﴾ were zāʾida (redundant), the verb would be nominative; and if it were in the sense of "what have we to do with such-and-such", it would be "وَمَالَنا وَأَلاّ نُقَاتِلَ".
And He said ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً لَّيُضِلُّونَ بِأَهْوَائِهِم﴾, and it is read ﴿ليُضِلُّونَ﴾. He made "أنَّ" fall on an indefinite noun because when speech is long it bears [this], and one part of it indicates another.

akhfash:123-123.t: And He said ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَابِرَ مُجَرِمِيهَا لِيَمْكُرُواْ فِيهَا﴾: He built it on [the pattern] "أَفاعِل", because it occurs in two ways: one says "هؤلاء الأكابر" and "الأكبرون". And He said ﴿نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالاً﴾, whose singular is "أَخْسَرُ", like "الأَكْبَر".

akhfash:137-137.t:
And He said ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾, because the partners made [it] seem fair.
Then He said ﴿لِيُرْدُوهُمْ﴾, from "أرْدى", "إِرْداءَ" (to destroy).

akhfash:138-138.t: And He said ﴿حِجْرٌ لاَّ يَطْعَمُهَآ﴾: "الحِجْر" is "the forbidden". It has also been read with ḍamma, ﴿حُجْرٌ﴾; and likewise ﴿حُجْراً مَحْجُورا﴾ has been read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and ﴿حِجْراً﴾, with one meaning. "الحِجْر" may also be intellect; Allah the Exalted said ﴿هَلْ فِي ذَلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ﴾, i.e. one possessed of intellect. Some said: "In His saying ﴿وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ﴾ there can only be kasra." This is nothing, because it means forbidden. As for "حجْرُ المرأة" (a woman's lap), it has fatḥa and kasra; and "حَجْرُ اليَمامة"* is with fatḥa; and "الحِجْرُ" is what you have enclosed, and it is [as in] the saying ﴿أصْحابِ الحجر﴾.

akhfash:139-139.t: And the saying of [Allah] the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾ — nominative, i.e.**: and if there is in their bellies a dead [foetus]. The nominative is permissible when you say ﴿يَكُن﴾ [with yāʾ], because the verb of a feminine may be made masculine. And ﴿خالِصَةٌ﴾ was made feminine to intensify the exclusiveness: as if, when He intensified the exclusiveness for them, it resembled abundance, so it was treated like "رَاوِية" (great transmitter) and "نَسّابة" (great genealogist).

akhfash:141-141.t: [And He said] ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ — genitive [in form], because the tāʾ of the [feminine] plural in the accusative position is genitive with tanwīn.

akhfash:142-142.t: Then He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾, i.e. and He produced of the livestock beasts of burden and small ones.

akhfash:143-143.t:
Then He said ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾, i.e. He produced beasts of burden and small ones, eight pairs, i.e. He produced eight pairs — as a badal (substitute), or as an explication (tibyān), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
Then He said: He produced ﴿مِنَ ٱلضَّأْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمَعْزِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾. He only said ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾ because each one is a "زَوْج" (mate). You say of two: "هذانِ زَوْجانِ" (these are two mates). Allah the Mighty and Majestic said ﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾. You say of a woman: "هي زَوْجٌ" and "هي زَوْجَةٌ" (she is a wife), and "هو زَوْجُها" (he is her husband). He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَها﴾, meaning the woman, and He said ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ﴾. Some say "الزَوْجَة". al-Akhṭal said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and twenty-seventh shāhid]:
زَوْجَةُ أَشْمَطَ مَرْهُوبٌ بَوادِرُهُ * قَدْ صار في رَأْسِهِ التَخْوِيصَ والنَزَعُ
(The wife of a grizzled man whose outbursts are feared, on whose head greyness and baldness have appeared.)
[Translator's note: the text has «السابع والشعرون», evidently for «السابع والعشرون» "twenty-seventh"; this and the next number are out of the sequence of this section.] One may also say of two: "هما زَوْجٌ" (they are a pair). [And "الزَوْجُ" is the patterned cloth thrown over the camel-litter.] Labīd said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and twenty-sixth shāhid]:
مِنْ كُلِّ محْفُوفٍ يُظِلُّ عِصِيَّهُ * زَوْجٌ عَلَيْهِ كِلَّةٌ وقِرامُها
(From every curtained litter whose poles are shaded by a cloth, with a canopy and its screen upon it.)
As for ﴿الضَأن﴾ (sheep), it has hamza, and it is a plural without a singular [of its own form]. One also says ﴿الضَئِين﴾, like "الشَعِير", and it is the plural of "الضَأْن"; the female is "ضائِنَة" and the plural "الضَوَائِن".
And ﴿المَعْزُ﴾ (goats) is a plural without a singular, and likewise "المِعْزَى". As for "المَواعِز", its singular is "الماعِز" and "الماعِزَة". The single male is "ضائِنْ", so "الضَأْن" is the plural of "الضائِنْ", like "صاحِب" and "صَحْب", "تاجِر" and "تَجْر"; and likewise "ماعِزْ" and "مَعْز". Some read ﴿ضأَنْ﴾ and ﴿مَعَز﴾, making it the plural of "الضَائِن" and "الماعِز", like "خَادِم" and "خَدَم"; and "حافِد" and "حَفَدَةْ" is like it, except that the hāʾ has been added to it.
As for His saying ﴿َآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ ٱلأُنثَيَيْنِ﴾, it is accusative by "حرّم" (He forbade).

akhfash:145-145.t: And He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقاً﴾, meaning: "unless it be carrion … or an abomination — for it is filth".

akhfash:146-146.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ﴾. The singular of "الحَوايا" (entrails) is "الحاوِياء" and "الحَاوِيَة". By His saying ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ﴾ He means — and Allah knows best — "and the cattle and sheep, We forbade to them"; but He put "مِنْ" in it. The Arabs say "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ حَديثٍ" meaning "there has been talk". And if you wish, you say "وَمِنْ الغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا الشُّحُومَ" (and of the sheep We forbade the fats), as you say "مِنَ الدّارِ أُخِذَ النِّصفُ والثُلُثُ" (of the house, half and a third were taken); so you attached [the pronoun by iḍāfa] in this sense, as you say "مِنَ الدّارِ أُخِذَ نِصْفُها" (of the house, its half was taken) and "مِنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ ضُرِبَ وَجْهُهُ" (of ʿAbdullāh, his face was struck).

akhfash:150-150.t: And He said ﴿هَلُمَّ شُهَدَآءَكُمُ﴾, because "هَلُمَّ" may be used for the singular, the dual and the plural.

akhfash:156-156.t: And He said ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا﴾ [depending] on ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ — out of dislike that ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا﴾.

akhfash:159-159.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً﴾, and some read ﴿فارَقُوا﴾, from "المُفارَقَة" (departing).

akhfash:160-160.t: And He said ﴿فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾ as a number, as you say "عَشْرُ سُودٍ" (ten black ones). If you ask how He said "عَشْر" [the form used with feminine nouns] when "المِثْل" is masculine: He only used the feminine because it is attached by iḍāfa to a feminine [pronoun], and in meaning too it is "حَسَنَةٌ" (a good deed) or "دَرَجةٌ" (a degree); if He used the feminine on that basis, it is a [valid] way. Some read ﴿عَشْرٌ أمْثالُها﴾, making "الأمثال" a qualifier of "العشر". This is the [proper] way, except that it is not read, because a number is not put in iḍāfa with what is a qualifier; rather one says "هُمْ عَشْرَةٌ قيامٌ" (they are ten, standing) and "عشرةٌ قُعُودٌ" (ten, sitting); one does not say "عشرةُ قيامٍ".

akhfash:161-161.t: And He said ﴿دِيناً قِيَماً﴾, i.e. upright; this is the reading of the generality. The people of Medina read ﴿قِيَما﴾, and it is good, though I have not heard it from the Arabs; it is in the meaning [as] explained. [Translator's note: both readings are written identically here; the reading of the generality was evidently «قَيِّماً».]

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ when you recite; ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً﴾ coverings, so that ﴿أَنْ﴾ [they do] not ﴿يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾ understand the Qur'an; ﴿وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا﴾ deafness, so they do not hear it with a hearing of acceptance. ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَا حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿هَذَا﴾ the Qur'an ﴿إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ﴾ lies ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ like jests and marvels; [أساطير is] the plural of أُسْطُورَة, with ḍamma.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ﴾ people ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ from following the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَيَنْأَوْنَ﴾ they keep far away ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ and do not believe in him. It is also said that it was revealed about Abū Ṭālib, who used to forbid [others] from harming him but did not believe in him. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿يُهْلِكُونَ﴾ by keeping away from him ﴿إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ because its harm falls upon them, ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿إِذْ وُقِفُوا﴾ [when] they are presented ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ فَقَالُوا يَا﴾ [yā here is] for drawing attention (tanbīh) ﴿لَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ﴾ to the world ﴿وَلَا نُكَذِّبُ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ with the two verbs in the nominative (marfūʿ) as a resumptive (istiʾnāf) statement; and with both in the accusative (manṣūb) [نُكَذِّبَ] [وَنَكُونَ] as the answer to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī); and with the first nominative and the second accusative. The answer (jawāb) of لَوْ [is omitted, its implied form being]: "you would have seen a tremendous thing."

celaleyn:28-28.t: The Exalted says: ﴿بَلْ﴾ for turning away (iḍrāb) from the wish for faith understood from the wishing; ﴿بَدَا﴾ has appeared ﴿لَهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ concealing by their saying {وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ}, through the testimony of their limbs, and so they wished that. ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّوا﴾ to the world, hypothetically, ﴿لَعَادُوا لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ of associating partners (shirk) ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ in their promise to believe.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ i.e. the deniers of the resurrection, ﴿إِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿هِيَ﴾ i.e. life ﴿إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ وُقِفُوا﴾ [when] they are presented ﴿عَلَى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ you would have seen a tremendous thing. ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them, on the tongue of the angels, by way of rebuke: ﴿أَلَيْسَ هَذَا﴾ resurrection and reckoning ﴿بِالْحَقِّ قَالُوا بَلَى وَرَبِّنَا﴾ it is indeed the truth. ﴿قَالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ in it in the world.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقَاءِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the resurrection, ﴿حَتَّى﴾ marking the end point (ghāya) of the denial ﴿إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمُ السَّاعَةُ﴾ the Resurrection ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly ﴿قَالُوا يَا حَسْرَتَنَا﴾ it is intense pain, and calling out to it is figurative (majāz), i.e. "this is your time, so come!" ﴿عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْنَا﴾ we fell short ﴿فِيهَا﴾ i.e. in the world. ﴿وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ in that, at the resurrection, they come to them in the ugliest form of anything and the foulest in smell, and ride upon them. ﴿أَلَا سَاءَ﴾ how evil is ﴿مَا يَزِرُونَ﴾ what they carry: that carrying of theirs.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ i.e. being occupied with it, ﴿إِلَّا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ﴾ whereas obedience and what helps toward it belong to the affairs of the Hereafter. ﴿وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ﴾ and in one reading [وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ], i.e. Paradise, ﴿خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ associating partners (shirk). ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْقِلُونَ], that, so that they would believe?

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿قَدْ﴾ for affirmation (taḥqīq) ﴿نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) ﴿لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ﴾ to you by way of denial; ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾ in secret, because they know that you are truthful — and in one reading with the lighter form [i.e. يُكْذِبُونَكَ], meaning they do not ascribe lying to you — ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ He put it in place of the pronoun, ﴿بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Qur'an ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ deny.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ in this there is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿فَصَبَرُوا عَلَى مَا كُذِّبُوا وَأُوذُوا حَتَّى أَتَاهُمْ نَصْرُنَا﴾ by the destruction of their peoples; so be patient until help comes to you by the destruction of your people. ﴿وَلَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ His promises. ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكَ مِنْ نَبَإِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ that by which your heart is calmed.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ كَبُرَ﴾ is grievous ﴿عَلَيْكَ إِعْرَاضُهُمْ﴾ from Islam, because of your eagerness for them, ﴿فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا﴾ a tunnel ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّمًا﴾ a means of ascent ﴿فِي السَّمَاءِ فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾ of what they demanded, then do so. The meaning is: you cannot do that, so be patient until Allah judges. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ their guidance ﴿لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْهُدَى﴾ but He did not will that, so they did not believe. ﴿فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾ of that.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَسْتَجِيبُ﴾ to your call to faith ﴿الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ with a hearing of understanding and taking heed. ﴿وَالْمَوْتَى﴾ i.e. the disbelievers; He likened them to them [the dead] in not hearing; ﴿يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ they are returned, and He requites them for their deeds.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ "why not" (hallā) ﴿نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ like the she-camel, the staff and the table spread. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَادِرٌ عَلَى أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ﴾ with shadda and without [يُنْزِلَ] ﴿آيَةً﴾ of what they demanded, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that its being sent down is a trial for them, since their destruction becomes binding if they deny it.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَمَا مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿دَابَّةٍ﴾ walking ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ﴾ in the air ﴿بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلَّا أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾ in the ordering of their creation, their provision and their states. ﴿مَا فَرَّطْنَا﴾ We have left out ﴿فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Preserved Tablet ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ so that We did not write it. ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ﴾ and He judges between them, and exacts retribution for the hornless [animal] from the horned one, then says to them: "Be dust!"

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the Qur'an ﴿صُمٌّ﴾ to hearing it with a hearing of acceptance ﴿وَبُكْمٌ﴾ from speaking the truth, ﴿فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ of disbelief. ﴿مَنْ يَشَإِ اللَّهُ﴾ to lead astray ﴿يُضْلِلْهُ وَمَنْ يَشَأْ﴾ to guide ﴿يَجْعَلْهُ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the religion of Islam.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muhammad, to the people of Mecca: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ﴾ tell me, ﴿إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ﴾ in the world ﴿أَوْ أَتَتْكُمُ السَّاعَةُ﴾ the Resurrection, which includes it, suddenly, ﴿أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ﴾ No! ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in [claiming] that the idols benefit you, then call on them.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿بَلْ إِيَّاهُ﴾ and none other than Him ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾ in hardships, ﴿فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ that He remove from you, of harm and the like, ﴿إِنْ شَاءَ﴾ its removal; ﴿وَتَنْسَوْنَ﴾ you abandon ﴿مَا تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him of the idols, and do not call on it.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى أُمَمٍ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿قَبْلِكَ﴾ messengers, and they denied them; ﴿فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِالْبَأْسَاءِ﴾ severe poverty ﴿وَالضَّرَّاءِ﴾ illness ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾ humble themselves and so believe.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ "why then not" (fa-hallā) ﴿إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا﴾ Our punishment ﴿تَضَرَّعُوا﴾ i.e. they did not do that, even though what called for it was present; ﴿وَلَكِنْ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ and did not soften for faith, ﴿وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of acts of disobedience, so they persisted in them.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا﴾ abandoned ﴿مَا ذُكِّرُوا﴾ were admonished and warned ﴿بِهِ﴾ of affliction and adversity, and did not take admonition, ﴿فَتَحْنَا﴾ with the lighter form and with shadda [فَتَّحْنَا] ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ of blessings, leading them on step by step (istidrāj), ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فَرِحُوا بِمَا أُوتُوا﴾ with the joy of insolence, ﴿أَخَذْنَاهُمْ﴾ with punishment ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly, ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾ despairing of all good.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ i.e. the last of them, in that they were uprooted. ﴿وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ for helping the messengers and destroying the disbelievers.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to the people of Mecca: ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ tell me, ﴿إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ﴾ made you deaf ﴿وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ﴾ made you blind ﴿وَخَتَمَ﴾ sealed ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ so that you know nothing, ﴿مَنْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾ with what He took from you, according to your claim? ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ the proofs of Our oneness; ﴿ثُمَّ هُمْ يَصْدِفُونَ﴾ they turn away from them and do not believe.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أَوْ جَهْرَةً﴾ by night or by day, ﴿هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ the disbelievers, i.e. none is destroyed but they.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَمَا نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ those who believe with Paradise ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ those who disbelieve with the Fire. ﴿فَمَنْ آمَنَ﴾ in them ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ his deeds, ﴿فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَمَسُّهُمُ الْعَذَابُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾ i.e. go out of obedience.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي خَزَائِنُ اللَّهِ﴾ from which provision is given, ﴿وَلَا﴾ [do I say] that I ﴿أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ﴾ what is hidden from me and has not been revealed to me, ﴿وَلَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ﴾ one of the angels. ﴿إِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَى﴾ the disbeliever ﴿وَالْبَصِيرُ﴾ the believer? No. ﴿أَفَلَا تَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ about that, and so believe?

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ﴾ warn ﴿بِهِ﴾ i.e. with the Qur'an ﴿الَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْ يُحْشَرُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيٌّ﴾ to help them ﴿وَلَا شَفِيعٌ﴾ to intercede for them. The negative clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of يُحْشَرُوا, and it is the object of the fear; those meant are the disobedient believers. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah, by desisting from what they are in and doing acts of obedience.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَلَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ﴾ by their worship ﴿وَجْهَهُ﴾ the Exalted's, not any of the goods of the world. They are the poor; the idolaters had disparaged them and asked that he drive them away so that they might sit with him, and the Prophet ﷺ wanted that, out of hope for their [the idolaters'] Islam. ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ if their inner state is not pleasing, ﴿وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ﴾ the answer to the negation (jawāb al-nafy); ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ if you do it.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ فَتَنَّا﴾ We tried ﴿بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. the noble by the lowly and the rich by the poor, by giving the latter precedence in coming first to faith, ﴿لِيَقُولُوا﴾ i.e. the nobles and the rich, disapprovingly: ﴿أَهَؤُلَاءِ﴾ the poor ﴿مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾ with guidance? i.e. if what they are upon were guidance, they would not have preceded us to it. The Exalted says: ﴿أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِالشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ to Him, so that He guides them? Yes indeed.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَإِذَا جَاءَكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِنَا فَقُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كَتَبَ﴾ has decreed ﴿رَبُّكُمْ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) — and in one reading with fatḥa [أَنَّهُ], as a badal (substitute) of الرَّحْمَةَ — ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنْكُمْ سُوءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ on his part, in that he committed it, ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ﴾ turned back ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ after his doing it ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ his deeds, ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿غَفُورٌ﴾ to him ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ toward him — and in one reading with fatḥa [فَأَنَّهُ], i.e. then forgiveness is his.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We have made clear what has been mentioned, ﴿نُفَصِّلُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ the Qur'an, so that the truth may appear and be acted upon, ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ﴾ and that may become manifest ﴿سَبِيلُ﴾ the path ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ and be avoided. In one reading [it is] with the lower-dotted letter [i.e. يَسْتَبِينَ], and in another with the upper-dotted letter and سَبِيلَ in the accusative, as an address to the Prophet ﷺ.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُلْ لَا أَتَّبِعُ أَهْوَاءَكُمْ﴾ in worshipping them; ﴿قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذًا﴾ if I followed them, ﴿وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ clear evidence ﴿مِنْ رَبِّي وَ﴾ [yet] ﴿كَذَّبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. my Lord, in that you associated partners. ﴿مَا عِنْدِي مَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ﴾ of the punishment. ﴿إِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿الْحُكْمُ﴾ in that and other matters ﴿إِلَّا لِلَّهِ يَقْضِي﴾ the judgement ﴿الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْفَاصِلِينَ﴾ the judges. In one reading [يَقُصُّ], i.e. He says.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدِي مَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ in that I would hasten it for you and be at rest; but it is with Allah. ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ [and] when He will punish them.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ its treasuries, or the ways that lead to knowledge of it; ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ and they are the five in His saying {إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ}… to the end of the ayah, as al-Bukhārī narrated. ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا﴾ happens ﴿فِي الْبَرِّ﴾ the deserts ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ﴾ the towns along the rivers. ﴿وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to وَرَقَةٍ, ﴿إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ it is the Preserved Tablet; and this exception is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of the exception before it.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ﴾ takes your souls at sleep ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُمْ﴾ you have earned ﴿بِالنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ﴾ i.e. in the day, by returning your souls, ﴿لِيُقْضَى أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى﴾ that is the term of life; ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ by the resurrection, ﴿ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and requites you for it.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ﴾ exalted ﴿فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُمْ حَفَظَةً﴾ angels who record your deeds, ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ﴾ — and in one reading [تَوَفَّاهُ] — ﴿رُسُلُنَا﴾ the angels charged with taking souls, ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ﴾ fall short in what they are commanded.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿ثُمَّ رُدُّوا﴾ i.e. the creation, ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ﴾ their Owner, ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ the Established, the Just, so that He may requite them. ﴿أَلَا لَهُ الْحُكْمُ﴾ the judgement that is executed upon them, ﴿وَهُوَ أَسْرَعُ الْحَاسِبِينَ﴾ He reckons with all creation in the measure of half a day of the days of the world, because of a hadith to that effect.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muhammad, to the people of Mecca: ﴿مَنْ يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِنْ ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ﴾ their terrors on your journeys, when ﴿تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعًا﴾ openly ﴿وَخُفْيَةً﴾ secretly, saying: ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ [its lām is] the lām of oath (qasam) ﴿أَنْجَيْتَنَا﴾ — and in one reading [أَنْجَانَا], i.e. Allah — ﴿مِنْ هَذِهِ﴾ darknesses and hardships, ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ the believers.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them: ﴿اللَّهُ يُنَجِّيكُمْ﴾ with the lighter form and with shadda ﴿مِنْهَا وَمِنْ كُلِّ كَرْبٍ﴾ distress other than it, ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ﴾ from the sky, like stones and the Cry, ﴿أَوْ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾ like being swallowed by the earth, ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ﴾ mix you up ﴿شِيَعًا﴾ into factions of differing inclinations, ﴿وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ﴾ through fighting. When it was revealed, he ﷺ said: "This is lighter and easier," and when what precedes it was revealed: "I seek refuge in Your Face." Al-Bukhārī narrated it. Muslim narrated the hadith: "I asked my Lord not to make the violence of my community among themselves, and He withheld it from me." And in a hadith: "When it was revealed he said: 'It will surely happen, though its interpretation has not yet come.'" ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ﴾ We make clear to them ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ the signs pointing to Our power, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ come to know that what they are upon is false.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ﴾ i.e. the Qur'an ﴿قَوْمُكَ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ﴾ the truth. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾ so as to requite you; I am only a warner, and your affair is with Allah. This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿لِكُلِّ نَبَإٍ﴾ piece of news ﴿مُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ a time in which it occurs and settles, and among it is your punishment. ﴿وَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ a threat to them.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا﴾ the Qur'an, with mockery, ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ and do not sit with them ﴿حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ وَإِمَّا﴾ in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated (idghām) into the added (mazīda) مَا; ﴿يُنْسِيَنَّكَ﴾ with sukūn on the nūn and the lighter form, and with fatḥa on it and shadda [يُنَسِّيَنَّكَ], ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ and you sit with them, ﴿فَلَا تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ الذِّكْرَى﴾ i.e. remembering, ﴿مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ in this the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun.

celaleyn:69-69.t: The Muslims said: "If we stand up every time they engage [in mockery], we will not be able to sit in the Mosque or to circumambulate." So there was revealed: ﴿وَمَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah ﴿مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ﴾ i.e. of those engaging [in it] ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ if they sit with them, ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ upon them is ﴿ذِكْرَى﴾ a reminder and admonition to them, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ engaging [in it].

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَذَرِ﴾ leave ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ﴾ which they were charged with ﴿لَعِبًا وَلَهْوًا﴾ by their mocking it, ﴿وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ and do not interfere with them — this was before the command to fight. ﴿وَذَكِّرْ﴾ admonish ﴿بِهِ﴾ people with the Qur'an, ﴿أَنْ﴾ lest ﴿تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ﴾ be handed over to destruction ﴿بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ did, ﴿لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيٌّ﴾ a helper ﴿وَلَا شَفِيعٌ﴾ to ward off punishment from it; ﴿وَإِنْ تَعْدِلْ كُلَّ عَدْلٍ﴾ offer every ransom, ﴿لَا يُؤْخَذْ مِنْهَا﴾ that with which it ransoms itself. ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُوا بِمَا كَسَبُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ water that has reached the utmost heat, ﴿وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ because of their disbelief.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قُلْ أَنَدْعُو﴾ shall we worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُنَا﴾ by worshipping it ﴿وَلَا يَضُرُّنَا﴾ by abandoning it — namely the idols — ﴿وَنُرَدُّ عَلَى أَعْقَابِنَا﴾ go back as idolaters ﴿بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ﴾ to Islam, ﴿كَالَّذِي اسْتَهْوَتْهُ﴾ led astray ﴿الشَّيَاطِينُ فِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ﴾ bewildered, not knowing where to go — a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ — ﴿لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ﴾ companions ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهُدَى﴾ i.e. to guide him to the road, saying to him: ﴿ائْتِنَا﴾ but he does not answer them, and so perishes. The interrogative is for disapproval (inkār), and the clause of comparison is a ḥāl of the pronoun of نُرَدُّ. ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ﴾ which is Islam ﴿هُوَ الْهُدَى﴾ and whatever is other than it is misguidance; ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ﴾ i.e. to submit ﴿لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ i.e. "and that" (bi-an) ﴿أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَاتَّقُوهُ﴾ the Exalted, ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ you will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ i.e. rightly. ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ﴾ to a thing ﴿كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection: He says to creation, "Rise!" and they rise. ﴿قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ﴾ the truth that will inevitably occur. ﴿وَلَهُ الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the horn — the second blowing, by Isrāfīl — in which no one besides Him has any dominion: {لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ}. ﴿عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ﴾ what is hidden and what is witnessed, ﴿وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His creation, ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ with the inward of things as with their outward.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾ it is his epithet (laqab), and his name is Tārakh: ﴿أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا آلِهَةً﴾ to worship? — an interrogative of rebuke (tawbīkh). ﴿إِنِّي أَرَاكَ وَقَوْمَكَ﴾ by taking them ﴿فِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ from the truth, ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ clear.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We showed him the going-astray of his father and his people, ﴿نُرِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ﴾ the dominion ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ so that he might infer from it Our oneness, ﴿وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ﴾ of it. The clause وَكَذَلِكَ and what follows it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ), and [what follows] is conjoined to قَالَ.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ﴾ grew dark ﴿عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأَى كَوْكَبًا﴾ it is said it was Venus; ﴿قَالَ﴾ to his people, who were star-gazers: ﴿هَذَا رَبِّي﴾ according to your claim. ﴿فَلَمَّا أَفَلَ﴾ set ﴿قَالَ لَا أُحِبُّ الْآفِلِينَ﴾ to take them as lords, because change and movement cannot apply to the Lord, since both belong to things that come into being (ḥawādith). But that had no effect on them.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْقَمَرَ بَازِغًا﴾ rising ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them: ﴿هَذَا رَبِّي فَلَمَّا أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنِي رَبِّي﴾ keep me firm on guidance, ﴿لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ an allusion (taʿrīḍ) to his people that they were in misguidance. But that had no effect on them.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بَازِغَةً قَالَ هَذَا﴾ he made it masculine because its khabar (predicate) is masculine, ﴿رَبِّي هَذَا أَكْبَرُ﴾ than the star and the moon. ﴿فَلَمَّا أَفَلَتْ﴾ and the argument against them grew strong but they did not turn back, ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Allah, of idols and of created bodies needing a creator. They said to him: "What do you worship?" He said:

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿إِنِّي وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ﴾ I have directed my worship ﴿لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ﴾ created ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ i.e. Allah, ﴿حَنِيفًا﴾ inclining to the upright religion, ﴿وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ with Him.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَحَاجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ﴾ disputed with him about his religion, and threatened him that the idols would strike him with harm if he abandoned them. ﴿قَالَ أَتُحَاجُّونِي﴾ with shadda on the nūn, and with the lighter form by dropping one of the two nūns — which is the nūn of the nominative (nūn al-rafʿ) according to the grammarians and the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) according to the Qur'an readers — i.e. do you dispute with me ﴿فِي﴾ the oneness of ﴿اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانِ﴾ the Exalted, to it? ﴿وَلَا أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [it] ﴿بِهِ﴾ of the idols, that they strike me with harm, since they have no power over anything, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئًا﴾ of misfortune to strike me, and then it will be. ﴿وَسِعَ رَبِّي كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ i.e. His knowledge encompasses everything. ﴿أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ this, and so believe?

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَا أَشْرَكْتُمْ﴾ with Allah, when it neither harms nor benefits, ﴿وَلَا تَخَافُونَ﴾ you, of Allah, ﴿أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ in worship ﴿مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ﴾ for worshipping it ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَانًا﴾ an argument and proof — and He is the One with power over all things? ﴿فَأَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَمْنِ﴾ we or you? ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ who is more entitled to it — i.e. it is we, so follow it.

celaleyn:82-82.t: The Exalted says: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوا﴾ mix ﴿إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ﴾ i.e. associating partners (shirk), as it is explained in the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs, ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ﴾ from punishment, ﴿وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَتِلْكَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and from it there is substituted (badal) ﴿حُجَّتُنَا﴾ which Ibrāhīm used as argument for the oneness of Allah: the setting of the star and what follows; and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿آتَيْنَاهَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ We guided him to it as an argument ﴿عَلَى قَوْمِهِ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ﴾ with the genitive construct (iḍāfa) and with tanwīn [دَرَجَاتٍ], in knowledge and wisdom. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ his [Isḥāq's] son; ﴿كُلًّا﴾ of the two ﴿هَدَيْنَا وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before Ibrāhīm; ﴿وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِ﴾ i.e. of Nūḥ, ﴿دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾ his son, ﴿وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ﴾ son of Yaʿqūb, ﴿وَمُوسَى وَهَارُونَ وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ as We rewarded them ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَى﴾ his son, ﴿وَعِيسَى﴾ son of Maryam — this shows that "offspring" (dhurriyya) includes the children of a daughter — ﴿وَإِلْيَاسَ﴾ son of the brother of Hārūn, the brother of Mūsā; ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of them ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ﴾ son of Ibrāhīm, ﴿وَالْيَسَعَ﴾ the lām is redundant (zāʾida), ﴿وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا﴾ son of Hārān, the brother of Ibrāhīm; ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ of them ﴿فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ with prophethood.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَمِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَإِخْوَانِهِمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كُلًّا or to نُوحًا; and مِنْ is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), because some of them had no child, and some of them had a disbeliever among their children. ﴿وَاجْتَبَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ We chose them ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the religion to which they were guided ﴿هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَلَوْ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ hypothetically, ﴿لَحَبِطَ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of "the Books", ﴿وَالْحُكْمَ﴾ wisdom, ﴿وَالنُّبُوَّةَ فَإِنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهَا﴾ i.e. these three, ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca, ﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا﴾ We have appointed for them ﴿قَوْمًا لَيْسُوا بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾ they are the Emigrants (Muhājirūn) and the Helpers (Anṣār).

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى﴾ them ﴿اللَّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ﴾ their way of affirming oneness (tawḥīd) and patience ﴿اقْتَدِهْ﴾ with the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt) both in pause and in continuous recitation, and in one reading it is dropped in continuous recitation. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to the people of Mecca: ﴿لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. the Qur'an ﴿أَجْرًا﴾ that you would give me; ﴿إِنْ هُوَ﴾ the Qur'an is not ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرَى﴾ an admonition ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans and jinn.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ i.e. they did not magnify Him as His greatness deserves, or did not know Him as He truly should be known, ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ, when they disputed with him about the Qur'an: ﴿مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى بَشَرٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿مَنْ أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ الَّذِي جَاءَ بِهِ مُوسَى نُورًا وَهُدًى لِلنَّاسِ يَجْعَلُونَهُ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَجْعَلُونَهُ] in the three places, ﴿قَرَاطِيسَ﴾ i.e. they write it in separate sheets, ﴿يُبْدُونَهَا﴾ [تُبْدُونَهَا] i.e. what they like to show of it, ﴿وَيُخْفُونَ كَثِيرًا﴾ [تُخْفُونَ] of what is in it, such as the description of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿وَعُلِّمْتُمْ﴾ O Jews, in the Qur'an, ﴿مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنْتُمْ وَلَا آبَاؤُكُمْ﴾ of the Torah, by the clarification of what was confused for you and what you differed about. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ﴾ sent it down — if they do not say it, there is no other answer. ﴿ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ﴾ their falsehood ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَهَذَا﴾ the Qur'an ﴿كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ before it of the Books, ﴿وَلِتُنْذِرَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [وَلِيُنْذِرَ]; conjoined to the meaning of what precedes it, i.e. We sent it down for blessing and confirmation and that you may warn with it ﴿أُمَّ الْقُرَى وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca and all other people. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَهُمْ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ﴾ out of fear of its [the Hereafter's] punishment.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ by claiming prophethood when he was not made a prophet, ﴿أَوْ قَالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ﴾ it was revealed about Musaylima; ﴿وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ they are the mockers, who said: "If we wished we could say the like of this." ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ those mentioned ﴿فِي غَمَرَاتِ﴾ the throes ﴿الْمَوْتِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَاسِطُوا أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ toward them, with beating and torment, saying to them harshly: ﴿أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ to us, that we may take them; ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ﴾ humiliation ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ﴾ by falsely claiming prophethood and revelation, ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهِ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ you were too proud to believe in them. The answer (jawāb) of لَوْ [is omitted, its implied form being]: "you would have seen a dreadful thing." And it will be said to them when they are resurrected:

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَى﴾ alone, without family, wealth or children, ﴿كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ i.e. barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, ﴿وَتَرَكْتُمْ مَا خَوَّلْنَاكُمْ﴾ what We gave you of wealth ﴿وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ﴾ in the world, against your choice. And it is said to them by way of rebuke: ﴿وَمَا نَرَى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعَاءَكُمُ﴾ the idols ﴿الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ﴾ i.e. in deserving your worship ﴿شُرَكَاءُ﴾ with Allah. ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ your bond, i.e. your union has been scattered; and in one reading with the accusative [بَيْنَكُمْ] as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. your bond between you. ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ has gone ﴿عَنْكُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ﴾ in the world about their intercession.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَالِقُ﴾ the Splitter ﴿الْحَبِّ﴾ to bring forth plants ﴿وَالنَّوَى﴾ to bring forth palm trees. ﴿يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ﴾ like the human being and the bird from the sperm-drop and the egg, ﴿وَمُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتِ﴾ the sperm-drop and the egg ﴿مِنَ الْحَيِّ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ the Splitter, the Bringer-forth, is ﴿اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ so how are you turned away from faith, when the proof is established?

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "the morning", i.e. the Splitter of the pillar of dawn, which is the first of the day's light that appears out of the darkness of the night. ﴿وَجَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ سَكَنًا﴾ in which creation rests from fatigue, ﴿وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ﴾ in the accusative, conjoined to the position (maḥall) of اللَّيْلِ, ﴿حُسْبَانًا﴾ a reckoning for times; or the bāʾ is omitted and it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of something implied, i.e. they run by a reckoning (bi-ḥusbān), as in the ayah of [Sūrat] al-Raḥmān. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned is ﴿تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿الْعَلِيمِ﴾ of His creation.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ النُّجُومَ لِتَهْتَدُوا بِهَا فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ﴾ on journeys. ﴿قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا﴾ We have made clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ the proofs of Our power ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ﴾ created you ﴿مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ that is Ādam; ﴿فَمُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ some of you in the womb ﴿وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ some of you in the loins; and in one reading with fatḥa on the qāf [فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ], i.e. a place of settling for you. ﴿قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ what is said to them.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا﴾ in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person, ﴿بِهِ﴾ with the water ﴿نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that grows, ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. from the plants, something ﴿خَضِرًا﴾ in the sense of "green" (akhḍar), ﴿نُخْرِجُ مِنْهُ﴾ from the green ﴿حَبًّا مُتَرَاكِبًا﴾ part of it lying upon part, like ears of wheat and the like; ﴿وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ﴾ a khabar (predicate), and from it there is substituted (badal) ﴿مِنْ طَلْعِهَا﴾ the first thing that comes out of it, and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is ﴿قِنْوَانٌ﴾ clusters ﴿دَانِيَةٌ﴾ close to one another; ﴿وَ﴾ We brought forth with it ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ gardens ﴿مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُشْتَبِهًا﴾ in their leaves — a ḥāl (circumstantial) — ﴿وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾ in their fruit. ﴿انْظُرُوا﴾ O you addressed, with a look of taking heed, ﴿إِلَى ثَمَرِهِ﴾ with fatḥa on the thāʾ and the mīm, and with ḍamma on both [ثُمُرِهِ]; it is the plural of ثَمَرَة, like شَجَرَة and شَجَر, and خَشَبَة and خَشَب; ﴿إِذَا أَثْمَرَ﴾ when it first appears, how it is, ﴿وَ﴾ to ﴿يَنْعِهِ﴾ its ripening when it matures, how it turns out. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكُمْ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ proofs of His power, the Exalted, over the resurrection and other things, ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ they are singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from them in faith, unlike the disbelievers.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ the second object (mafʿūl) ﴿شُرَكَاءَ﴾ the first object, and from it there is substituted (badal) ﴿الْجِنَّ﴾ in that they obeyed them in worshipping idols, ﴿وَ﴾ yet ﴿خَلَقَهُمْ﴾ He created them, so how can they be partners? ﴿وَخَرَقُوا﴾ with the lighter form and with shadda [وَخَرَّقُوا], i.e. they fabricated ﴿لَهُ بَنِينَ وَبَنَاتٍ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ when they said, "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah," and "the angels are the daughters of Allah." ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ a declaration of His transcendence (tanzīh), ﴿وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ by [claiming] that He has a child. He is

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ their Originator without any prior model. ﴿أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صَاحِبَةٌ﴾ a wife, ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ whose nature is to be created, ﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَاعْبُدُوهُ﴾ affirm His oneness; ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ Guardian.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ﴾ i.e. do not see Him; and this is restricted, given the believers' seeing Him in the Hereafter, because of His saying, Exalted is He: {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاضِرَةٌ إِلَى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ}, and the hadith of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim]: "You will see your Lord as you see the moon on the night it is full." It is also said that what is meant is: they do not encompass Him. ﴿وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ﴾ i.e. He sees them and they do not see Him; and it is not possible for anyone other than Him to perceive sight while not being perceived by it, or to encompass it in knowledge. ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ﴾ toward His friends, ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ of them. Say, O Muhammad, to them:

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَصَائِرُ﴾ proofs ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ﴾ them and so believed, ﴿فَلِنَفْسِهِ﴾ he has seen, because the reward of his seeing is his; ﴿وَمَنْ عَمِيَ﴾ to them and so went astray, ﴿فَعَلَيْهَا﴾ is the evil consequence of his leading astray [the correct reading is: "the evil consequence of his going astray"]. ﴿وَمَا أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ﴾ a watcher over your deeds; I am only a warner.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We have made clear what has been mentioned, ﴿نُصَرِّفُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ so that they may take heed, ﴿وَلِيَقُولُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, in the outcome of the matter: ﴿دَارَسْتَ﴾ you have studied with the People of the Book — and in one reading [دَرَسْتَ], i.e. [you have studied] the books of those of the past and brought this from them — ﴿وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿اتَّبِعْ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. the Qur'an; ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكُوا وَمَا جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا﴾ so as to requite them for their deeds, ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾ so as to compel them to faith. This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿وَلَا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ﴾ them ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the idols, ﴿فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْوًا﴾ in aggression and wrongdoing ﴿بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ i.e. out of their ignorance of Allah. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We made attractive to these what they are upon, ﴿زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ﴾ of good and evil, and they did it; ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and He will requite them for it.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ i.e. with the utmost of their effort in them, ﴿لَئِنْ جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ﴾ of what they demanded ﴿لَيُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهَا قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْآيَاتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ He sends them down as He wills, and I am only a warner. ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ﴾ what makes you know of their oaths [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source, أَيْمَانِهِمْ; the sense suggests إِيمَانِهِمْ, "their believing"] when it comes? i.e. you do not know that. ﴿إِنَّهَا إِذَا جَاءَتْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ because of what preceded in My knowledge. In one reading [it is] with tāʾ [لَا تُؤْمِنُونَ], as an address to the disbelievers; and in another with fatḥa on أنّ [أَنَّهَا], in the sense of لَعَلَّ ("perhaps"), or governed (maʿmūla) by what precedes it.

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ﴾ We turn their hearts away from the truth, so they do not understand it, ﴿وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾ from it, so they do not see it and do not believe, ﴿كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ﴾ i.e. in the signs that were sent down ﴿أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَنَذَرُهُمْ﴾ We leave them ﴿فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ﴾ their misguidance ﴿يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ wandering to and fro, bewildered.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ وَكَلَّمَهُمُ الْمَوْتَى﴾ as they demanded, ﴿وَحَشَرْنَا﴾ gathered ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا﴾ with two ḍammas, the plural of قَبِيل, i.e. group upon group; and with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ [قِبَلًا], i.e. face to face, and they testified to your truthfulness, ﴿مَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا﴾ because of what preceded in Allah's knowledge, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ their faith, and then they would believe. ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَجْهَلُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا﴾ just as We made these your enemies; and from it there is substituted (badal) ﴿شَيَاطِينَ﴾ the rebellious ones ﴿الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ يُوحِي﴾ whispering ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ its gilded falsehood ﴿غُرُورًا﴾ i.e. to delude them. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ﴾ i.e. the aforementioned inspiring; ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ leave the disbelievers ﴿وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ of disbelief and other things made attractive to them. This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَلِتَصْغَى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to غُرُورًا, i.e. that there may incline ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. to the gilding ﴿أَفْئِدَةُ﴾ the hearts of ﴿الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا﴾ earn ﴿مَا هُمْ مُقْتَرِفُونَ﴾ of sins, and be punished for it. And there was revealed, when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to appoint an arbiter between himself and them: Say:

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْتَغِي﴾ shall I seek ﴿حَكَمًا﴾ a judge between me and you, ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Qur'an ﴿مُفَصَّلًا﴾ in which truth is made clear from falsehood? ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah, like ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّلٌ﴾ with the lighter form and with shadda [مُنْزَلٌ] ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ those who doubt it; what is meant by that is to make the disbelievers acknowledge that it is the truth.

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ with rulings and promises ﴿صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification); ﴿لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾ by diminution or breach, ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of what is said, ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is done.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, ﴿يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion. ﴿إِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ﴾ in their disputing with you about carrion, when they said: "What Allah has killed is more deserving that you eat it than what you have killed." ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ i.e. "not" (mā) ﴿هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ﴾ lie in that.

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ i.e. knows ﴿مَنْ يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ and He will requite each of them.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. what was slaughtered in His name, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ بِآيَاتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ أَ﴾ n [i.e. أَنْ] ﴿لَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ of slaughtered animals, ﴿وَقَدْ فُصِّلَ﴾ in the passive and in the active in both verbs [فَصَّلَ حَرَّمَ] ﴿لَكُمْ مَا حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in the ayah {حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ}, ﴿إِلَّا مَا اضْطُرِرْتُمْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ of it, for that too is lawful for you. The meaning is: nothing prevents you from eating what has been mentioned, when He has made clear to you what is forbidden to eat, and this is not among it. ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا لَيُضِلُّونَ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma on it [لَيَضِلُّونَ] ﴿بِأَهْوَائِهِمْ﴾ by what their souls desire, of declaring carrion lawful and other things, ﴿بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ that they rely on in that. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾ those who transgress from the lawful to the forbidden.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿وَذَرُوا﴾ leave ﴿ظَاهِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾ its open and its secret [forms]. As for الْإِثْم, it is said: fornication; and it is said: every act of disobedience. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْسِبُونَ الْإِثْمَ سَيُجْزَوْنَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَقْتَرِفُونَ﴾ earn.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ in that it died [by itself] or was slaughtered in the name of other than Him. Otherwise, what a Muslim slaughters without pronouncing the name [of Allah] over it, deliberately or out of forgetfulness, is lawful; Ibn ʿAbbās said this, and al-Shāfiʿī holds it. ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. eating from it ﴿لَفِسْقٌ﴾ a going out from what is lawful. ﴿وَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ﴾ whisper ﴿إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ﴾ the disbelievers, ﴿لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ﴾ about making carrion lawful; ﴿وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ in it, ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ﴾ And it was revealed concerning Abū Jahl and others:

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿أَوَ مَنْ كَانَ مَيْتًا﴾ through disbelief ﴿فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ﴾ through guidance ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ﴾ by which he discerns the truth from other than it, and it is faith, ﴿كَمَنْ مَثَلُهُ﴾ مَثَل is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. like one who is ﴿فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِنْهَا﴾ and that is the disbeliever? No. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as faith was made attractive to the believers, ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of disbelief and acts of disobedience.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We made the wicked of Mecca its great ones, ﴿جَعَلْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَابِرَ مُجْرِمِيهَا لِيَمْكُرُوا فِيهَا﴾ by barring from faith; ﴿وَمَا يَمْكُرُونَ إِلَّا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ because its evil consequence falls upon them, ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَإِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca, ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ for the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿قَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ﴾ in him ﴿حَتَّى نُؤْتَى مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيَ رُسُلُ اللَّهِ﴾ of the message and revelation to us, because we are greater in wealth and older in age. The Exalted says: ﴿اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَاتِهِ﴾ in the plural and the singular [رِسَالَتَهُ]; and حَيْثُ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of a verb indicated by أَعْلَمُ, i.e. He knows the place fit for putting it in, and He puts it there, and these are not worthy of it. ﴿سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا﴾ by that saying of theirs ﴿صَغَارٌ﴾ abasement ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ i.e. because of their scheming.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ﴾ by casting a light into his heart, so that it expands for it and accepts it, as has come in a hadith; ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدْ﴾ Allah ﴿أَنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا﴾ with the lighter form and with shadda [ضَيْقًا], [too narrow] to accept it, ﴿حَرِجًا﴾ extremely narrow — with kasra on the rāʾ it is an adjective (ṣifa), and with fatḥa on it [حَرَجًا] it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description for intensification (mubālagha) — ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ﴾ and in one reading [يَصَّاعَدُ]; in both there is assimilation (idghām) of the originally present tāʾ into the ṣād, and in another [reading it is] with sukūn on it [i.e. يَصْعَدُ], ﴿فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾ when he is charged with faith, because of how hard it is for him. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ [like] this making, ﴿يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ الرِّجْسَ﴾ the punishment, or Satan, i.e. He gives it power ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَهَذَا﴾ which you are upon, O Muhammad, ﴿صِرَاطُ﴾ the path of ﴿رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ with no crookedness in it; its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) that emphasizes the sentence (ḥāl muʾakkida), and what governs it (al-ʿāmil) is the meaning of pointing [in the demonstrative]. ﴿قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا﴾ We have made clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ in it the originally present tāʾ is assimilated (idghām) into the dhāl, i.e. who take admonition; they are singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿لَهُمْ دَارُ السَّلَامِ﴾ i.e. of safety, and it is Paradise, ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ [يَحْشُرُهُمْ], i.e. Allah [gathers] creation ﴿جَمِيعًا﴾ and it is said to them: ﴿يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ﴾ by your leading astray; ﴿وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمْ﴾ who obeyed them ﴿مِنَ الْإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ﴾ humans benefited from the jinn making appetites attractive to them, and the jinn from humans obeying them; ﴿وَبَلَغْنَا أَجَلَنَا الَّذِي أَجَّلْتَ لَنَا﴾ and that is the Day of Resurrection — this is an expression of regret on their part. ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to them, on the tongue of the angels: ﴿النَّارُ مَثْوَاكُمْ﴾ your abode, ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ of the times in which they go out to drink the boiling water, for it is outside it, as the Exalted said: {ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لَإِلَى الْجَحِيمِ}. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: that it concerns those whom Allah knew would believe, so مَا is in the sense of مَنْ. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We let the disobedient among humans and jinn enjoy one another, ﴿نُوَلِّي﴾ from wilāya (authority) ﴿بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضًا﴾ i.e. over some, ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ of acts of disobedience.

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. from your totality, i.e. some of you, which applies to humans; or the messengers of the jinn are their warners, who listen to the speech of the messengers and convey it to their people, ﴿يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا قَالُوا شَهِدْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا﴾ that it has indeed been conveyed to us. The Exalted says: ﴿وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ so they did not believe, ﴿وَشَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the sending of messengers, ﴿أَنْ﴾ the lām is implied (muqaddara), and it [أَنْ] is lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. "because He" ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ الْقُرَى بِظُلْمٍ﴾ on their part ﴿وَأَهْلُهَا غَافِلُونَ﴾ no messenger having been sent to them to make things clear to them.

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ of those who act ﴿دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ recompense ﴿مِمَّا عَمِلُوا﴾ of good and evil. ﴿وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ].

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ free of need of His creation and their worship, ﴿ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca, by destruction, ﴿وَيَسْتَخْلِفْ مِنْ بَعْدِكُمْ مَا يَشَاءُ﴾ of creation, ﴿كَمَا أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾ whom He took away; but He has kept you, out of mercy for you.

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ of the Hour and the punishment ﴿لَآتٍ﴾ inevitably, ﴿وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾ escaping Our punishment.

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿يَا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلَى مَكَانَتِكُمْ﴾ your state; ﴿إِنِّي عَامِلٌ﴾ according to my state. ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ﴾ a relative noun (mawṣūla), the object of knowing, ﴿تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ﴾ i.e. the praiseworthy outcome in the abode of the Hereafter — we or you? ﴿إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ﴾ will not prosper ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ the disbelievers.
