These two parenthetical clauses occurred among the enumerated items to stress the falsity of their sayings. نَبِّئُونِي is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; بِعِلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نَبِّئُونِي; إِنْ is conditional; كان and its noun, which is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and صادِقِينَ is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it.
(وَمِنَ الْإِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ) The i'rab of its parallel has been given exactly.
(أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهذا) أَمْ is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), estimated as «بل» and the hamza, the estimate being: "rather, were you witnesses?". إِذْ is an adverb attached to شُهَداءَ, and the clause وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ is in the position of a genitive by annexation; بِهذا is attached to وَصَّاكُمُ.
(فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The fāʾ is the eloquent one (faṣīḥa), i.e. "when you have known this and it has taken root in your minds"; مَنْ is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ and أَظْلَمُ is the khabar, and the clause has no position; the interrogation has the sense of negation, i.e. "no one is more wrongful". مِمَّنِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أَظْلَمُ; the clause افْتَرى has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; عَلَى اللَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افْتَرى; كَذِباً is a direct object or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and the i'rab of its parallel has preceded. The lām is for justification; يُضِلَّ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām of justification; النَّاسَ is a direct object; the lām of justification and what follows it are attached to افْتَرى; بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of افْتَرى, i.e. he fabricated against Him the Exalted.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) إِنَّ and its noun; the clause لا يَهْدِي is its khabar; الْقَوْمَ is a direct object and الظَّالِمِينَ a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْمَ; and the nominal clause is a justification with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
Idghām (assimilation): It is the entering of one letter into another letter of its kind, such that the two become a single doubled letter. It has three states:

1- Obligatory assimilation:
That is when the two are homogeneous in a single word. As for the words of the poet:
الحمد لله العليّ الأجلل ... الواسع الفضل الوهوب المجزل
(Praise be to Allah, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Vast in bounty, the Bestower, the Generous.)
it is among the poetic necessities. Assimilation of two identical adjoining letters, the first of which has a vowel, is obligatory when they are in two words, as when they are in one word, such as: سكتّ, سكّنا, عنّي and عليّ, and اكتب بالقلم, and استغفر ربك, and like the verse we are dealing with, «أمّا اشتملت عليه». Some words are irregular and not to be taken as a model, such as: ألل السّقاء والأسنان (when their smell changes and spoils), دبب الإنسان (when hair grows on his forehead), ضببت الأرض (when its lizards become many), قطط الشعر (when it is short and curly; and one says قطّ with assimilation), لححت العين (when its eyelids stick together with rheum), and الخخت (when its tears are many and its eyelids thick).

2- Permissibility of assimilation and of leaving it:
This occurs in four places:
(a) That the first letter of the two identical ones is vowelled and the second is quiescent with an incidental sukūn, for the jussive or for the construction (binā') in the singular imperative; so you say: لم يمدّ and مدّ with assimilation, and لم يمدد and امدد; and the unassimilated is better, and the Qurʾān speaks with it. The Exalted said: «يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار». And He said: «واشدد على قلوبهم». The vowel of the second of the two assimilated letters in the jussive imperfect and the imperative, to which nothing has been attached, follows the vowel of its first letter, and this is the more frequent; and we hold that it should be vowelled with fatḥa for lightness.
(b) That the ʿayn of the word and its lām are two yāʾs, the second of which necessarily takes a vowel, such as: عيي and حيي. So you say: عيّ and حيّ; and if the vowel of the second is incidental, for the sake of case-ending, such as لن يحيي, its assimilation is prevented.
(c) That at the beginning of the past verb there are two tāʾs, such as: تتابع and تتبّع; assimilation is then permitted with the addition of a hamzat waṣl at its beginning, to avert beginning with a quiescent letter, such as: اتّابع and اتّبع. If it is imperfect, assimilation is not permitted, but lightening it is permitted by dropping one of the two tāʾs, so you say for تتلظّى: تلظّى, and for تتجلّى: تجلّى. The Exalted said: «تنزّل الملائكة والرّوح», and He said: «نارا تلظّى»; and Abū Tammām said, describing spring:
أضحت تصوغ بطونها لظهورها ... نورا تكاد له القلوب تنوّر
(They (the clouds/the plants) have come to fashion, from their insides for their backs, a light at which hearts almost become illumined.)
(d) That two identical vowelled letters adjoin in two words, such as: جعل لي, and كتب بالقلم. Assimilation is then permitted by making the first identical letter quiescent, so you say: جعل لي and كتب بالقلم «[Translator's note: the source prints these two examples exactly as in the previous sentence, without showing the assimilated pronunciation; they are given as written. The word printed "تقل" is evidently "تقول", "you say".]», except that assimilation is permitted here in pronunciation and not in writing.

3- Prevention of assimilation:
That is in seven places:
(a) That the two identical letters stand at the beginning, like ددن, i.e. play.
(b) That they are in a noun on the pattern فُعَل (ḍamma then fatḥa) like دُرَر, or فُعُل (two ḍammas) like سُرُر, or فِعَل (kasra then fatḥa) like لِمَم, or فَعَل (two fatḥas) like طَلَل.
(c) That the two identical letters are in a pattern augmented for linking (ilḥāq), like جلبب and هيلل.
(d) That something already assimilated is attached to the beginning of the two identical letters, like هلّل. That is because the second assimilation would be like a repetition of assimilation, which is prohibited.
(e) That the two identical letters are on the pattern «افْعِلْ» in the exclamation of wonder, as in: أحبب بالعلم.
«[Translator's note: the source gives no letter "و" for the next item; it is translated as it appears, unlettered.]» And that the sukūn of one of the two identical letters occurs incidentally, because of its attachment to a vowelled nominative pronoun, like مددت.
(ز) That it is among what the Arabs irregularly left unassimilated by choice, and these are memorised words, mentioned at the beginning of the discussion.

dervis-irab:151-151.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تعال): one of the specific usages that became general; originally it was said by one who was in a high place to one below him, then it became frequent and widened until it became general. It is an imperative verb that always has a fatḥa at its end, and for this reason they accused Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī of a grammatical error in his saying:
أيا جارتا ما أنصف الدهر بيننا ... تعالي أقاسمك الهموم تعالي
(O my neighbour, Time has not been fair between us; come, let me share my sorrows with you, come.)

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: تَعالَوْا أَتْلُ ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ): a new sentence, uttered to command him ﷺ to recite to them what their Lord has forbidden them, as a reality and not a conjecture, as certainty and not guesswork. The clause تعالوا is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying; it is an imperative verb indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; أتل is an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the answer to a request, though Ibn Hishām prefers to say that it is the answer of an implied condition; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object; the clause حرم عليكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e.
"that which He has forbidden". It is also permissible that "ما" be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "recite the forbidding of your Lord"; but a prohibition is not recited; rather it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the direct object.
ربكم is the agent of حرم; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرم or to أتل, on the basis that the matter belongs to the chapter of conflict (tanāzuʿ). (أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً): there are many views on "أن", of which two are preferred. The first is that it is explicative, because what has the meaning of saying, without its letters, precedes it; لا is prohibitive; تشركوا is an imperfect verb jussive by it, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. The second view is that it is a maṣdar particle, and it and what is within its scope are a badal of «ما حرم»; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشركوا; شيئا is a direct object, or in the sense of a maṣdar, in which case it is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); and a like of it has been indicated before. بالوالدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the verb of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "show kindness to the parents"; and إحسانا is an absolute object of the omitted verb. An important discussion by Ibn Hishām on the i'rab of this verse will come in the section on Benefits. (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; أولادكم is a direct object; من إملاق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقتلوا, i.e. "for the sake of poverty", so من is causal (sababiyya); the object of purpose was not put in the accusative because its condition fails, since الإملاق is a maṣdar that is not of the heart; further discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and the clause نرزقكم is the khabar; the clause نحن نرزقكم is resumptive, giving the reason for the prohibition before it; إياهم is conjoined to the pronoun in نرزقكم; and He put those addressed before the pronoun of the children, the reverse of the verse in al-Isrāʾ, for a rhetorical secret that will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها وَما بَطَنَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقربوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the wāw is the agent; الفواحش is a direct object; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a badal of الفواحش, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl); the clause ظهر has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظهر; and ما بطن is conjoined to ما ظهر. (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): conjoined to what precedes and included within its scope, to complete the list of prohibitions, which are ten things.
لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; النفس is a direct object; التي is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as an adjective; the clause حرم الله has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the exception is an emptied one from the most general of circumstances, i.e. "do not kill it in any circumstance except the circumstance of your being linked with the truth", so the باء is the باء of accompaniment, and it with its genitive noun is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the wāw in «تقتلوا». It is also permissible that the emptied exception be from the verb itself, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are an absolute object, i.e. "except the killing that is linked with the truth", such as retaliation (qawad), the ḥadd for apostasy, and the stoning of a muḥṣan. (ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive, uttered to point to what precedes; the clause وصاكم is the khabar of ذلكم; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وصاكم; and لعلكم تعقلون is لعل with its noun and khabar; the clause of hope is a ḥāl clause, i.e. "that you may use your intellects, which restrain your selves and hold them back from committing these prohibited things".

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains marvellous varieties of rhetoric that require length, but it is a length that does not weary, for talk of beauty is long, and the longer it is, the more it improves, like beauty itself: the more you look closely at it, the more the marks of its loveliness increase:
يزيدك وجهه حسنا ... إذا ما زدته نظرا
(His face increases you in beauty whenever you increase your gazing.)

1- Tawhīm (creating a false impression):
The first art in this verse is the art of tawhīm, which was indicated in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and we renew our acquaintance with it here and say: it is that the speaker brings a word such that what follows it of speech gives the impression that the speaker intended a corruption of it (taṣḥīf), whereas he intends something else; and that is in His saying: «أن لا تشركوا به شيئا».
For the apparent speech indicates the prohibition of the negation of polytheism, and its entailment is the permitting of polytheism, which is impossible and contrary to the intended meaning. The interpretation that resolves the difficulty is that, among the commands mentioned in the context of the verse and what follows, there are things forbidden to them and things they are commanded to do. Polytheism towards Allah, the killing of the inviolable soul, and the consuming of the orphan's property are among what is forbidden outwardly and inwardly, while giving full measure and weight with equity, justice in speech let alone in deed, fulfilling the covenant, and following the straight path are among the deeds commanded with an obligatory command. Were the speech to come without «لا», it would be cut off, disordered and corrupted in meaning, for the meaning would become: "He has forbidden you polytheism and kindness to parents", which is the opposite of the intended meaning. For this reason the addition came, whose outward appearance gave the impression of corruption of meaning, so that one would resort to the interpretation by which the conjoining of the remaining commands to what precedes is made sound.

2- Taghāyur (variation):
The second art in it is taghāyur, and that is in His saying: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق». Its definition is the variation of two approaches, whether in a single meaning, such that a person praises a thing or blames it, or blames what another has praised, and the reverse, and prefers one thing over another, then returns and makes the less-preferred one the preferred. Among the forms of taghāyur is the variation of meaning through the variation of wording, as in His saying: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم», which differs from His saying on this very same subject in (Sūrat) Banī Isrāʾīl: «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم». In the verse of al-Anʿām He put (the parents) first because it is addressed to the poor, as His saying «من إملاق» shows; so rhetoric required that the promise to them, I mean the impoverished fathers, of provision that would enrich them come first, and rhetoric required completing the meaning with a promise for the sons after the promise for the fathers, so that the souls might be completely at rest. In Banī Isrāʾīl the address is to the rich, as His saying «خشية إملاق» shows, for none fears poverty but the rich, while the poor man's poverty is already present. So rhetoric required putting first the promise of provision to the sons, so that this precedence might point to the fact that He, glory be to Him, is the One who provides for the sons, in order to remove what the rich imagined, that by spending on the sons they would come to poverty after wealth; then this reassurance was completed by their promise of provision after the promise for their sons. Glory be to the One who spoke this speech!

Taghāyur in Arabic poetry:
The poets have excelled in this meaning, played with it and taken every path with it, and we shall present to you below a selection of what has been completed by taghāyur, where poets praised what is commonly blamed and blamed what deserves praise. The first to allude to this was ʿAntara ibn Shaddād, the ʿAbsī poet and the famous horseman, when he desired to kiss swords because they gleamed like the flash of the mouth of the one who loves them, and he said his two famous verses:
ولقد ذكرتك والرماح نواهل ... منّي وبيض الهند تقطر من دمي
(I remembered you while the spears were drinking from me and the white swords of India were dripping with my blood,)
فوددت تقبيل السيوف لأنها ... لمعت كبارق ثغرك المتبسّم
(and I longed to kiss the swords because they gleamed like the flash of your smiling mouth.)
How lovely is the saying of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī, who took another path and said:
مسيء محسن طورا وطورا ... فما أدري عدّوي أم حبيبي
(At one time wrongdoer and at another benefactor; I do not know whether he is my enemy or my beloved.)
يقلّب مقلة ويدير طرفا ... به عرف البريء من المريب
(He turns an eye and rolls a glance by which the innocent is known from the suspect.)
وبعض الظالمين وإن تناهى ... شهيّ الظلم مغتفر الذنوب
(And some wrongdoers, even if they go to extremes, are pleasing in their wrong and their sins are forgiven.)
Al-Buḥturī was fond of this art, and said:
عيّرتني بالشيب من بدآته ... في عذاري بالهجر والاجتناب
(She reproached me for grey hair, from its beginnings at my cheek, with shunning and avoidance.)
لا تريه عارا فما هو بالشيب ولكنه جلاء الشباب
(Do not see it as a disgrace; it is not grey hair, but rather the brightening of youth.) [Translator's note: the source prints this verse as a single run without the hemistich separator]
وبياض البازيّ أصدق حسنا ... إن تأمّلت من سواد الغراب
(And the whiteness of the falcon is truer in beauty, if you ponder, than the blackness of the raven.)
And he said on the same meaning, and did well:
عذلتنا في عشقها أمّ عمرو ... هل سمعتم بالعاذل المعشوق؟
(Umm ʿAmr blamed us for loving her; have you ever heard of a blamer who is beloved?)
ورأت لمّة ألمّ بها الشّيب فريعت من ظلمة في شروق
(She saw a lock of hair that grey had touched, and was alarmed at a darkness amid a dawn.)
ولعمري لولا الأقاحي لأبصر ... ت أنيق الرياض غير أنيق
(By my life, were it not for the white camomile flowers, you would see the lovely meadows as not lovely.)
ومزاج الصهباء بالماء أولى ... بصبوح مستحسن وغبوق
(And mixing the red wine with water is better suited to a morning or evening draught that is deemed good.)
وسواد العيون لو لم يكمّل ... ببياض ما كان بالموموق
(And the blackness of the eyes, were it not completed by whiteness, would not be admired.)
أيّ ليل يبهى بغير نجوم؟ ... وسماء تندى بغير بروق؟
(What night is splendid without stars? And what sky is moist without lightning?)
Al-Buḥturī described the day of parting as short, though people have agreed on its length, where he said:
ولقد تأمّلت الفراق فلم أجد ... يوم الفراق على امرئ بطويل
(I have pondered parting and found the day of parting not long for anyone.)
قصرت مسافته على متزوّر ... منه لدهر هن صبابة وغليل
(Its span is short for one who visits from it, for a time of longing and thirst.) [Translator's note: the second verse is textually obscure in the source]
As for Ibn al-Rūmī, he rose above the earlier and later poets in blaming what people have agreed to praise, and said, satirising the full moon:
لو أراد الأديب أن يهجو البد ... ر رماه بالخطة الشنعاء
(If the man of letters wished to satirise the full moon, he would pelt it with the ugly charge.)
قال: يا بدر أنت تغدر بالسا ... ري وتغري بزائر الحسناء
(He would say: O full moon, you betray the night traveller and expose the visitor of the beauty.)
يعتريك المحاق في كل شهر ... فترى كالقلامة الحجناء
(The waning befalls you every month, and you appear like a curved nail-paring.)
نمش في بياض وجهك يحكي ... كلفا فوق وجنة برصاء
(Freckles in the whiteness of your face resemble blotches on the cheek of a leper.)
لا لأجل المديح بل خيفة الهجر أخذنا جوائز الخلفاء
(Not for the sake of praise but for fear of abandonment have we taken the caliphs' rewards.) [Translator's note: this line, appended in the source without a hemistich separator, appears to be a separate fragment]
And al-Sharīf al-Raḍī satirised the sun, saying:
في خلقة الشمس وأخلاقها ... شتى عيوب ستة تذكر
(In the sun's creation and character are various faults, six of which may be mentioned.)
رمداء عمشاء إذا أصبحت ... عمياء عند الليل لا تبصر
(She is bleary and dim-eyed by morning, and blind at night, unable to see.)
ويغتدي البدر لها كاسفا ... وجرمه من جرمها أصغر
(The full moon becomes dimmed beside her, though its body is smaller than hers.)
حرورها في القيظ لا يتّقى ... ودفؤها في القر مستحقر
(Her scorching heat in summer cannot be warded off, and her warmth in the cold is despised.)
وخلقها خلق الملول الذي ... ينكث للعهد ولا يبصر
(Her nature is the nature of the weary one who breaks the covenant and does not see.)
ليست بحسناء وما حسن من ... يحسر منه الطرف إذ ينظر
(She is not beautiful, and what beauty is it from which the eye recoils when it looks?)
Were we to expand, we would fill the whole book with this delightful, unique poetry, but it suffices us of the necklace to take what encircles the neck.

3- Al-majāz al-mursal (the unrestricted figurative use):
In His saying, the Exalted: «من إملاق», which runs the course of a metonymy (kināya), because when his wealth leaves his hand poverty rides him, so the word of the cause is used in the place of the effect. It is said in Asās al-Balāgha: "Among the figurative usages: أملق الدهر ماله, 'Time took his wealth away and removed it from his hand'; and أملق الرجل means 'the man spent his wealth until he became poor', and he is a مملق. A Bedouin said: 'May Allah fight women, how they draw out excuses, as if they came out from beneath their feet', i.e. they extract them."

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām has a lengthy discussion of this verse. He said: "As for His saying, the Exalted:
«قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم أن لا تشركوا به شيئا», it was said that لا is negative, it was said prohibitive, and it was said redundant, and all are possible. The sum of the matter in the verse is that «ما» is declarative, in the sense of "that which", in the accusative by «أتل», and «حرم ربكم» is the ṣila, and «عليكم» is attached to حرم. This is the apparent view. Al-Zajjāj allowed «ما» to be interrogative, in the accusative by حرم, with the clause quoted by «أتل», because it has the sense of "I say"; and it is permissible that «عليكم» be attached to «أتل», and whoever prefers giving effect to the first of the two conflicting words, namely the Kufans, prefers it over its being attached to حرّم. Concerning «أن» and what follows it there are several views: first, that the two are in the position of the accusative as a badal of «ما», on the basis that it is relative and not interrogative, since the badal is not accompanied by the interrogative hamza. Second, that the two are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted «هو»; some of the grammarians allowed these two. On these two, «لا» is redundant; Ibn al-Shajarī said: the correct view is that it is negative on the first and redundant on the second.
Third, that the original is: 'He made that clear to you so that you not associate partners (with Him)'; this is because when their leaders forbid them what Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted, has made lawful, and they obey them, they commit polytheism, because they have set up other than Allah in His position. Fourth, that the original is: 'I enjoin you not to associate partners', by the proof that «وبالوالدين إحسانا» means 'and I enjoin you regarding the parents', and that at the end of the verse is «ذلكم وصّاكم به'; on these two views the clause and the preposition are omitted. Fifth, that the implied form is: «أتل عليكم أن لا تشركوا», indicated by what precedes. Al-Zajjāj allowed these three views. Sixth, that the speech is complete at «حرم ربكم», then begins «عليكم أن لا تشركوا وأن تحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا وأن لا تقتلوا ولا تقربوا»; in that case «عليكم» is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning 'hold fast to'. «أن» in the six views is a maṣdar particle, and «لا» in the last four views is negative. Seventh, that «أن» is explicative, with the meaning of 'أي', and «لا» is prohibitive, and the verb is jussive, not accusative, as if it had been said: 'I say to you: do not associate anything with Him, and show kindness to the parents.' These two views were allowed by Ibn al-Shajarī." Ibn Hishām also said in another place in al-Mughnī:
"As for the saying of some of them regarding «قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم عليكم ربكم أن لا تشركوا به شيئا» that the pause is before «عليكم», and that «عليكم» is an incitement (ighrāʾ), it is good, and it escapes an apparent difficulty in the verse that requires interpretation."
We have lengthened the quotation only because much has been said about the verse. So reflect, and Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:123-124.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَغارٌ): al-ṣaghār (with fatḥa on the ṣād) is abasement and humiliation. One says ṣaghira (like karuma), ṣaghran (with kasra on the ṣād and fatḥa on the ghayn), and ṣaghran (with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the ghayn), and ṣaghār (with fatḥa on the ṣād and the ghayn), and ṣaghāra and ṣughrān (with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the ghayn). As for ṣaghura (with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the ghayn, and likewise ṣaghira with kasra on the ghayn), it is the opposite of "to be big" and "to be great". [Translator's note: the vowel marks in the source's description of these forms are partly unclear; the forms are rendered as the description states them.]

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكابِرَ مُجْرِمِيها) A resumptive speech, to begin dividing people into the strong and the weak; and He singled out the great ones for crime because they are most able to spread crime and corruption. It was also said to be a conjunction on what precedes it, and there is nothing to prevent that. وكذلك is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, as has preceded. وجعلنا is a verb and fāʿil; وفي كل قرية is the second object of جعلنا; وأكابر is the first object of جعلنا; and مجرميها is a muḍāf ilayhi to أكابر.
(لِيَمْكُرُوا فِيها وَما يَمْكُرُونَ إِلَّا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ) The lām is for giving a reason; it was also said to be the lām of consequence or of becoming (ʿāqiba, ṣayrūra), and both are correct; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلنا. The wāw is a ḥāl wāw; ما is negative; ويمكرون is an imperfect verb, and the sentence is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يمكروا; إلا is a particle of restriction; and بأنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يمكرون. The wāw is a ḥāl wāw; ما is negative; and the sentence ما يشعرون is in the position of the accusative from the pronoun of يمكرون.
(وَإِذا جاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ قالُوا: لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ حَتَّى نُؤْتى مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ رُسُلُ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a coordinate conjunction on what has preceded; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to قالوا; the sentence جاءتهم is in the position of the genitive by annexation; وآية is the fāʿil; and the sentence قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and futurity; ونؤمن is an imperfect verb, accusative because of لن, and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl. حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; ونؤتى is a passive imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after حتى, its nāʾib fāʿil being latent; ومثل is the second mafʿūl bihi; ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation; the sentence أوتي has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; and رسل الله is the nāʾib fāʿil.
(اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسالَتَهُ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم is its khabar. As for حيث:
The opinions of the grammarians differ on it. One group said: it is not an adverb, because it is not for Him the Exalted to be more knowing in one place than in another, and because His knowledge does not differ with the difference of places. It is rather a mafʿūl bihi of a verb indicated by «أعلم», that is: "He knows the place fit for placing His message, and these are not people worthy of having it placed in them."
Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: "The apparent view is to leave it as a figurative adverbial, with «أعلم» containing the sense of a verb that governs an adverb, so that the implied form is: Allah is the most effective in knowledge where He places, that is, His knowledge is effective in this place in which He places His message." Al-Safāqusī said: "The apparent view is that it stays in its adverbial sense, and the difficulty arises only from the implication (mafhūm) of the adverb; and how many places there are in which the implication has been abandoned because of evidence for it, particularly as that evidence is present in this place." The sentence يجعل رسالته is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and رسالته is the mafʿūl bihi.
(سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا صَغارٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِما كانُوا يَمْكُرُونَ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to explain what will reach them on the Day of Resurrection. The sīn is a particle of futurity; ويصيب is an imperfect verb, nominative; الذين is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the sentence أجرموا has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; وصغار is the fāʿil; وعند الله is an adverb attached to يصيب, or a naʿt of صغار, that is, "established with Allah"; وعذاب شديد is conjoined to صغار; the bāʾ is a preposition of causation; ما is a maṣdar particle or a relative in the sense of "that which"; the sentence كانوا has no grammatical position in either case; and the sentence يمكرون is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:125-126.t:
* I'rab:
(فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, a mubtadaʾ; ويرد is the protasis and الله is its fāʿil; أن يهديه is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi, that is, "guidance" (هداية); ويشرح is the apodosis; وصدره is the mafʿūl bihi; and للاسلام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشرح. The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».
(وَمَنْ يُرِدْ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرَجاً كَأَنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّماءِ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, conjoined to the first «من»; أن يضلّه is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يرد; ويرد is the protasis; ويجعل is the apodosis, jussive; وصدره is the mafʿūl bihi; وضيقا is the second mafʿūl bihi; وحرجا is a naʿt of «ضيقا»; the comparative sentence beginning كأنما is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from صدره, or from the latent pronoun in «ضيقا», where (كأنما) is restrictive and restricted (kāffa and makfūfa); ويصعّد is an imperfect verb; and في السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يصّعد.
(كَذلِكَ يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ الرِّجْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The sentence is resumptive; and كذلك, the preposition and its genitive noun, is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; ويجعل is an imperfect verb; الله is the fāʿil; الرجس is the mafʿūl bihi; وعلى الذين is in the position of the second object; and the sentence لا يؤمنون is the ṣila of the relative.
(وَهذا صِراطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيماً) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to explain that what Muhammad ﷺ follows is Islam. وهذا is a mubtadaʾ; وصراط ربك is the khabar; ومستقيما is a ḥāl confirming the sentence (ḥāl muʾakkida), and the operator in it is the demonstrative, in view of the sense of a verb in it, for it means "I point" (أشير).
(قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) The sentence is resumptive; قد is a particle of confirmation; فصلنا الآيات is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ولقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فصّلنا; and the sentence يذكرون is a naʿt of قوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «كأنما يصّعد في السماء» there is a representational simile abstracted from several things, that is: the state of one whose breast has been made narrow and constricted is like the state of one who is charged with climbing into the sky. Its like has passed before.

dervis-irab:145-146.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَسْفُوحاً): Al-safḥ: pouring. Safaḥa comes both intransitive and transitive; one says: safaḥa so-and-so his tears and his blood, i.e. he shed it; except that the difference between them is made by the difference of the maṣdar: in the transitive one says safḥan, and in the intransitive one says sufūḥan. In this verse it occurs transitively, because the passive participle is formed only from a transitive verb. And as an intransitive example is what Abū ʿUbayda recited for Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
أقول ودمعي واكف عند رسمها ... عليك سلام الله والدمع يسفح
(I say, with my tears dripping by her abode: Peace of Allah be upon you, while the tears flow.)
And of the figurative use in this root: وبينهم سفاح, i.e. fighting or mutual slaughter (of camels), because they shed one another's blood; and سافحها مسافحة: he committed fornication with her, because each of them pours out his fluid and wastes it. Among their sayings: «في النكاح غنية عن السفاح» ("in marriage there is sufficiency from fornication").
This root has already been mentioned, together with the characteristics of the sīn and the fāʾ being the first and second radicals of the word.
(الْحَوايا): The intestines and bowels.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain what Allah the Exalted forbade to them. The clause لا أَجِدُ is the content of the saying; فِيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أَجِدُ; the clause أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; إِلَيَّ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of a nominative as the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of أُوحِيَ; مُحَرَّماً is a direct object of أَجِدُ, i.e. "a forbidden thing"; and عَلى …
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَماً مَسْفُوحاً أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ) The exception is connected (muttaṣil). طاعِمٍ is a preposition's genitive noun attached to مُحَرَّماً (with the preposition عَلى), and the clause يَطْعَمُهُ is an adjective of طاعِمٍ, because it is an exception from the genus, and its position is accusative; it is also permissible that it be a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it is an "occurrence" and what precedes is a substance, and its position is accusative also. مَيْتَةً is the khabar (predicate) of يَكُونَ, and its noun is latent, referring to His words «مُحَرَّماً»; the exception clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). دَماً is conjoined to مَيْتَةً, and مَسْفُوحاً is an adjective, i.e. flowing, like blood in the veins, not like the liver and spleen; and أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ is conjoined likewise.
«[Translator's note: the source text in the first clause breaks off at "وعلى"; it is rendered as printed.]»
(فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ) The fāʾ is for justification; inna and its noun; رِجْسٌ is its khabar; أَوْ is a conjunction; فِسْقاً is conjoined to لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ; the clause أُهِلَّ is an adjective, أُهِلَّ being a past verb; لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; بِهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أُهِلَّ; and the clause «فإنه رجس» is a justification with no position.
(فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ وَلا عادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The fāʾ is resumptive; مَنِ is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); اضْطُرَّ is a passive past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "then there is no blame on him". The meaning of اضْطُرَّ is: necessity befell him, calling him to partake of something of what was mentioned. غَيْرَ باغٍ is a ḥāl, i.e. not unjust; وَلا عادٍ is conjoined to باغٍ, i.e. not a transgressor. A similar statement has been verified in Sūrat al-Baqara. The fāʾ is for justification; inna and its noun; غَفُورٌ is a first khabar and رَحِيمٌ a second khabar; and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is the khabar of «مَنِ».
(وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ) A resumptive statement introduced to explain the reason for the prohibition of everything with a hoof/claw (ẓufur) to the Jews, because of their wrongdoing; the verification of that has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara. It includes everything with a ẓufur, namely the ostrich, the camel and the like of animals, and everything that does not have split digits among beasts and birds, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose and the duck. عَلَى الَّذِينَ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا; هادُوا is a verb and an agent; حَرَّمْنا is also a verb and an agent; كُلَّ is a direct object; ذِي is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); and ظُفُرٍ is genitive by the annexation of «ذِي» to it.
(وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُما) The wāw is a conjunction; مِنَ الْبَقَرِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا, and الْغَنَمِ is conjoined to الْبَقَرِ; عَلَيْهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حَرَّمْنا; and شُحُومَهُما is a direct object. The meaning is that He forbade to them the meat of everything with a ẓufur, and its fat, and everything from it, and left cattle and sheep/goats permitted, and forbade from them only the pure fats, namely al-thurūb, i.e. the thin fats that cover the paunch and the intestines, and the fat of the kidneys. (The kidneys are) the plural of kulya or kulwa, with ḍamma on the kāf in both.
(إِلَّا ما حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُما أَوِ الْحَوايا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ) إِلَّا is a particle of exception; مَا is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a connected exception from al-shuḥūm; the exception clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause حَمَلَتْ has no position because it is a ṣila; أَوْ is a conjunction and الْحَوايا is conjoined to ظُهُورُهُما; أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ: أَوْ is a conjunction, and مَا is a relative noun conjoined to ظُهُورُهُما; اخْتَلَطَ is a past verb, its agent being "he" (latent); and بِعَظْمٍ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اخْتَلَطَ.
(ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصادِقُونَ) The clause has no position because it is explicative (mufassira), to explain the reason for the prohibition. ذلِكَ is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ; the clause جَزَيْناهُمْ is the khabar; بِبَغْيِهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جَزَيْناهُمْ; a pronoun must be supposed, i.e. "we recompensed them with it, because of their transgression". More of the i'rab of this expression will come. The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and صادِقُونَ is the khabar of inna.

* Benefits:
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "ذلك is in the position of an accusative by جَزَيْناهُمْ; and it is said: a mubtadaʾ, the estimate being 'we recompensed them for it' (جزينا هموه); and it is said: a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'the matter is that'." It is noticed that Abū l-Baqāʾ did not explain on what basis it is accusative: is it as a maṣdar or as a direct object? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ذلك is the recompense with which we recompensed them, and it is the prohibition of good things", and its apparent sense is that it is accusative in the manner of a maṣdar. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Ibn Mālik claimed that a demonstrative noun does not become accusative, being used to point to the maṣdar, unless it is followed by the maṣdar; so you say: قمت هذا القيام, and قعدت ذلك القعود. It is not permissible to say: قمت هذا, nor قعد ذلك." On this basis it is not sound for «ذلك» to be accusative as a pointing to the maṣdar. I say: Sībawayh and the majority held that this is not a condition, and among the speech of the Arabs: «ظننت ذلك», by which they point to the supposition.

dervis-irab:127-128.t:
* I'rab:
(لَهُمْ دارُ السَّلامِ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) A resumptive sentence with no grammatical position, as if it came as an answer to a questioner asking what Allah has prepared for them, and he was told that. It is also possible that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يذكرون. ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar; ودار السلام is a postponed mubtadaʾ; وعند ربهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl from «دار السلام», the operator in it being the sense of abiding latent in «لهم»; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; وهو is a mubtadaʾ; ووليهم is the khabar; the bāʾ is a preposition of causation; ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle; the sentence كانوا has no grammatical position in either case; and the sentence يعملون is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ)
The wāw is resumptive; ويوم is an adverb accusative through an omitted verb, that is: "and remember the day We gather them" (واذكر يوم نحشرهم); the sentence نحشرهم (with nūn or yāʾ, both being readings) is in the position of the genitive by annexation after the adverb; and جميعا is a ḥāl. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Some made «يوم» a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted اذكر. It is preferable that the adverb be governed by the verb of saying with which the vocative is quoted, that is: 'And the day We gather them, We say: O assembly of the jinn' ; and this is preferable to what some permitted, namely making it accusative through اذكر as a mafʿūl bihi, because it takes it out of being an adverb." ويا معشر الجن is a vocative muḍāf, the maqūl of an omitted saying, that is: "and We say to them: O assembly of the jinn". قد is a particle of confirmation; واستكثرتم is a verb and fāʿil; and ومن الإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استكثرتم.
(وَقالَ أَوْلِياؤُهُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنا بِبَعْضٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; وقال أولياؤهم is a verb and fāʿil; ومن الإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; وربنا is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; واستمتع بعضنا is a verb and fāʿil; وببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استمتع; and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as the saying.
(وَبَلَغْنا أَجَلَنَا الَّذِي أَجَّلْتَ لَنا) The wāw is a conjunction; وبلغنا is a verb and fāʿil; وأجلنا is the object; والذي is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «أجلنا»; the sentence أجلت has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; and ولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أجلت.
(قالَ النَّارُ مَثْواكُمْ خالِدِينَ فِيها إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to convey Allah the Exalted's answer to them. وقال is a past verb whose fāʿil refers to Allah; والنار is a mubtadaʾ; ومثواكم is the khabar; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl; وخالدين is a ḥāl from the kāf in «مثواكم»; وفيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين; and وإلا ما شاء الله: إلا is a particle of exception, and ما is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle in the position of the accusative as an exception of the same genus, taking into account time, or place, or the punishment, since خالدين indicates them, that is: "abiding for every period of the periods, except the time of Allah's will", or "abiding in a specific place and punishment, unless Allah wills to transfer them to something other than the two". More discussion of this astonishing exception will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) إن and its ism; حكيم is its first khabar and عليم its second khabar; and the sentence has no grammatical position because it is in the nature of a giving of reasons.

* Rhetoric:
We spoke in the section on i'rab about the astonishing exception, in accordance with what the context and the grammatical texts guide to. But the seeker of the ideal rhetoric is not satisfied with such facility, and for this reason the rhetoricians took care over this verse and its sister from Sūrat Hūd, as will come, and the disagreements and discussions around it multiplied; we shall content ourselves with the most important of what we reached.

The view of al-Zamakhsharī:
1- Al-Zamakhsharī has a fine view, far from forced interpretations and nearer to precision. He said: "Or it may be of the speech of the one who has been wronged (mawtūr) who has gained the upper hand over his oppressor and keeps gnashing his teeth at him, while he is asked to ease the grip on his throat: 'May Allah destroy me if I ease it for you, unless you will' , and he knows that he wills only to take his satisfaction from him with the utmost he is able to of harshness and severity. His saying 'unless you will' is thus among the severest of threats with mockery of the one threatened, because it comes out in the form of an exception that holds out hopes." What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is preferable to the reports and forced interpretations, such as their saying: "It has been reported that they will enter a valley in which there is so much of the zamharīr (freezing cold) that it separates some of their limbs from others, so they howl and ask to be returned to the Hellfire."

The view of al-Zajjāj:
We have come upon a fine view of al-Zajjāj's that quenches thirst, but it is truncated and needs clarification and disclosure. Al-Zajjāj said: "What is meant, and Allah knows best, is: except what He wills of increase of punishment." However he, that is al-Zajjāj, did not make clear how the exception is sound, and the excepted on this interpretation does not differ from the excepted-from in ruling. It is apparent that punishment is of varying degrees, differing ranks and unequal measures, and as if what is meant is that they are held in the prison of punishment, except what your Lord wills of an increase that reaches the extreme and surpasses the limit, until, for its reaching the farthest extremes, it is almost counted as outside punishment, as though it were not of it nor within its sphere. It is known of the Arabs in the ways of their speech that they express a thing by its opposite when it reaches the extreme. So it is as if these tormented people, with affliction having overwhelmed them, and having reached the extreme of severity and the end of hardship, have arrived at a limit that almost takes it out of absolute punishment, so that treating it in expression as something different became permissible. This is a leap of al-Zajjāj's whose import we perceive only through this elaboration, whose understanding requires fineness of taste and transparency of nature. And Allah is the granter of success.

dervis-irab:129-130.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نُوَلِّي): from wilāya, that is, authority (imāra). One says: wallā fulānan al-amra tawliya: he made him a governor over it. Its origin is from waliya (with the lām lightened and with kasra), yalī wilāya (with kasra on the wāw) and walāya (with fatḥa): the thing, and ʿalayhi: he undertook it and took possession of its affair; and waliya al-balad: he gained mastery over it.

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضاً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; and كذلك is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, as has preceded in its like. It is also permissible that the preposition and its genitive noun be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is like the appointing of some of the wrongdoers over others" (الأمر مثل تولية بعض الظالمين); to this al-Zajjāj inclined. ونولي is an imperfect verb; وبعض الظالمين is its first object; وبعضا is its second object, or accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "over some" (على بعض), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to نولي. وبما: the bāʾ is a preposition, ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نولّي; وكان and its ism; the sentence يكسبون is its khabar; and the sentence كانوا is the ṣila of the relative.
[Translator's note: in the source text of the following passages, the opening of each Qur'anic quotation is cut off or fused with the end of the preceding sentence (for example «امَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ», «صفةَقُصُّونَ», «الُوا شَهِدْنا», «َ غَرَّتْهُمُ»). They are translated below as the verses they evidently quote: (يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ), (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا), (قالُوا شَهِدْنا عَلى أَنْفُسِنا), (وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ).]
(يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ)
يا is a vocative particle; ومعشر الجن is a vocative muḍāf; the vocative sentence is the maqūl of an omitted saying, that is: "it is said to them"; and the omitted saying is a resumption introduced to relate the state of their rebuke. The hamza is for rhetorical, rebuking questioning; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; ويأتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; ورسل is the postponed fāʿil; and منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, at «صفة»; the sentence evidently continues as «صفة لرسل» ("a naʿt of رسل")].
(يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا)
The sentence يقصون is a second naʿt of رسل; وعليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقصون, or to an omitted ḥāl, so that the indefinite noun is specified by the description. وآياتي is the mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is a conjunction; the sentence ينذرونكم is conjoined to يقصون, the wāw being the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; ولقاء is the second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ينذرونكم; ويومكم is a muḍāf ilayhi; and هذا is a naʿt of ليومكم, or a badal from it.
(قالُوا شَهِدْنا عَلى أَنْفُسِنا)
The sentence is resumptive, introduced to serve as an answer to a question, as though it were asked: "What did they say after the rebuke?" The sentence شهدنا على أنفسنا is in the position of the accusative as the content of their saying; and على أنفسنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهدنا, that is: "we acknowledged and affirmed".
(وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ)
The wāw is parenthetical, and the sentence غرتهم الحياة الدنيا is a parenthetical one to show the extent of their persistence in delusion. He repeated their testimony against themselves because in the first He related their saying, and how they say and confess, while in the second He intended merely to censure them, to declare their opinions foolish, and to brand them with scant reflection. أن and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "that they were disbelievers" (بأنهم كانوا كافرين); the sentence كانوا is the khabar of أن; and كافرين is the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:147-148.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ واسِعَةٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and إِنْ is conditional; كَذَّبُوكَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is a connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قُلْ is an imperative verb; رَبُّكُمْ is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject); ذُو رَحْمَةٍ is the khabar (predicate); and واسِعَةٍ is an adjective of رَحْمَةٍ; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause of the saying and what is within its scope is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.
(وَلا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the nominal clause, entering the scope of the saying; يُرَدُّ is a passive imperfect verb; بَأْسُهُ is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); عَنِ الْقَوْمِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُرَدُّ; and الْمُجْرِمِينَ is a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْمِ.
(سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا: لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا) The clause is resumptive, introduced to report what will issue from them in speech. The sīn is a particle of futurity; يَقُولُ is an imperfect verb; الَّذِينَ is the agent; the clause أَشْرَكُوا has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative; the clause لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of an accusative as the content of the saying; لَوْ is conditional; شاءَ اللَّهُ is a verb and an agent, and the object of the willing is omitted, i.e. "had He willed that we not associate partners", and parallels to it have preceded. وَلا آباؤُنا is conjoined to the pronoun in أَشْرَكْنا, and the conjunction was permitted because of the presence of «لا».
(وَلا حَرَّمْنا مِنْ شَيْءٍ) It is conjoined to ما أَشْرَكْنا, and مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida) in the direct object.
(كَذلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The kāf is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and this has preceded, i.e. "those before them denied with a denial like that denial".
(حَتَّى ذاقُوا بَأْسَنا قُلْ: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنا) حَتَّى is a particle of limit and of genitive, i.e. "they persisted in denial until they tasted"; بَأْسَنا is a direct object; هَلْ is an interrogative particle; the adverb is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مِنْ is redundant in the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the content of the saying. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; تُخْرِجُوهُ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after it; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ a direct object; and لَنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تُخْرِجُوهُ.
(إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ) The clause is resumptive; إِنْ is negative; تَتَّبِعُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; الظَّنَّ is a direct object; the wāw of وَإِنْ is a conjunction; إِنْ is negative; أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; and the clause تَخْرُصُونَ is the khabar of أَنْتُمْ.

dervis-irab:149-150.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبالِغَةُ) The clause of the saying is resumptive, and the fāʾ is the eloquent one (faṣīḥa), because it disclosed an implied condition, i.e. say: "if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof". لِلَّهِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; الْحُجَّةُ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and الْبالِغَةُ is an adjective, i.e. the one that has reached the utmost limit of finality and clarity and cut off every excuse of the one against whom the proof is brought; and the clause is the content of the saying.
(فَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and لَوْ is conditional; شاءَ is a verb with a latent agent, and the direct object is omitted, i.e. "your guidance"; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْ; هَداكُمْ is a verb with a latent agent and a direct object; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and أَجْمَعِينَ is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun; the ruling on emphasis with أجمع will come in the section on Benefits.
(قُلْ: هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هذا) The clause is resumptive; قُلْ is an imperative verb; هَلُمَّ is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of command, and a discussion of it will come in the section on Benefits; شُهَداءَكُمْ is a direct object, for a verbal noun works like what it names, whether transitive or intransitive; الَّذِينَ is an adjective; the clause يَشْهَدُونَ is a ṣila; أَنَّ اللَّهَ is أَنَّ and its noun, in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition; and the clause حَرَّمَ هذا is the khabar of أَنَّ.
(فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَلا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and إِنْ is conditional; شَهِدُوا is a past verb and the wāw is the agent, in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is a connective for the apodosis; لا is prohibitive; تَشْهَدْ is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and مَعَهُمْ is an adverb of place attached to تَشْهَدْ.
(وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تَتَّبِعْ is an imperfect verb made jussive by لا; أَهْواءَ is a direct object; الَّذِينَ is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by annexation; بِآياتِنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كَذَّبُوا, and the clause is the ṣila.
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and الَّذِينَ is conjoined to the preceding relative noun; the aim is to enumerate their ugly attributes. The meaning: do not follow the whims of those who combine the denial of the signs of Allah with disbelief in the Hereafter and the association of partners with Him. The clause لا يُؤْمِنُونَ is the ṣila of the relative; بِالْآخِرَةِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُؤْمِنُونَ; the wāw is a conjunction; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يَعْدِلُونَ is its khabar; and بِرَبِّهِمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يَعْدِلُونَ.

* Rhetoric:
In applying the name of testimony (shahāda) to submission to them and agreeing with them and confirming them in the false testimony, there is an explicit, derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya); and it is also sound that it be a free figurative expression (majāz mursal), from applying the necessary concomitant while intending what necessitates it, because testimony is among the concomitants of submission.

* Benefits:
When it is intended to strengthen the emphasis, the word «أجمع» is brought after the word «كله», and after the word «كلها» the word «جمعاء», and after the word «كلهم» the word «أجمعين», and after the word «كلهنّ» the word «جمع». You say: جاء الصفّ كله أجمع ("the whole class came, all of it"), and جاءت القبيلة كلها جمعاء ("the tribe came, all of it"); the Exalted said: «فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون»; and جاءت النساء كلهن جمع ("the women came, all of them"). Emphasis may also be made with أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعين and جمع even when the word «كل» has not preceded them, and from that are the words of the Exalted: «لأغوينهم أجمعين».
It is not permitted to form the dual of أجمع and جمعاء, there being no need for that, given the two words كلا and كلتا. Ibn Mālik, in his Alfiyya, summarised the rule of أجمع:
وبعد كل أكدوا بأجمعا ... جمعاء أجمعين ثم جمعا
ودون كل قد يجيء أجمع ... جمعاء أجمعون ثم جمع
(After kull they emphasise with ajmaʿ, jamʿāʾ, ajmaʿīn, then jumaʿ; and without kull there may come ajmaʿ, jamʿāʾ, ajmaʿūn, then jumaʿ.)
Halumma: a word in the sense of calling to a thing; it is thus intransitive, and it may be used transitively, as in: هلم شهداءكم, i.e. bring them. It is among the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), in which the singular and plural, the masculine and feminine are the same; and they conjugate it by making it a verb and attaching the pronouns to it, so they say in the dual: هلما; in the feminine: هلمي; in the masculine plural: هلموا; and for women: هلممن; and the first is more eloquent. It may be linked with the lām, so one says: هلمّ لك, like their saying: هيت لك. The heavy nūn of emphasis may be attached to it, so one says: هلمّنّ يا رجل, and هلمنّ يا امرأة, and هلمّانّ يا رجلان, and يا امرأتان, and هلمّنّ يا رجال, and هلمنانّ يا نسوة.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: you put kasra on the alif of (أنّ) and on the one after it in its jawāb (apodosis), as a fresh start (iʾtināf), and that is in the reading of the Readers.
And if you wish, you put fatḥa on the alif of (أنّ), meaning: your Lord has written upon Himself that whoever does…
And for the (أنّ) that comes after the fāʾ you have both kasra and fatḥa. As for the one who reads it with fatḥa, he says: the writing (al-kitāb) needs (أنّ) only once; but the predicate (khabar) is its proper place, so when it entered at the beginning of the speech it was repeated in its proper place; as He said: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾: since the position of أنّ is "does he promise you that you will be brought forth when you have died", it entered at the beginning of the speech and at its end. Similar to it is: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنّهُ مَـنْ تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ﴾ with fatḥa. And similar to it is: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ مَنْ يُحَادِدِ اللّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾. And you may put kasra on the (إن) that comes after the fāʾ in these passages, as a resumption (istiʾnāf); do you not see that you would find it good to say: "كتب أنه من تولاه فهو يضله" ("It was written that whoever takes him as an ally, he leads him astray") with fatḥa [Translator's note: i.e. with fatḥa on the first أنه]. Likewise "وأصلح فهو غفور رحيم" ("and makes amends, then He is Forgiving, Merciful"), if it were so, it would be correct. So whenever the insertion of (هو) is good, the kasra is good.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: you put (السبيل) in the nominative by His saying (وليستبين), because the verb belongs to it. Whoever treats السبيل as feminine says: ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. And the verb may be made to belong to the Prophet ﷺ, so you put السبيل in the accusative, the meaning being: "and that you, O Muhammad, may make clear the way of the criminals (ولتستبين يا محمد سبيلّ المجرمين)".

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلاَّ للَّهِ يَقُصُّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾: it was written with the yāʾ dropped because it meets the alif and lām [Translator's note: i.e. the reading يقضِ الحقّ, written without yāʾ]; just as ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانيَةَ﴾ was written without wāw, and as ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ was written without yāʾ, following the pronunciation. This is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd]. And it is reported from ʿAlī that he read: (يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ) with ṣād. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, he said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to me from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from a man from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (يقضِى بالحق). Al-Farrāʾ said: and so it is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: it is permissible to put it in the nominative (rafʿ).

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِّن ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾: one says خُفيَة and خِفية. And there is a dialect form of it with wāw — not valid in recitation —: خُفوة and خِفوة; just as it is said: "he untied his ḥubwa (حُبْوته), ḥibwa (حِبوته) and ḥibya (حِبْيته)".
His saying: ﴿لَّئِنْ أَنجَانَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ﴾ is the reading of the people of Kufa — and so it is in their codices —: "أن ج ى ن ألف" [Translator's note: i.e. spelled with a yāʾ, nūn and alif: أنجينا]; some of them read with the alif (أنجانا), and the reading of the people at large is (أنجيتنا) with tāʾ.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱلْقَادِرُ عَلَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَاباً﴾: as He did to the people of Noah: the rain, the stones and the flood. ﴿أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾: the swallowing up by the earth (al-khasf). ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾: He mixes you up into factions (shiyaʿ) of differing whims.

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن ذِكْرَىٰ﴾ is in the position of the accusative or the nominative; [the accusative] by an implied (muḍmar) verb: (ولكِن) we remind them a (ذِكرى) reminding; and the nominative on the reading: (ولكن) it is (ذكرى) a reminder.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً﴾: it is said: there is no people but that they have a feast, and they amuse themselves at their feasts, except the community of Muhammad ﷺ; for their feasts are piety, prayer, takbīr and good.
His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ﴾ means: [lest a soul] be held in pledge. (The Arabs say: "هذا عليك بَسْل", i.e. this is forbidden to you. And for that reason it is said "أسَد باسل", i.e. a lion that is not to be approached.) And the Arabs say: "أعْطِ الراقِىَ بُسْلته" ("give the charmer his busla"), which is the fee for the charm.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and his wife were calling their son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to Islam. That is His saying: ﴿إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾, i.e. obey us. And if it were "إِلى الهدى أن ائتنا" it would be correct; as He said: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إِلَى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾, in many similar cases, where أَنْ is sometimes brought and sometimes dropped.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاةَ...﴾ is referred back (maʿṭūf) to the lām in His saying: ﴿وأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ﴾. The Arabs say: "أمرتك لتذهب" ("I commanded you that you go"), (and "وأن تذهب"); so أَن is in the position of the accusative by being referred back to the command. And there is much like it in the Qurʾān.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾: it is said that His saying (فيكون) refers specifically to the Trumpet (al-ṣūr), i.e. He says to the Trumpet: (كُنْ فَيَكُونُ).
And it is said that His saying (كن فيكون) belongs with His saying "His word is the truth (هو الحقّ)", as a naʿt (description) of the word; then you make its verb ﴿يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾, meaning: His word will be the truth on that day. And it may be that you say: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾ of every thing, so that it is a self-sufficient phrase, and you put "the word (القول)" in the nominative by "the truth (الحقّ)", and put (اليوم) in the accusative because it is the setting (maḥall) for "His word is the truth".
The Arabs say: نِفخ فى الصورِ and نُفِخَ; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (كهيئة الطير فأنفخها فتكون طيرا بإذنى). And the poet said:
لولا ابنُ جَعْدة لم يُفتَح قُهُنْدُزكم * ولا خُراسانُ حتى يُنْفَخَ الصورُ
(Were it not for Ibn Jaʿda, your citadel would not have been opened, nor Khurāsān, until the Trumpet is blown.)
And it is said that al-ṣūr is a horn; and it is said: it is a plural of ṣūra (form), the blowing into the forms (al-ṣuwar) being into the dead.
And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾: it is said: آزر is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), and it does not take tanwīn (lā yujrā) because it is foreign (aʿjamī). The genealogists are agreed that he was the son of Tāraḥ, so it is as though Āzar was a nickname for him. And it has reached me that the meaning of (آزر) in their language is "crooked", as though he reproached him for his deviation and crookedness from the truth. Some of them read (لأبيه ازرُ) in the nominative, as a vocative (with يا), and that is a good reading. His saying: ﴿أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَاماً آلِهَةً﴾: you put the idols in the accusative because the verb falls upon them.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾: one says جنّ عليه الليل and أَجَنَّ, and أَجنَّه الليل and جَنّه الليل; with the alif is better when you drop (على), and it is more common than جنَّه الليل.
Two views are given on His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ رَأَى كَوْكَباً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾: that he said "this is my Lord" only to draw his people step by step towards the proof against them, in order to reproach their gods as being nothing, and that the star, the moon and the sun were greater than them and yet were not gods; and it is said: he said it in the other sense; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَى. وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالاّ فَهَدَى﴾; and here they adduced as proof Abraham's saying: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنى رَبِّى لأَكُونَنّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ﴾.

farraa:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾: if you wish you may make ﴿الجِنّ﴾ an explanation of "partners". And if you wish you may make its accusative be on [the meaning]: they made the jinn partners to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
His saying: ﴿وَخَرَقُواْ﴾: and اخترقوا, خلقوا and اختلقوا, meaning: they fabricated.

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: ﴿خَالِقُ﴾ is put in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ), or as being a khabar (predicate). If you put it in the accusative, since it has no alif and lām, by way of qaṭʿ (cutting off), it would be correct; it is like His saying: ﴿غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ﴾, and likewise: ﴿فَاطِرِ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرْضِ﴾ — if you put it in the accusative when there is a complete definite noun before it, that would be permissible; for you may say: "الفاطر السموات", "الخالق كل شىء", "القابل التوب", "الشديد العقاب". And you may say: "مررت بعبد الله محدِّثِ زيد" ("I passed by ʿAbdallāh, the one who talks with Zayd"), making it definite even though alif and lām would fit it well, when he has become known by that; so it is like your saying: "مررت بوحشىّ قاتل حمزة" ("I passed by Waḥshī, the slayer of Ḥamza"), and "بابن ملجَم قاتِل علىّ" ("by Ibn Muljam, the slayer of ʿAlī"): he became known by it until it became like a name for him.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾: they say: you learned from the Jews. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (وليقولوا درس), meaning Muhammad ﷺ. It is as you say in speech: "قالوا لى: أساء" ("they said to me: he did wrong") and "قالوا لى: أسأت" ("…you did wrong"). Similar to it: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَيُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾.
Some read (دارست), meaning: you disputed with the Jews and they disputed with you; and so said Ibn ʿAbbās. Mujāhid read it (دارَسْت) and explained it: you read to the Jews and they read to you.
And it has been read (دُرِسَتْ), i.e. it was read and recited. And they read (دَرُسَتْ) and they read (دَرَسَتْ), meaning: it has grown old, i.e. this that he recites to us is something that has lasted long and passed by us.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾: that is because they said to him: "Do you not fear that our gods will strike you with madness for your reviling them?" So he said to them: "Do you not fear that yourselves from them, since you have made equal the small and the great, the male and the female — that the great one will be angry since you have made the small one equal to it?" Then he said to them: "Is the one who worships one god more entitled to be safe, or the one who worships scattered gods?" They said: "The one who worships one god", and so they became angry with themselves. That is His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ﴾: this hāʾ is for Noah: and (We guided) of his offspring David and Solomon. If David and Solomon were put in the nominative on this meaning, since the verb is not overt, it would be correct; just as you say: "أخذت صدقاتِهِم لكل مائة (شاةٍ شاةً) وشاةٌ" ("I took their alms: for every hundred sheep, one sheep"), [with شاة in the accusative] and [in the nominative] شاةٌ.

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْيَسَعَ﴾: the companions of ʿAbdallāh double the lām [Translator's note: i.e. read وَاللَّيْسَع], and that is more like the foreign names than [the reading of] those who say (والْيَسَعَ); the Arabs hardly ever put alif and lām on what does not take tanwīn (mā lā yujrā), such as Yazīd and Yaʿmur, except in poetry; one of them recited:
وَجَدْنا الوليد بن اليزيد مباركا * شديدا بأَحْنَاء الخِلافةِ كاهِله
(We found al-Walīd son of al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong to bear the burdens of the caliphate.)
He put the alif and lām on Yazīd only because he had put them on al-Walīd. And when the Arabs do that, they give the word a touch of praise.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن يَكْفُرْ بِهَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾ means the people of Mecca; ﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْماً﴾ means the people of Medina; ﴿لَّيْسُواْ بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾ — [disbelieving] in the sign (al-āya).

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾: they did not magnify Him as He truly should be magnified. His saying ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾: He says: how could you say "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being", when the Torah was sent down to Moses ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾; and al-qirṭās in this place is a sheet. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَاباً فى قِرْطَاسٍ﴾ means: on a sheet.
﴿تُبْدُونَهَا وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيراً﴾: He says: you show what you like, and you conceal the description of Muhammad ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: Muhammad ﷺ was commanded to say ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, i.e. Allah sent it down to you. And if you wish you may say: say: (He is) Allah.
And His saying ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ may be an answer to His saying: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِهِ مُوسَىٰ﴾ — ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ sent it down. I chose putting ﴿ٱللَّهُ﴾ in the nominative not as an answer only because it is Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who commanded Muhammad ﷺ to ask them: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾, and it is not a question from them so that they would be answered; but it is permissible because it is a question, and a question may have an answer.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: if it were in the jussive (jazm) it would be correct; as He said: ﴿ذَرْهُمْ يأكُلُوا وَيَتَمتّعُوا﴾.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾: it is said in the exegesis that the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) is Mecca.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾: the hāʾ may refer to Muhammad ﷺ or to the Revelation.

farraa:93-93.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: it is said that it was revealed concerning Musaylima the Liar, and that is because he claimed prophethood.
﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ﴾: and مَن is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ). He means: and who is more wrongful than this one and than this one who said: "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down." It was revealed concerning ʿAbdallāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ.
That is because he used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿وَاللّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمُ﴾ he would write (سميع عليم) or (عزيزحكيم), and the Prophet ﷺ would say to him: "It is the same"; until he dictated to him His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلاَلَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾, and Ibn Abī Sarḥ said ﴿فَتَبَارَكَ اللّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ﴾, in wonder at the detailing of the creation of man. He said: and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Thus was it sent down to me", so he doubted and apostatised. And he said: "If Muhammad ﷺ is truthful, then it has been revealed to me (as it was revealed to him), and if he is lying, then I have said the like of what he said." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down concerning him: ﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنَزلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: and it is said: stretching out their hands to draw out the souls of the disbelievers. It is like His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ﴾. If it were (باسطون), it would be (أيدِيَهُمْ) [in the accusative]; and if it were "باسطو أيديهم أن أخرِجوا" it would be correct. Similar to it, among cases where أن is left out, is His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهدَى ائْتِنَا﴾. And when you drop (أن) from speech like this, a verb of saying is implied (muḍmar) in it, as in His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تـَرَى إِذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — they say: ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ﴾: it is a plural. The Arabs say: [a people] فرادى and فرادُ, O you, and they do not give it tanwīn (lā yujrūnahā), likening it to ثُلاَث and رُبَاع. The singular of فرادى is فَرْد, فرِد and فريد; and فراد is for the plural, and فرد is not permissible in this sense. One of them recited to me:
ترى النُعَراتِ الزُرْق تحت لَبَانه * فُرَادَ ومثنى أصعقتها صواهِله
(You see the blue gadflies beneath his breast, singly and in pairs, struck down by his neighing.)
His saying: ﴿لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: Ḥamza and Mujāhid read (بينُكُمْ), meaning "your bond". And in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (لقد تقطع ما بينَكم), and that is the natural form of the speech. When the verb is made to belong to بين it is left in the accusative; just as they say: "أتانى دونك من الرجال" ("there came to me men below you"), leaving it in the accusative although it is in the position of the nominative, because it is a description (ṣifa). And when they say: "هذا دون من الرجال" ("this is an inferior one among men") they put it in the nominative in the nominative position. Likewise you say: "بين الرجلين بين بعيد" and "بون بعيد" ("between the two men is a great gap"); when you use it on its own you give it tanwīn in Arabic and give it the case inflection (iʿrāb).

farraa:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾: al-iṣbāḥ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أصبحنا إصباحا" ("we entered the morning"), and al-aṣbāḥ is the morning of each day, collectively.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْلَّيْلَ سَكَناً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾: الليل is in the position of the accusative in meaning. So He referred the sun and the moon back to its meaning, since He separated between them by His saying (سكنا); and when you do not separate them by anything, they prefer the genitive. And the accusative is permissible even if nothing comes between them; one of them recited:
وبينا نحن ننظره أتانا * معلِّقَ شَكْوةٍ وزِنادَ راع
(While we were watching for him, he came to us, hanging up a water-skin and a shepherd's fire-stick.)
And you say: "أنت آخذٌ حقَّك وحَقِّ غيرك" ("you are taking your right and the right of others"), putting the second in a genitive construct while you gave tanwīn to the first; because the meaning of your saying "أنت ضارب زيدا" and "ضاربُ زيدٍ" is the same. The best of this is that you put something between them; as Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فظلّ طُهاة اللحم من بينِ مُنْضِج * صفيفَ شِواءٍ أو قَدِيرٍ معجَّلِ
(And the cooks of the meat kept on, some ripening a row of roast, or a hastened pot-stew.)
So he put الصفيف in the accusative and القَدِير in the genitive, according to what I told you.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ means in the womb, ﴿وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ in the man's loins. And it is read (فمستقِرّ), meaning the child in the womb, (ومستودع) in the man's loins. Its nominative is by implying a description (ṣifa) [Translator's note: i.e. an implied predicate such as "of them"]; as when you say: "رأيت الرجلين عاقل وأحمق" ("I saw the two men: a wise one and a fool"), meaning: of them is such and such.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: those swearing are the disbelievers. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring them the sign that was revealed in al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾; so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to have it sent down and swore that they would believe.
