The believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask your Lord to send it down upon them so that they believe." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: Say to those who believe: "And what makes you perceive that they will believe?" This is the reason for the accusative [fatḥa] in أنّ: "and what makes you perceive that they will believe", (and) We ﴿نُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾. Some read: (إنها) with kasra on the alif, (إذَا جَاءَتْ) as a fresh start, and make His saying (وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ) a self-sufficient statement. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is: (وما يشعِركم إذا جاءتهم أنهم لا يؤمنون).
And (لا) in this place is a ṣila (redundant connective); like His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: the meaning is: it is forbidden to them that they return. And similar to it: ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ لاَ تَسْجُدَ﴾, its meaning is: that you prostrate.
In the reading of Ubayy it is: (لعلها إِذا جاءتهم لا يؤمِنون). The Arabs have a usage for (لعلّ) in that they say: "ما أدرى أنك صاحبها" ("I do not know — perhaps you are the one"), meaning: لعلك صاحبها; and they say: "ما أدرى لو أنك صاحبها"; and it is a good interpretation to make (أنّ) stand in the place of لعل.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ﴾: this is a thing they had asked for, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: if We did that for them they would not believe ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: (قُبُلاً) is the plural of qabīl, and al-qabīl is the guarantor (al-kafīl). I chose here that al-qubul should be in the sense of guaranteeing only because of their saying: ﴿أَوْ تَأتِى بِاللّهِ وَالْمَلاَئِكَةِ قَبِيلاً﴾ — guaranteeing that. And (قُبُلا) may mean: from before their faces; as you say: "I came to you from the front (قُبُلا) and did not come to you from behind (دُبُرا)". And al-qabīl may be a plural of qabīla (tribe), as though you said: or you bring us Allah and the angels tribe by tribe and group by group. And if it were read قَبَلا in the sense of "face to face (muʿāyanatan)" it would be correct, as you say: "أنا لقيته قبلا" ("I met him face to face").

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ﴾: you put "enemy" and "devils" in the accusative by His saying: جعلنا.
His saying: ﴿يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾: Iblīs — according to what is mentioned — assigned one party of his devils to humans and one party to the jinn; when the devil of the human and the devil of the jinnī meet, [the first] says: "I led my companion astray with such and such, so lead your companion astray with it", and (the devil of the jinnī) says the like of that to him. This is their inspiring one another. Al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥayyān narrated that to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:113-113.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَقْتَرِفُواْ مَا هُم مُّقْتَرِفُونَ﴾: al-iqtirāf is earning; the Arabs say: "So-and-so went out to earn (yaqtarif) for his family."

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿مُنَزَّلٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾: of those who doubt that they know that it is sent down from your Lord.

farraa:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ in eating carrion, ﴿يُضِلُّوكَ﴾, because most of them were astray. That is because they said to the Muslims: "Do you eat what you have killed and not eat what your Lord has killed!" So this verse was sent down: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ﴾: (من) is in the position of the nominative, like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أىُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى﴾. When (من) comes after [verbs of] knowing, looking and perceiving — such as نظرت, علمت and دريت — it follows the pattern of أىّ. If after it there is a verb whose agent it is, you put it in the nominative by that verb; and if after it there is a verb that falls upon it, you put it in the accusative; as when you say: "ما أدرى من قام" ("I do not know who stood"), you put (من) in the nominative by قام; and "ما أدرى من ضربت" ("I do not know whom you struck"), you put it in the accusative by ضربت.

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ظَاهِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾: as for its outward part, it is debauchery and fornication; and as for its inward part, it is secret companionship (al-mukhālla): that the woman takes a lover and that he takes her.

farraa:121-121.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ﴾: He says: your eating that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned is fisq, i.e. disbelief. He alluded to the eating [by the pronoun], as He said: ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾, meaning: the people's saying increased them in faith.

farraa:122-122.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ﴾: i.e. he was astray and We guided him.
His saying: ﴿نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ means his faith.

farraa:124-124.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُواْ صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from Allah; so said the exegetes. And in Arabic it is as you say: "سيأتينى رزق عندك" ("provision with you will come to me"), like your saying: "سيأتينى الذى عند الله" ("what is with Allah will come to me"): the humiliation that is with Him will strike them, and it is for Muhammad ﷺ to bring it down on them. But it is not permissible in Arabic to say "جئت عند زيد" while you mean "from Zayd (من عند زيد)".
And His saying ﴿صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ may mean that they chose disbelief out of pride and disdain for following Muhammad ﷺ, so Allah made that humiliation in His sight.

farraa:125-125.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ﴾: [مَن] and مَن are in the position of the nominative by the hāʾ that refers back to each of them.
His saying: (يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرِجاً): Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUmar read it (حرِجا), and the people read it حَرَجا. Al-ḥaraj — according to Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation — is a place thick with trees which the grazing flock cannot reach. He said: likewise the breast of the disbeliever, wisdom cannot reach it. With kasra and with fatḥa it is like waḥad and waḥid, farad and farid, danaf and danif: the Arabs say them with one meaning.
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: He says: the way became narrow for him, and he found nothing but to climb into the sky, and he is not able. And it is read (كأنما يصَّاعَد), meaning يتصاعد, and (ويَصْعد) without doubling.

farraa:128-128.t: His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ﴾: He says: you have led many astray. His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُم مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا ٱسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ﴾: the humans' enjoyment of the jinn is that a man, when he went off alone and felt lonely, or killed one of their game and became afraid, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley", and would spend the night feeling safe. As for the jinn's enjoyment of humans, it is the reverence from humans that they obtained through them; the jinn used to say: "We have become lords of the jinn and the humans."

farraa:130-130.t:
His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ﴾: someone may say: the messengers are from humans only, so how did He say to the jinn and the humans (منكم) "from among you"? It is said: this is like His saying: ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ﴾, then He said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾, whereas pearls and coral come out only from the salt water and not from the fresh.
So it is as though you said: they come out from part of them, from one of them.

farraa:131-131.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ﴾: if you wish you may make (ذلك) in the position of the accusative, and make (أن) one of those where a genitive-governing preposition fits, so that when you drop it, it is accusative. He means: He did that because [your Lord] was not one to destroy the towns.
And if you wish you may make (ذلك) nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), since the verb is not overt. Similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾. And similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللّهُ مُوهِنُ كَيْد الْكَافِرِينَ﴾: the nominative and the accusative are permissible in all of it.
His saying: ﴿مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا غَافِلُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing while they are heedless, no messenger nor proof having yet come to them. And His saying in Hūd: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرَى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing, i.e. for their associating partners [with Allah], (while their people are doing right), dealing with each other justly among themselves. Thus the exegesis has come. And there is another sense in it — and it is dearer to me than this, because associating partners [with Allah] is the greatest of sins — and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: He was not one to destroy them by wrongdoing on His part while they are doing right.

farraa:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: He says: the provision of every thing, meaning what grows and is fit as nourishment for every thing. Thus the exegesis has come, and it is the natural sense of the speech. In Arabic it is also permissible that you put "vegetation" in a genitive construct with "every thing" while by "every thing" you also mean the vegetation, so that it is like His saying: ﴿إنّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾, where al-yaqīn is the ḥaqq itself. His saying: ﴿مِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾: the proper form is the nominative for القنوان, because the meaning is: and from the palm trees, their clusters are near. If it were put in the accusative — "and He brought out from the palm trees, from their spathes, near clusters (قنوانا دانية)" — it would be permissible in speech, but it is not recited so because of the written text.
His saying: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾ is accusative, except that the feminine plural with tāʾ takes the genitive ending in the position of the accusative; and if you put الجنات in the nominative following القنوان, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَفِى الأَرضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ﴾: the proper form there is the nominative, making it follow القطع; and if you put it in the accusative and made it follow الرواسى and الأنهار, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ﴾ means the olive tree and the pomegranate trees, just as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلَ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning the people of the town.
His saying: ﴿ٱنْظُرُوۤاْ إِلِىٰ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ﴾: He says: look at it when it first sets fruit, (وَيَنْعِهِ): its ripening. And it has been read (ويُنْعِهِ) and (ويانِعِهِ). As for His saying: ﴿ويُنْـعِهِ﴾, it is like "its ripeness (نضجه)", and يانعه is like "its ripe and mature state (ناضجه وبالغه)".

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: (مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ) is in the position of the nominative; and if you put it in the accusative it would be correct; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَاللّهُ يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: when the subject of the verb is feminine and of the nature of a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as al-ʿāqiba (outcome), al-mawʿiẓa (admonition) and al-ʿāfiya (well-being), then when you put its verb before it you may make the verb feminine or masculine; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَمَنْ جَاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ with the masculine, and said: ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ with the feminine. Likewise ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ﴾. So do not shy away from either masculine or feminine in this.
[Translator's note: the source literally says "when the verb (al-fiʿl) is feminine"; al-Farrāʾ means the noun that the verb is predicated of.]

farraa:136-136.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا للَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ﴾, and برُعْمِهم and زِعمِهم: three dialect forms [Translator's note: the source writes برُعْمِهم with rāʾ, evidently for بزُعْمِهم]. No one we know of has read it with kasra on the zāy. The Arabs sometimes treat a word thus in cases like this; they say: al-fatk, al-futk and al-fitk, and al-wudd, al-widd and al-wadd, among similar words. The best of it is what the Readers from whom recitation is transmitted have chosen. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "وهذا لشركائِهم"; and it is as you say in speech: ʿAbdallāh said: "he has wealth (إنّ له مالا)" and "I have wealth (إنّ لى مالا)", meaning himself. And the poet said:
رَجْلانِ من ضَبّة أَخبرانا * إنا رأينا رجلا عريانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
And if he had said "they informed us that they had seen" it would be correct.

farraa:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿ٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾: they were a people who served their gods, and they made burying daughters alive seem fair to them. Also, one of them would say: "If such-and-such a number of males is born to me, I will sacrifice one of them." That is the killing of their children. And الشركاء is nominative, because they are the ones who made it seem fair.
Some used to read: "وكذلك زُيِّن لِكثِيرٍ مِن المشركين قتلُ أولادِهم", putting القتل in the nominative since its agent is not named, and putting (الشركاء) in the nominative by a verb he intends; as though he said: their partners made it seem fair to them. Similar to it is His saying: (يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالآصَالِ), then He said: ﴿رجَالٌ لاَ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ﴾. In some of the codices of the people of Syria it is (شركايهم) with yāʾ; if that is established from the early ones, then it ought to be read (زُيِّنَ), and the partners would be the children, because they share with them in lineage and inheritance. But if they read (زَيَّنَ), I do not know its rationale; unless in it they were following the dialect of a people who say "أتيتها عِشايا" and then say in the dual of (الحمراء: حمرايان); this would be a way for them to have said: "زَيَّنَ لكثيرٍ من المشركين قتل أولادِهم شركايُهُمْ". And if you wish, when you read (زَيَّنَ) with fatḥa, you may make it a verb of Iblīs and then put الشركاء in the genitive as following الأولاد. The view of whoever said that they intended something like the poet's saying:
فزججتها متمكّنا * زجَّ القَلوصَ أبِى مزاد
(I thrust her firmly, as Abū Mazād thrusts the young she-camel.)
is worth nothing. This is among what the grammarians of the people of the Ḥijāz used to say, and we have not found its like in Arabic.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation is cut in the source as ﴿ٰلِكَ﴾, i.e. ﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ﴾; the poetic verse illustrates separating muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi by the object, the construction attributed to the Syrian reading زُيِّنَ … قتلُ أولادَهم شركائِهم.]

farraa:139-139.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is "خالص لذكورنا". Its being feminine is because of the femininity of الأنعام; since what is in their bellies is like them, it was made feminine because of their femininity. Whoever makes it masculine does so because (ما) is masculine. Some have read "خالصُهُ لذكورِنا", putting it in a genitive construct with the hāʾ, the hāʾ referring to ما. And you could put الخالص and الخالصة in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), making the predicate of ما lie in the lām in His saying (لِذُكُورِنَا), as though you said: what is in the bellies of these cattle is for our males, exclusively (خالصا / خالصةً), as He said: ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾. But the accusative in this position is rare; they hardly say "عبدالله قائما فيها" ("ʿAbdallāh, standing, is in it"), but it is analogically sound.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾: if you wish you may put الميتة in the nominative, and if you wish you may put it in the accusative, saying (ميتةً). And you may say تكن or يكن, with tāʾ or yāʾ.
And al-khāliṣa may be a maṣdar, given its feminine form, as you say al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. It is like His saying: ﴿إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ﴾.

farraa:141-141.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَّعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ﴾: these are the vines. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهاً﴾ in its colour, and ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾ in its taste: some of it sweet and some of it sour.
His saying: ﴿وَآتُواْ حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾: this is for the orphans and the poor who are present at it.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾: in giving all of it. That is because Thābit ibn Qays left the people free to take from his palm trees, and all of it was taken and nothing of it remained for his family; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.

farraa:142-142.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾: He says: and He produced for you from the cattle beasts of burden (ḥamūla), meaning those able to carry and work; and al-farsh: the small ones.

farraa:143-143.t:
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: if you wish you may make "eight" referred back (as badal) to الحمولة; and if you wish you may imply a verb for it.
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: the male is a pair-member (zawj) and the female is a zawj. And if you put "two and two" in the nominative because of the entry of (مِن), it would be correct, as you say: "رأيت القوم منهم قاعد ومنهم قائم" ("I saw the people: of them is one sitting and of them one standing"), and [also] قاعد وقائما.
The meaning of His saying: ﴿قُلْ ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ﴾: He says: did the prohibition come to you, in what you have forbidden of the sāʾiba, the baḥīra, the waṣīla and the ḥām, from the two males or from the two females? If they said: "from the side of the male", every male would be forbidden to them; and if they said: "from the side of the female", every female would be forbidden to them.
Then He said: ﴿أَمَّا ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ﴾: He says: or has He forbidden you what the womb contains? If they said that, male and female would be forbidden to them, because the womb contains both male and female. And (ما) in His saying "أمّا اشْتَمَلَتْ" is in the position of the accusative; you put it in the accusative as following the two males and the two females.

farraa:144-144.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ﴾: He says: did Allah enjoin this on you, you seeing it with your own eyes?

farraa:145-145.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَجِدُ فِي مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً﴾, then He, Majestic is His Face, said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً﴾; and if you wish, (تَكُونَ). In (الميتة) there are two possibilities: the nominative and the accusative. The nominative is not valid in recitation, because الدم is in the accusative by being referred back to الميتة, and it [i.e. أو دما] has an alif that prevents the nominative from being permissible. And (أن تكون) is permissible because الميتة is feminine, then you refer what comes after it back to it. Whoever puts (الميتة) in the nominative makes it the fiʿl of (يكون) [Translator's note: al-Farrāʾ's term; here: its subject], content with يكون without a predicate. Likewise (يكون) in all exception constructions does not need a predicate; do you not see that you say: "ذهب الناس إلا أن يكون أخاك" and "أخوك" ("the people went, unless it be your brother")? Kāna and yakūn could do without a predicate only as what follows إلا does without a verb belonging to the noun. Since it is said "قام الناس إلا زيدا" and "إلا زيد", putting it in the accusative without a verb and in the nominative without a verb, kāna was fit to be complete (tāmma).
Whoever reads the accusative says: kāna, by the Arabs' usage, has a nominative and an accusative, so they implied in kāna an unknown noun (ism majhūl) [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun of the matter, ḍamīr al-shaʾn], and made what comes after it the predicate (fiʿl) of that unknown. That is permissible with kāna, laysa and lam yazal, and with aẓunnu and its sisters: that you say (أظنه زيد أخوك, and) أظنّه فيها زيد ("I think — Zayd is in it"). And it is permissible with inna and its sisters; as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿يَا بُنَىّ إِنَّهَا إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ﴾, and as in His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾. You make the hāʾ masculine and singular; it is not permissible to make it dual, nor plural with a plural or anything else. Making it feminine with a feminine, and masculine with a feminine, is permissible; so you say: "إنها ذاهبة جاريتك" and "إنه ذاهبة جاريتك" ("your slave-girl is going").
If you say: how is the feminine permissible with the female, while the dual is not permissible with two? I say: because the Arabs only had regard to the feminine and masculine of the verb; since ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ﴾ are permissible, feminine and masculine are permissible; and since "قاما أخواك" and "قاموا قومك" are not permissible, its dual and plural are not permissible.
If you say: do you permit its dual in the usage of those who say "ذهبا أخواك"? I say: no, because the verb is singular, and the alif in it is as it were an indication of the two doers of the verb, and the wāw in the plural indicates the doers of the verb; so it is not sound to allude to a verb and a noun in one knot. The verb is always singular, because the additions in it are nouns.
And you say, in two questions of this from which one may infer others: "إنها أسَد جاريتك" ("your slave-girl is a lion"), making it feminine because الأسد is the predicate (fiʿl) of الجارية; but if you made الجارية the predicate of الأسد and of masculine nouns like it, only the masculine hāʾ would be permissible. Likewise every masculine noun that you liken to a feminine, make the hāʾ masculine in it; and every feminine that you liken to a masculine, it has the hāʾ masculine or feminine; this is one. And whenever you make the verb of a feminine masculine, saying "قام جاريتك" or "طال صلاتك", (then introduce إنه on it), only the masculine is permissible, so you say: "إنه طال صلاتك" ("your prayer has become long"); you make it masculine because the verb is masculine; it is not permissible to make it feminine when the verb has been made masculine.
And when you see the noun put in the nominative by the locatives (al-maḥāll) — such as عندك, فوقك and فيها — use feminine or masculine with the feminine, and do not use the feminine with the masculine. That is because with the ṣifa (locative phrase) one cannot make it feminine as one can (in قام) جاريتك, by saying قامت جاريتك. Therefore with locative phrases the original form is followed.
And when you devote kāna to a single noun, you may put it in the nominative and make the verb belong to it. And if you wish, you may imply in it an unknown [noun] and put what comes after it in the accusative, saying: "إذا كان غدا فأتنا" ("when it is tomorrow, come to us"). And you say: "اذهب فليس إلا أباك" and "أبوك" ("go, for there is none but your father"). Whoever reads the nominative implies "anyone", as though he said: there is no one but your father; and whoever reads the accusative implies the unknown noun and puts it in the accusative; because the unknown is definite, therefore you put it in the accusative. And whoever says "إذا كان غُدْوةً فأتنا" ("when it is morning, come to us") may not say "إذا غدوةً كان فأتنا"; likewise the unknown noun may not be preceded by its accusative. And when you couple an indefinite noun with a locative phrase (ṣifa) in kāna, saying "إن كان بينهم شرّ فلا تقربهم" ("if there is evil between them, do not approach them"), you put it in the nominative. And if you begin with الشر and put the locative phrase after it, the proper form is the nominative, saying: "إن شر بينهم فلا تقربهم", and the accusative is permissible. He said: and one of them recited to me:
فعينَىَّ هلاَّ تبكيان عِفَاقا * إذا كان طعنا بينهم وعِناقا
(O my two eyes, will you not weep for ʿIfāq, when there was spearing between them and close grappling?)
When you devote kāna to an indefinite noun alone, the accusative and nominative are equal; and when you devote kāna to a definite noun alone, the proper form is the accusative; they say: "لو كان إلا ظله لخاب ظله" ("if it were [nothing] but his shadow, his shadow would fail"). These are as I have described to you.

farraa:146-146.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ﴾: He forbade them the omentum (al-tharb) and the fat of the kidneys.
Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾: and (ما) is in the position of the accusative by the verb, through the exception.
And (الحَوَايَا) is in the position of the nominative, referring it back to الظهور: "except what their backs carry or the entrails carry"; and they are the intestines and the "daughters of milk" (bināt al-laban). The accusative is on your intending (أو شحوم الحوايا) "or the fat of the entrails", dropping "fat" and contenting yourself with "entrails"; as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning: and ask the people of the town.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾: it is the fat-tail (al-alya). And (ما) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:151-151.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً﴾: if you wish you may make (لاَ تُشْرِكُوا) a prohibition on which you have brought in (أن); and if you wish you may make it a statement (khabar), with (تشِركوا) in the position of the accusative; as when you say: "أمرتك ألاَّ تذهبَ إلى زيد" ("I commanded you not to go to Zayd") (accusative), and "أن لا تذهبْ" (jussive). And if you wish you may make what you have joined on to (أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُوا بِه) partly jussive and partly accusative; as He said: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّى أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾: He put the first of it in the accusative and prohibited in the last of it; as the poet said:
حجَّ وأوصى بسليمى الأعبدا * ألاّ ترى ولا تكلمْ أحدا * ولا تُمَشِّ بفَضاء بعدَا
(He went on pilgrimage and charged the slaves concerning Sulaymā: that she should see no one, and "speak to no one, and do not walk in open country afterwards".)
He intended a statement in its first part and a prohibition in its last. He said: and the jussive in this verse is dearer to me because of His saying: (وَأَوفُوا الْكَيْلَ); so I made its first part a prohibition because of His saying: (وَأَوفُوا الْكَيْلَ).

farraa:153-153.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً﴾: you put kasra on إنّ when you intend a resumption (istiʾnāf), and fatḥa because (أتل) falls on it. And if you wish you may make it genitive, meaning ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ﴾ and [by] ﴿وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ﴾ means Judaism and Christianity. He says: do not follow them, or you will go astray.

farraa:154-154.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ تَمَاماً عَلَى ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ﴾: as a completion for the one who does good. And "the one who does good" may have the sense of a plural; as He said: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (تَمَاماً عَلَى الذِين أحسنوا), confirming that.
And if you wish you may make (الذى) in the sense of (ما), meaning: as a completion for what Moses did well, so that the meaning is: as a completion for his good-doing. And (أحسن) may be nominative, meaning: for the one who is best [i.e. الذى هو أحسنُ]; and you put (أحسن) in the accusative [form] here while intending the genitive by it; because the Arabs say: "مررت بالذى هوخير منك وشر منك" ("I passed by the one who is better than you, and worse than you"), but they do not say "مررت بالذى قائم"; because "خيرا منك" is like a definite noun, since alif and lām do not enter it. Likewise they say: "مررت بالذى أخيك" and "بالذى مثلِك" ("by the one who is your brother", "by the one who is like you"); when they make the ṣila (relative clause) of الذى a definite noun, or an indefinite noun that alif and lām do not enter, they make it follow الذى [in case]. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
إن الزُّبيرىَّ الذى مِثْلَ الحَلَمْ * مَشَّى بأسلابك فى أهل العَلَم
(The Zubayrid, the one who is like a tick, paraded your spoils among the people of the banner.)

farraa:155-155.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ﴾: you have made "blessed" a naʿt (adjective) of the Book, so you put it in the nominative. If you put it in the accusative, as departing from the hāʾ in (أَنْزَلْنَاهُ) [i.e. as a ḥāl], it would be correct.

farraa:156-156.t: His saying: ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ﴾: (أن) is in the position of the accusative from two directions. One of them: We sent it down lest you say: "it was only sent down…". The other is from His saying: "and beware lest you say". (لا) is fit in the place of (أن) here, like His saying: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾, in which (لا تضلون) is fit; as He said: ﴿سَلَكْنَاهُ فِى قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ. لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾.

farraa:158-158.t: His saying: ﴿ هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾: to take their souls; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ﴾: the Resurrection; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ﴾: the rising of the sun from its place of setting.

farraa:159-159.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ﴾: ʿAlī read it (فارقوا), and said: "By Allah, they did not divide it, but they abandoned it." They are the Jews and the Christians. The people read it (فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ), and each is a valid reading.
His saying: ﴿لَّسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ﴾: He says: you have nothing to do with fighting them; then it was abrogated by: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾.

farraa:160-160.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾: whoever reads the genitive means: he will have ten good deeds like it. And if He had said here "فله عشر مِثْلِها", meaning ten good deeds like it, it would be correct. Whoever says "عشْرٌ أَمثالها" makes them a naʿt (adjective) of the ten. And (مثل) may be singular: you say in speech of this kind "هم مثلكم" and "أمثالكم" ("they are like you"); Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿إِنكم إِذاً مثلهم﴾, using the singular, and said: ﴿ثم لا يكونوا أَمثالكم﴾, using the plural. And if you said "عَشْرٌ أمثالها", as you say "عندى خمسةٌ أثوابٌ" ("I have five garments"), it would be permissible.
His saying: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾: with "there is no god but Allah"; and the evil deed: associating partners [with Allah].

farraa:161-161.t: His saying: ﴿دِيناً قِيَماً﴾ and "قَيِّما". Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me from a man from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudhayfa, he said: My father Ḥudhayfa saw me bowing with my head lowered; he said: "Raise your head — an upright religion (دينا قيما)." (دينا قيما) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and (مِلةَ إِبراهِيم) likewise.

farraa:165-165.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلاَئِفَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: the community of Muhammad ﷺ was made the successors of all the nations; ﴿ورفع بعضكم فوق بعضٍ درجاتٍ﴾ in provision, (لِيبلوكم) by that (فِيما آتاكم).

farraa:6-6.t: His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ﴾ — a qarn (generation) is eighty years; some have said: seventy.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾ — if you wish, you can make (الرحمة) the end of a statement and then begin afresh after it with (ليَجْمَعَنَّكم). And if you wish, you can treat it [the following clause] as being in the position of the accusative, as He said: ﴿كَتَب ربكم على نفسِهِ الرحمة أَنه من عمل مِنكم﴾. With the words that admit the answer of an oath, the Arabs use both «أن» with fatḥa and the lām. So they say: "arsaltu ilayhi an yaqūma" ("I sent to him that he should stand"), and "arsaltu ilayhi la-yaqūmanna" ("I sent to him [saying] he shall surely stand").
Likewise His saying: ﴿ثم بدا لهم مِن بعدِ ما رأَوُا الآياتِ ليسجُنُنَّهُ﴾, and this is frequent in the Quran. Do you not see that if you said "badā lahum an yasjunūhu" ("it occurred to them to imprison him"), it would be correct?

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ — [«فاطر»] is genitive in its case: you make it one of the attributes of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Had you put it in the accusative as praise, it would have been correct, since it is definite. And had you intended "fāṭiran" in the sense of "creator" [i.e. as an indefinite participle], you would put it in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), since it has no alif-lām. Had you begun afresh and put it in the nominative, it would have been correct, as He said: (ربُّ السمواتِ والأَرضِ وما بينهما الرحمن).

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ﴾ — everything that subdues something is above it.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿لأُنذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَن بَلَغَ﴾ — He means: and whomever the Quran reaches after you. (بلغ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من), and (من) is put in the accusative by the warning.
His saying: ﴿آلِهَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾ — He did not say "ukhar" (plural), because «الآلهة» is a plural, and (a plural) can be treated as feminine [singular], as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿ولِلّهِ الأَسماءُ الحسنى﴾, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿فما بال القُرونِ الأُولى﴾, and did not say "al-uwal" or "al-awwalīn". All of that is correct.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَآءَهُمُ﴾ — it is mentioned that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to ʿAbdallāh ibn Salām: "What is this recognition by which you recognise Muhammad ﷺ?" He said: "By Allah, when I see him I know him better than I know my own son while he is playing with the boys; for I have no doubt about him that he is Muhammad ﷺ, whereas I do not know what the women may have done regarding the son." So this recognition is by his description in their Book.
The exegesis has come concerning His saying: ﴿خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ — it is said: there is no believer and no unbeliever but he has a dwelling in Paradise, and a family and spouses. Whoever embraces Islam and is felicitous goes to his dwelling and his spouses, (and whoever disbelieves, his dwelling and his spouses go) to the one who embraced Islam and was felicitous. That is His saying ﴿الذِين يَرِثُون الفِردوسَ﴾ — He is saying: they inherit the dwellings of the unbelievers; and that is His saying: ﴿الذِين خسِروا أنفسهم وأهليهم﴾.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — it is read «ربِّنَا» and «ربَّنا», in the genitive and the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, related to me from al-Aʿmash, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama, that he read (واللّهِ ربَّنا), and said: its meaning is "By Allah, O our Lord." Whoever says (ربِّنا) makes it [part of] what is sworn by.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَلدَّارُ ٱلآخِرَةُ﴾ — «الدار» is made a noun here and «الآخرة» is made its description, while in other places it is put in a construct [«دار الآخرة»]. Similar to it, among things annexed to what is like them in meaning, is His saying ﴿إِنّ هذا لهو حَقُّ اليَقِين﴾: "the truth" is "the certainty", just as "the abode" is "the hereafter". Likewise "I came to you bāriḥata al-ūlā" and "al-bāriḥata al-ūlā" ("the night before last"). And of it is "yawm al-khamīs" ("the day of Thursday") and "laylat al-khamīs". A thing is annexed to itself when its wording differs, just as «الحق» and «اليقين», «الدار» and «الآخرة», and «اليوم» and «الخميس» differ.
When they agree, the Arabs do not say "ḥaqq al-ḥaqq" or "yaqīn al-yaqīn", because when the two differ in wording they fancy that they differ in meaning. Similar to it is, in the reading of ʿAbdallāh, (وذلك الدِين القَيِّمة), and in our reading (دِين القَيِّمة). Al-qayyim and al-qayyima are like your saying "a man who is a rāwiya (great transmitter) and a wahhāba (great giver) of wealth", alongside wahhāb and rāwin, and the like.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾ — the generality read it with the doubled form. He said: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Asadī related to me from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, from Nājiya ibn Kaʿb, from ʿAlī, that he read (يُكْذِبونك), in the light form.
The meaning of the light form — and Allah knows best — is: they do not make you out to be a liar; they only mean that what you have brought is false. For they had never found him ﷺ to lie, so as to call him a liar (yukadhdhibūhu); rather they declared [what he brought] false (akdhabūhu), i.e. what you have brought is a lie that we do not recognise. Takdhīb is to say: "You have lied." And Allah knows best.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن ٱسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾ — "then do so" is implied; thus the exegesis has come, and that is its meaning. The Arabs do this only in every place where the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb) is known. Do you not see that you say to a man "If you are able to give charity…", "If you see fit to stand with us…", leaving out the apodosis, because you know that he knows it? But when there comes something whose apodosis is known only by its being expressed, you express it, as in your saying to a man: "If you stand, you will obtain good." In this there must be an apodosis, because its meaning is not known if it is dropped.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ﴾ — (الطائر) is genitive. Its nominative is permissible, (as you say: "mā ʿindī min) rajulin wa-lā imraʾatin" and "imraʾatun"; whoever uses the nominative means: "I have no man, and I have no woman." Likewise His saying: ﴿وما يعزُبُ عن ربِّك مِن مِثقالِ ذرةٍ﴾, after which He said (ولا أصغرَ مِن ذلك، ولا أَصغرُ ولا أَكبرَ، ولا أَكبرُ): if you put (أصغر) in the accusative [form], it is intended as genitive [being a diptote]; and whoever uses the nominative refers it back to the meaning.
As for His saying ﴿وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ﴾: a bird flies only with its two wings. In speech it is like His saying (له تِسع وتسعون نعجة [ولى نعجة] أنثى), and like your saying to a man: "I spoke to him with my own mouth," and "I walked to him on my own feet," for emphasis in speech.
It is said that every kind of animal is a community (umma). The Arabs say ṣinf [and ṣanf] (kind).
﴿ثم إِلى ربِّهِم يحشرون﴾ — their gathering is their death; then they are gathered with mankind and are told: "Be dust!" At that point the unbeliever wishes that he were dust like them.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُكُم﴾ — the Arabs have two usages and two meanings in (أرأيت).
One of them is that a man asks another: "Have you seen Zayd with your own eyes?" This is with the hamza. If you apply it to the man himself, you say: "a-raʾaytaka ʿalā ghayri hādhihi al-ḥāl?", meaning: "Have you seen yourself in a state other than this?" Then you make it dual and plural, saying to two men "a-raʾaytumākumā", to a group "a-raʾaytumūkum", to women "a-raʾaytunnakunna", and to a woman "a-raʾaytiki", with kasra on the tāʾ and the kāf; nothing but that is permissible.
The other meaning is that you say "a-raʾaytaka" meaning "Tell me" (and you pronounce it with hamza), giving the tāʾ fatḥa; or you leave out the hamza if you wish, which is most of the speech of the Arabs. And you leave the tāʾ singular with fatḥa for the masculine and feminine singular [and the plural, in] its feminine and masculine. So you say to a woman: "a-raʾaytaki Zaydan hal kharaja?" ("Tell me, has Zayd gone out?"), and to women: "a-raʾaytakunna Zaydan mā faʿala?" ("Tell me, what has Zayd done?"). The Arabs left the tāʾ singular only because they did not intend the action from it to fall upon the person himself; so they were content to mark the person in the kāf, and they directed the tāʾ toward the masculine and the singular, since the action did not fall [on an object]. The position of the kāf is accusative, but its interpretation is nominative; just as when you say to a man "dūnaka Zaydan" ("Take Zayd!"), you find the kāf genitive in wording but nominative in meaning, because it is the one commanded.
When the Arabs make the action of something fall upon itself, with the noun referred to by a pronoun, they say with the complete verbs something other than what they say with the deficient (nāqiṣa) ones. To a man one says: "You killed yourself (nafsaka)" and "You did good to yourself (nafsika)"; they do not say "qataltaka" or "aḥsanta ilayka". Thus Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فاقتلوا أنفسكم﴾, as in much of the Quran, like His saying ﴿وماظلمناهم ولكِن ظلموا أنفسهم﴾. But when the verb is deficient — like ḥasibtu and ẓanantu — they say: "aẓunnunī khārijan" ("I think myself to be going out"), "aḥsibunī khārijan", and "matā tarāka khārijan?" ("When do you see yourself going out?"); and they do not say "matā tarā nafsaka" or "matā taẓunnu nafsaka". That is because they wanted to distinguish between the verb that may be suspended (yulghā) and the verb whose suspension is not permissible. Do you not see that you say "anā — aẓunnu — khārijun" ("I am — I think — going out"), cancelling (أظنّ), so that the noun's own operator governs it? [Translator's note: «العفل» in the text is evidently a misprint for «الفعل».]
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has said ﴿إِن الإِنسان ليطغى. أَن رآه استغنى﴾, and did not say "raʾā nafsahu". In poetry "ḍarabtaka" or the like may occur with a complete verb. Of that is the poet's saying:
خُذَا حَذراً يا جارتىَّ فإننى * رأيتُ جِرَان العَوْدِ قد كاد يُصْلح
لقد كان لى فى ضَرّتين عدِمتُنى * وما كنت أَلقَى من رزينة أَبرحُ
(Take care, my two wives, for I have seen that the neck-hide of the old camel [i.e. the whip] is nearly ready. I had, in two co-wives — may I lose myself! — and in what I used to suffer from Razīna, more than enough distress.)
The Arabs say "ʿadimtunī" ("may I lose myself"), "wajadtunī" and "faqadtunī", but it is not the proper form of speech.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاۤ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُواْ﴾ — the meaning of (فلولا) is "why not then" (fa-hallā). It can also have the meaning of «لولا» [counterfactual], as though you said: "Were it not for ʿAbdallāh, I would strike you." If you see after it a single noun in the nominative, it is in the sense of the «لولا» whose apodosis has the lām; and if you do not see a noun after it, it is a question [an incitement], as in His saying: ﴿لولا أَخَّرْتَنِى إلى أَجلٍ قريب [فأصدّق وأَكُن مِنَ الصالِحِين]﴾ and His saying: ﴿فلولا إِن كنتم غير مدِينين [ترجِعونها إن كنتّم صادِقِين]﴾. Likewise (لوما) has in it what is in «لولا»: the question and the statement.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ — He means the gates of provision and rain, which is the good things of this world, in order to try them by it. It is like His saying: ﴿حتى إذا أخَذَتِ الأَرْضُ زُخْرُفها وازَّيَّنَتْ وظنّ أَهْلُها أنهم قادِرون عليها أتاها أَمْرُنا ليلا أَوْ نهارا﴾, and similar is ﴿وأن لوِ استقاموا على الطرِيقةِ لأسقيناهم ماءً غدَقا لِنفتِنهم فيه﴾ — the "way" is the way of shirk; i.e. had they persisted in it, We would have done that to them.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ مُّبْلِسُونَ﴾ — al-mublis is one who despairs, whose hope has been cut off. That is why it is said of someone who falls silent when his argument fails and he has no answer: "He has become mublis (ablasa)." The rajaz poet said:
يا صاحِ هل تعرف رَسْما مُكْرَسَا * قال نعم أعرِفه، وأبلسا
(O companion, do you recognise a trace [of an encampment] covered with dung? He said: Yes, I recognise it — and fell silent.)
i.e. he gave me no answer.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾ — [the pronoun] refers to the loss of hearing and sight and the sealing of hearts. When you refer to actions, even if they are many, you make the pronoun singular, as in your saying to a man: "Your coming and your going annoy (yuʾdhīnī) me." It is also said that the hāʾ in (به) refers to guidance; and it is like the first interpretation.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنذِرْ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَن يُحْشَرُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — He is saying: they fear being gathered to their Lord, knowing that it will happen. That is why the exegetes explained (يخافون) as "they know".

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ — someone may ask: how would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drive away anyone who calls upon his Lord, so that he should be forbidden that? It has reached us that ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī came in to the Prophet ﷺ while Salmān, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and their like were with him. ʿUyayna said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to put these away from you, the nobles of your people would come to you and embrace Islam." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ﴾.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكاً لَّجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلاً﴾ — in the form of a man, because they are not able to look upon the form of an angel.

harrat-mujtaba:115-115.t: «صدقا»: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The preposition «لكلماته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «لا», the lā of generic negation. The clause «لا مبدِّل لكلماته» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تمت», and the link between the ḥāl and the one it describes is achieved by the overt noun; the original is: لا مبدِّل لها. The clause «وهو السميع» is resumptive, and «العليم» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:116-116.t: «إن يتبعون»: «إن» is negating, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); «الظن» is the object; the clause is resumptive. The clause «يخرصون» is in the position of the nominative as a khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:117-117.t: «هو»: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and «أعلم» is the khabar (predicate) of inna. The relative noun «مَن» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. يعلم مَن. The clause «وهو أعلم» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «إن ربك».

harrat-mujtaba:118-118.t: The clause «فكلوا» is resumptive, and the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:119-119.t: His words «وما لكم»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The interpreted maṣdar «ألا تأكلوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition (في), i.e. "what thing has settled in preventing eating?" The clause «وقد فصَّل لكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تأكلوا». «ما» in his words «اضطررتم» is a relative noun, excepted, in the position of the accusative. The clause «وإن كثيرا ليضلون» is resumptive, and the preposition «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl from the wāw in «يضلون». The clause «إن ربك هو أعلم» is resumptive, and the clause «هو أعلم» is the khabar of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:120-120.t: The clause «إن الذين يكسبون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:121-121.t: The clause «وإنه لفسق» is conjoined to the clause «لا تأكلوا», with no grammatical position; conjoining a statement (khabar) to a performative (inshāʾ) is valid. The lām in «ليوحون» is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). The clause «وإن أطعتموهم» is conjoined to the clause «إن الشياطين ليوحون». The clause «إنكم لمشركون» is the answer to an implied oath, on the reading of «إنْ» as «لئن»; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, and the lām that prepares for the oath's answer (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa) was dropped.

harrat-mujtaba:122-122.t: (أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The hamza is for interrogation, and the wāw is resumptive. «مَن» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «كمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «مَن», i.e. "being like the one who". The clause «ليس بخارج» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun «مَن». The clause «زُيِّن» is resumptive, and the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "it was made fair-seeming to the disbelievers with a making-fair like that making-fair"; the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:123-123.t: «أكابر»: the first object of «جعلنا», and the preposition «في كل قرية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The clause «وما يمكرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يمكروا», and the clause «وما يشعرون» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يمكرون».

harrat-mujtaba:124-124.t: His words «الله أعلم»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «حيث» has left its adverbial function and become a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); what governs it is a verb indicated by «أعلم». It is not an adverb, because He the Exalted is not more knowing in one place than in another place; the implied form is: "He knows the place fit for placing His message". «صَغَار» is the fāʿil (agent), and the interpreted maṣdar «بما كانوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصيب».

harrat-mujtaba:125-125.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن يهديه» is the object of «يُرد». «حرجا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) multiplied: just as an explicit khabar (predicate) may be multiple, so may what was originally such. The clause «كأنما يصَّعَّد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «حرجا»; «كأنما» is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa), with no governing effect. The clause «يجعل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:126-126.t: «مستقيما»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «صراط». The clause «قد فَصَّلنا» is resumptive. The clause «يذَّكرون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:127-127.t: The clause «لهم دار السلام» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يذكرون», and likewise the clause «وهو وليهم».

harrat-mujtaba:128-128.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) «يقول», and the implied clause «يقول» is resumptive. «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يحشرهم». The clause «وقال» is conjoined to the implied one. The relative clause «الذي أجَّلتَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أجلنا». «خالدين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مثواكم». «إلا» is for exception, and «ما» is the excepted, connected (muttaṣil).

harrat-mujtaba:129-129.t: (وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «بعضا» is the second object. The clause «نولِّي» is resumptive, and the clause «كانوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.

harrat-mujtaba:130-130.t: The clause «ألم يأتكم» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive. The clause «يقصُّون» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «رسل». «لقاء» is the second object of أنذر. «هذا» is a naʿt of «يومكم». The interpreted maṣdar «أنهم كانوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:131-131.t: «ذا»: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "the matter". «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy (inna), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), its implied form being: أنه. The interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām, i.e. "that matter which We related is because it was not...". The preposition «بظلم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «مهلك», i.e. "involved in wrongdoing". The clause «وأهلها غافلون» is a ḥāl from «القرى», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:132-132.t: The preposition «مما عملوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «درجات». The clause «وما ربك بغافل» is conjoined to the resumptive clause at the start of the verse; «ما» is Ḥijāzī, and the bāʾ in its khabar (predicate) is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:133-133.t: «ذو»: a second khabar (predicate). The conditional clause is resumptive. «يذهبكم» became transitive through the entry of the hamza of transitivity on its past form «أَذْهَبَ». The kāf in «كما» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He will cause to succeed with a causing-to-succeed like His bringing you into being"; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «يشاء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the noun relative, and the clause «أنشأكم» is the ṣila of the particle relative.

harrat-mujtaba:134-134.t: «إن», its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). The clause «وما أنتم بمعجزين» is conjoined to the resumptive clause at the start of the verse, and the bāʾ in the khabar of «ما» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:135-135.t: The clause «إني عامل» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and likewise the clause «فسوف تعلمون» is resumptive. «مَنْ» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

harrat-mujtaba:136-136.t: The preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعلوا», and the first is «نصيبا». «من الحرث»: this preposition phrase is a badal (substitute) from «مما ذرأ», attached to what it is attached to; the first is attached to «جعلوا». The preposition «بزعمهم» is attached to «قالوا». «ما» in his words «فما كان» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject). The fāʾ in «فلا يصل» links the apodosis, and it entered upon an omitted detached pronoun, the implied form being: فهو لا يصل. The clause «فما كان» is conjoined to the clause «فقالوا». The clause «ساء ما يحكمون» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «ساء», and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "their judgement".

harrat-mujtaba:137-137.t: (وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "he made fair-seeming with a making-fair like that making-fair". His words «شركاؤهم»: the fāʿil (agent) of the verb (زيَّن), and the interpreted maṣdar «ليردوهم» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «زيَّن». The conditional clause «ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه» is conjoined to the clause «زيَّن», and the clause «فذَرْهم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:138-138.t: «مَنْ نشاء»: a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). The preposition «بزعمهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «قالوا». His words «أنعام حرمت»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and these are cattle"; the clause «حُرِّمت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أنعام». His words «وأنعام لا يذكرون»: a khabar, i.e. "and these are cattle", and the clause «لا يذكرون» is a naʿt of أنعام. «افتراء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the preposition is attached to a naʿt of «افتراء». The clause «سيجزيهم» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar «بما كانوا» is genitive, attached to «يجزيهم».

harrat-mujtaba:139-139.t: «ما»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خالصة» is its khabar (predicate). The preposition «في بطون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). His words «ومحرم»: conjoined to «خالصة». The clause «وإن يكن ميتة» is conjoined to the clause that is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «سيجزيهم وصفهم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنه حكيم عليم»; «وعليم» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:140-140.t: «سَفَهًا»: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «قتلوا». «افتراء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The clause «قد ضلُّوا» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:141-141.t: His words «وغير»: conjoined to «معروشات». «مختلفا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النخل»; «أكله» is the fāʿil (agent) of مختلف. «متشابها» is a ḥāl from «الرُّمَّان». His words «إذا أثمر»: conditional and adverbial, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the implied (muqaddar) apodosis, i.e. "when it bears fruit, then eat"; the clause «أثمر» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The conditional clause «إذا أثمر فكلوا» is resumptive, and the clause «إنه لا يحب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:142-142.t: The preposition «من الأنعام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. أنشأ; «حمولة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied verb أنشأ. The implied clause (وأنشأ) is conjoined to the earlier verb «أنشأ». The clause «كلوا» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنه عدو».

harrat-mujtaba:143-143.t: «ثمانية»: a badal (substitute) from «حمولة». The preposition «من الضأن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثنين», and «اثنين» is a badal from «ثمانية», and likewise what comes after it. «الذَّكَرَيْن» is an object placed before «حرَّم»; «أم» is a conjunction, and «الأنْثيين» is conjoined to «الذَّكرين», accusative with yāʾ. His words «أم ما اشتملت»: «أم» is a conjunction, and «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «الأنْثيين». The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:144-144.t: His words «ومن الإبل اثنين»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition phrase is conjoined to the preposition phrase «من الضأن»; «واثنين» is conjoined to «الضأن» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably meant: to «اثنين» of verse 143], and likewise its counterpart that follows. «أم» in his words «أم كنتم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), and the clause after it is resumptive. His words «إذ»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهداء». The clause «فمن أظلم» is resumptive; «مَن» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أظلم» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition is attached to «أظلم», and the interpreted maṣdar «ليضل» is genitive, attached to «افترى».

harrat-mujtaba:145-145.t: «محرما»: the object of «أجد», and the preposition «على طاعم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «محرما». The interpreted maṣdar «أن يكون» is excepted, disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). The fāʾ in «فإنه رجس» is parenthetical, and so is the clause. His words «أو فسقا»: conjoined to «لحم», and the clause «أُهِلَّ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «فسقا». The clause «فمن اضطر» is resumptive. «غير» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «اضطر»; «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), and «عادٍ» is a noun conjoined to «باغ».

harrat-mujtaba:146-146.t: The clause «حرَّمنا» is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «حرَّمنا»; the second «حرَّمنا» is conjoined to the first. «إلا» is for exception, and «ما» is a relative noun, excepted. The clause «ذلك جزيناهم» is resumptive; the bāʾ in «ببغيهم» is causal, and the clause «وإنَّا لصادقون» is conjoined to the verbal clause «جزيناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:147-147.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «ولا يُرَدُّ» is conjoined to the single word (mufrad) «ذو رحمة».

harrat-mujtaba:148-148.t: His words «ولا آباؤنا»: conjoined to the nominative pronoun «نا»; what permitted conjoining an overt noun to the pronoun is the presence of a separator, namely the negating particle. «شيء» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The kāf in «كذلك» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "those before them denied with a denial like that denial", and the clause «كذَّب» is resumptive. «عِلْم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِن» is redundant, and the adverb «عندكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The fāʾ in «فتخرجوه» is causal, and the verb is accusative by أن necessarily concealed; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "is there any knowledge with you, and so its bringing forth to us?" «إن» is negating and «إلا» is a particle of restriction; the clause «إن تتبعون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:149-149.t: His words «فلله»: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e. "so if the matter is as you claimed". The conditional clause after it, «فلو شاء», is conjoined to the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf in «هداكم».

harrat-mujtaba:150-150.t: «هلمَّ»: a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning "bring". The interpreted maṣdar «أن الله حرم» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. The clause «فإن شهدوا» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «قل». The clause «وهم يعدلون» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), as a case of conjoining a nominal clause to a verbal one.

harrat-mujtaba:151-151.t: «تعالوا»: an inflexible (jāmid) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn. «أتل» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), occurring as the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition; «أن» after it is explicative, and the clause «لا تشركوا» is explicative. The preposition «بالوالدين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb «أحسنوا», and «إحسانا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the implied clause «أحسنوا» is conjoined to «لا تشركوا». The clause «نحن نرزقهم» is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. His words «إياهم»: a detached accusative pronoun conjoined to the kāf in «نرزقكم». His words «ما ظهر»: a relative noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «الفواحش». The preposition «بالحق» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تقتلوا». The clause «ذلكم وصَّاكم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «لعلكم تعقلون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:152-152.t: The preposition «بالقسط» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object. The clause «لا نكلف نفسا» is parenthetical, and «وسعها» is a second object. The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «أوفوا». The wāw in «ولو كان» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), conjoining to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "be just in every state, even in this state"; this is for exhausting all the states. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The noun of kāna is implied, "he", referring to the one spoken about. The clause «ذلكم وصَّاكم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «لعلكم تذكَّرون».

harrat-mujtaba:153-153.t: The interpreted maṣdar «وأن هذا صراطي» is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I recite to you", and the implied clause is conjoined to «أتل» in verse 151. «مستقيما»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «صراطي», accusative. The clause «فاتبعوه» is conjoined to the clause «وأن هذا صراطي». The fāʾ in «فتفرَّق» is causal, and the verb is accusative by a concealed أن; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there not be from you a following of the paths, and so a scattering". The clause «ذلكم وصَّاكم» is resumptive, and likewise «لعلكم تتقون».

harrat-mujtaba:154-154.t: «تماما»: stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "We completed a completing", and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «تماما». The clause «لعلهم يؤمنون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:155-155.t: The clause «أنزلناه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», and «مبارك» is a second naʿt. The clause «فاتبعوه» is conjoined to the clause «وهذا كتاب». The clause «لعلكم ترحمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:156-156.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن تقولوا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of aversion", and what governs it is an implied (muqaddar) «أنزلناه», not the one actually uttered, so that the governor and what it governs are not separated by an extraneous element, namely «مبارك». The preposition «من قبلنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «طائفتين». «إنْ» is lightened from the heavy (inna) and inoperative, and the lām with it is the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa) between it and the negating إن. «غافلين» is the khabar (predicate) of «كنا». The clause «وإن كنا» is conjoined to the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:157-157.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أَنَّا أُنزلَ» is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) «ثبت», i.e. "if a sending down were established". The clause «فقد جاءكم» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are truthful, then there has come to you". The preposition «من ربكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of «بيِّنة». The clause «فمن أظلم» is resumptive, made up of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The clause «سنجزي» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar «بما كانوا» is genitive by the bāʾ, attached to «نجزي».

harrat-mujtaba:158-158.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن تأتيهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «نفسا» is an object, and «إيمانها» is a fāʿil (agent) placed later. The clause «لا ينفع» is resumptive, and the clause «لم تكن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «نفسا». «خيرا» is the mafʿūl bihi of «كسبت». The clause «قل» is resumptive. The clause «إنا منتظرون» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:159-159.t: The preposition «في شيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the notion of being settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached. The clause «إنما أمرهم إلى الله» is resumptive, and the clause «ينبئهم» is conjoined to the resumptive clause. The relative «بما كانوا» is genitive, attached to «ينبئهم».

harrat-mujtaba:160-160.t: «مَن»: a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «جاء» is the khabar (predicate). The clause «فلا يُجْزَى» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), on the implied form فهو لا يُجزى; the clause «يُجزى» is the khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ. The nominal clause «وهم لا يظلمون» is conjoined to the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:161-161.t: «دينا»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb «الزموا», concealed; «قيما» is a naʿt (adjective), «ملة» is a badal (substitute) from «دينا», and «حنيفا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «إبراهيم». A ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is permitted because the muḍāf ilayhi is like a part of the muḍāf. The clause «وما كان» is conjoined to the wording of the ḥāl «حنيفا», as a case of conjoining a clause to a single word.

harrat-mujtaba:162-162.t: The preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna. «رب» is a badal (substitute), genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:163-163.t: The clause «لا شريك له» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رب العالمين». The clause «أُمرت» is resumptive, and the clause «وأنا أول» is conjoined to the resumptive clause, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:164-164.t: «غير»: an object placed before «أبغي», and «ربا» is a tamyīz (specification). The clause «وهو رب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the Divine Name. «إلا» is for restriction; the preposition «عليها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl from the omitted object, i.e. "no soul earns a sin except as being thrown back upon it". The clause «ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم» is conjoined to the clause «لا تَزِرُ», and the clause «ينبئكم» is conjoined to the nominal clause «ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم».

harrat-mujtaba:165-165.t: «درجات»: a second object, on «رفع» being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of بَلَّغَ (to make reach). The interpreted maṣdar «ليبلوكم» is genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) رفع. The clause «إن ربك سريع العقاب» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون» is conjoined to the initial clause «الحمد لله». The preposition phrase «بربهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعدلون».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «وأجل مسمى عنده» is conjoined to the clause «قضى أجلا», with no grammatical position; beginning with the indefinite noun «أجل» is permitted because it is qualified. The clause «ثم أنتم تمترون» is conjoined to the clause «هو الذي خلقكم».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition phrase «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the Divine Name, because of the meaning of "the One worshipped" that it contains. The clause «يعلم» is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «من آية» is the fāʿil (agent), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); a past verb may occur after «إلا» because it comes after a verb; and the clause «كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «تأتيهم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «فقد كذبوا» is resumptive, and the clause «لما جاءهم» is parenthetical between the conjoined items, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being omitted, what precedes indicating it; the clause «فسوف يأتيهم» is conjoined to the clause «فقد كذبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «كم» is predicative (khabariyya), a fronted object, and the preposition phrase «من قرن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective (ṣifa) of «كم»; the clause «أهلكنا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يروا», «كم» having suspended the seeing from operating. The clause «مكنَّاهم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قرن», and the pronoun refers back to it in the plural according to its meaning. His saying «ما لم نمكن لكم»: «ما» is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, i.e.: a thing that We did not establish for you, in the position of the accusative as a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause «لم نمكن» is an adjective of the implied «شيئًا». «مدرارًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «السماء», and the clause «فأهلكناهم» is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: they disbelieved, so We destroyed them.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The preposition phrase «في قرطاس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كتابًا»; «إن» is negating; «هذا سحر» are mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «ولو أنزلنا ملكًا» is resumptive, and the clause «لا ينظرون» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His saying «للبسنا عليهم»: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is for strengthening the link, and «ما» is a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «ولقد استهزئ برسل» is resumptive, and the clause «لقد استهزئ» is the reply to the oath, with no grammatical position. «ما» in His saying «ما كانوا» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «حاق», and the clause «فحاق» is conjoined to the clause «استهزئ», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition phrase «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The preposition phrase «لله» is attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it belongs to Allah. The clause «كتب» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause «(والله) ليجمعنَّكم» is resumptive, and the clause «ليجمعنكم» is the reply to the oath; the clause «لا ريب فيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «يوم القيامة», in the position of the accusative. His saying «الذين خسروا»: mubtadaʾ, and the clause «فهم لا يؤمنون» is the khabar; the redundant fāʾ may be attached to the khabar because the relative is likened to the conditional.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «وله ما سكن» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause «وهو السميع» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «غير» is the first object of «أتخذ», «وليًا» is the second object, and «فاطر» is a badal (substitute) of the Divine Name, even though a badal from derived words is uncommon. The clause «وهو يطعم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the position of the accusative, of the Divine Name. The interpreted maṣdar «أن أكون» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. His saying «من أسلم»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «ولا تكونن» is conjoined to the clause «قل», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «إن عصيت ربي» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: if I disobeyed Him, punishment would befall me.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «يومئذ» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُصْرَف»; «إذٍ» is an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its tanwīn is in compensation for a clause. The clause «وذلك الفوز» is resumptive; it is a nominal clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: His saying «فلا كاشف»: the fāʾ is linking; [«لا» is] the lā of generic negation and [«كاشف» is] its noun; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); and «هو» is a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in the omitted khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «فوق» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate), and «الخبير» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «أَيُّ»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is «أكبر», and «شهادة» is tamyīz (specification). The adverb «بيني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهيد», and the clause «وأوحي إليَّ هذا القرآن» is conjoined to the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). His saying «مَنْ بلغ»: a relative noun conjoined to the kāf. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن مع الله آلهة» is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ), and «مع» is an adverb of place attached to the khabar. The clause «أئنكم لتشهدون» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «قل لا أشهد»; the preposition phrase «مما تشركون» is attached to «بريء»; and the clause «وإنني بريء» is conjoined to the content of what is said.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «يعرفونه» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; the kāf in «كما» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e.: they know him with a knowing like the knowing of their sons; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «فهم لا يؤمنون» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين», the fāʾ being joined to the khabar because the relative is likened to the conditional.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive; «مَنْ» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أظلم» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; and the hāʾ in «إنه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and its clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: His saying «ويوم»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied «اتقوا» (beware), and the clause «اتقوا» is resumptive; «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun «هم»; «أين» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied khabar (predicate); «شركاؤكم» is mubtadaʾ (subject); and «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن قالوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان»; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «ربنا» is a badal (substitute) of the Divine Name; the clause «لم تكن فتنتهم» is conjoined to the clause «نقول»; and the clause «ما كنا» is the reply to the oath, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «كيف كَذَبوا» is a clause in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb «انظر», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. «ما» is the fāʿil (agent) of «ضل», and the clause «ضلَّ» is conjoined to the clause «كذبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «وجعلنا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative; the ḥāl-wāw may be joined to a past verb. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يفقهوه» is mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: out of dislike. The preposition phrase «في آذانهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «وَقْرًا», and «وقرًا» is conjoined to «أكنَّة». «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the conditional clause after it is resumptive; the clause «يجادلونك» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «جاءوك», and the clause «يقول» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وإن يهلكون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «ينأون», «إن» being negating; and the clause «وما يشعرون» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «يهلكون», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: (ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: you would see something terrible; the clause «وُقِفوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The wāw in His saying «ولا نكذب» is for accompaniment (maʿiyya), and the verb is accusative by «أن» necessarily concealed after it; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: would that there were for us a return and an absence of denial; and the clause «نكذِّب» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī), with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «بل بدا ما كانوا» is resumptive; the conditional clause is conjoined to the resumptive one; and the clause «وإنهم لكاذبون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: (إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «إن» is negating, without governing effect (muhmala), and the clause «وما نحن بمبعوثين» is conjoined to the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: you would see something terrible. The clause «قال» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the reply to the oath is implied, i.e.: yes, by Allah, it is indeed the truth. The clause «ولو ترى» is conjoined to the clause «لو ترى» in verse (27). The fāʾ in His saying «فذوقوا» links to the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you have disbelieved, then taste; the implied conditional clause and its apodosis are the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative, and the clause «فذوقوا» is the apodosis, in the position of the jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); «إذا» is an adverbial conditional attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قالوا»; and the clause is resumptive. «بغتة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «وهم يحملون أوزارهم» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «قالوا». His saying «ألا ساء ما يزرون»: «ألا» is a particle of opening and drawing attention, [«ساء» is] a past verb, and the relative is its fāʿil; the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e.: that burden of theirs; and the clause of blame is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: His saying «وللدار»: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is for emphasis, and [then come] mubtadaʾ (subject), its naʿt (adjective) and its khabar (predicate). The clause is conjoined to the resumptive one, and the clause «أفلا تعقلون» is resumptive; the hamza is placed first because it has the right to the head of the clause (al-ṣadāra).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The hamza of «إن» is given a kasra because of the presence of the lām in the khabar (predicate), and the clause «إنه ليحزنك» stands in place of the two objects of «نعلم». The relative «الذي» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يحزن». The clause «فإنهم لا يكذبونك» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause «ولكن الظالمين يجحدون» is conjoined to the clause «فإنهم لا يكذبونك». The preposition phrase «بآيات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يجحدون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسل». The clause «ولا مبدِّل لكلمات الله» is resumptive, and the clause «ولقد جاءك» is resumptive. The fāʿil (agent) of «جاءك» is implied, i.e.: the news; the preposition phrase «من نبإ» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied «الخبر»; and «المرسلين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive, and the noun of «كان» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «كبر إعراضهم» is in the position of the accusative as khabar (predicate) of «كان».
