(على): a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (اشتملت). (أرحام): fāʿil, nominative. (الأنثيين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ. (نبّئوا): imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil, (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (بعلم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نبئوني). (إن): a jussive conditional particle. (كنتم): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogating verb (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the sukūn «[Note: In the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).]», and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of كان. (صادقين): khabar, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «حرّم» is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اشتملت.... أرحام» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «نبئوني....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: resumptive … and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then inform me with knowledge".
(144) (الواو): conjunction. (من الإبل اثنين ... أرحام الأنثيين): see the i'rab of its like, من الضأن اثنين ..., above. (أم): the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل together with the hamza. (كنتم): like the first. (شهداء): khabar of كنتم, accusative, barred from tanwīn because it is assimilated to words ending in the extended feminine alif, on the pattern فعلاء. (إذ): an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to شهداء. (وصّى): past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (الباء): a preposition. (ها): for alerting (tanbīh). (ذا): demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (وصّاكم). (الفاء): resumptive. (من): interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (أظلم): khabar, nominative. (من): a preposition. (من): relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to أظلم. (افترى): like وصّى, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), the referring pronoun. (على الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (افترى). (كذبا): mafʿūl bihi, accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its synonym, i.e. افترى افتراء.]». (اللام): of purpose (taʿlīl). (يضلّ): imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (هو). (الناس): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (بغير): a preposition and its genitive noun, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl governed by يضلّ «[Note: Or governed by افترى.]», i.e. "he misleads them while ignorant". (علم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (إنّ الله لا يهدي القوم): like إنه لا يحب المسرفين «[Note: In verse (141) of this sura.]». (الظالمين): naʿt of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «حرّم....» is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «اشتملت ... أرحام» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «كنتم شهداء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «وصاكم الله....» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «من أظلم....» has no grammatical position: resumptive «[Note: It may be the apodosis of an implied condition, linked to what precedes it by a causal link, i.e. "if you speak about Allah other than the truth, then how great is your wrongdoing".]».
The clause «افترى....» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إن الله لا يهدي....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إن.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضل ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām of purpose, attached to (افترى).

* Morphology:
(حمولة): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for all beasts that carry loads, especially the large ones; its pattern is فعولة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(فرشا): a collective noun for small beasts … Abū Zayd said: it may be a naming by the maṣdar (verbal noun), because it is originally a maṣdar, and it is shared among many meanings. It is said that small beasts were called فرش because from their wool, fur and hair is made what is spread out (yufrash), and this is the point of benefit.
(الضأن): it is said to be the plural of ضائن for the male and ضائنة for the female, and it is said to be a collective noun; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(المعز): what was said about الضأن is said about المعز; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn….
In al-Miṣbāḥ: المعز is a generic noun (ism jins) with no singular from its own root; it is the hairy kind of small cattle; the singular is شاة, which is feminine. The ʿayn takes fatḥa or sukūn. The plural of the form with sukūn is أمعز and معيز, like عبد, أعبد and عبيد. In المعزى the alif is for assimilation (ilḥāq), not for the feminine; hence it takes tanwīn when indefinite and its diminutive is معيز … Also in it: العنز is the female of المعز once a year has passed over it.
(الإبل): a collective noun with no singular from its own root; its pattern is فعل, with two kasras; its plural is آبال.

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ», the speech is a denial that Allah the Exalted forbade them anything of these four kinds, and an exposure of their lying in that. The detailing of what is mentioned — the males and females and what is in their wombs — is for hyperbole in refuting them, by directing the denial at every single item of their fabrication.

safi-cedvel:145-145.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you". (لا) a particle of negation. (أجد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "I". (في) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أجد). (أوحي) a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, implied as "it", and it is the referent pronoun. (إلى) a preposition, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أوحي). (محرّما) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governing word is أجد, accusative (manṣūb); it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "something forbidden". (على طاعم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (محرّما). (يطعم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object; the fāʿil is "he". (إلا) a particle of exception. (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle. (يكون) an incomplete imperfect verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — in the subjunctive (manṣūb); its noun is a latent pronoun, implied as "it", i.e. the forbidden thing. (ميتة) its predicate, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون) is in the position of accusative as the excepted of a disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) or a conjoined (muttaṣil) exception, there being a difference of opinion on that [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) of (محرّما), in the position of accusative.].
(أو) a conjunction. (دما) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ميتة, accusative [Note: Or to the interpreted maṣdar that is accusative as the excepted; likewise the rest of the conjoined nouns.]. (مسفوحا) a naʿt of (دما), accusative. (أو) like the first. (لحم) conjoined to ميتة, accusative. (خنزير) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) causal. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (رجس) its khabar (predicate), nominative. (أو) like the first. (فسقا) conjoined to ميتة, accusative. (أهلّ) a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "it". (لغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أهلّ). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أهلّ). (الفاء) resumptive. (من) a conditional noun causing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (اضطر) like أهلّ, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (غير) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the deputy agent, accusative. (باغ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation. (عاد) conjoined to باغ and parsed like it. (الفاء) causal. (إن ربك غفور) like إنه رجس. (رحيم) a second predicate, nominative.
The clause «قل....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا أجد....» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أوحي إليّ....» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يطعمه» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of طاعم.
The clause «يكون....» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنه رجس....» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, giving the cause.
The clause «أهلّ ... » is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (فسقا).
The clause «من اضطرّ ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اضطر ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «إن ربك غفور» has no grammatical position: causal ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then there is no blame on him".

* Morphology:
(أجد): it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by omission: the first radical (fāʾ) was omitted because it is a mithāl weak verb (first radical weak) whose imperfect has kasra on the middle radical; its original form is أوجد ... Its pattern is أعل.
(طاعم): active participle of the triliteral طعم يطعم; its pattern is فاعل.
(مسفوحا): passive participle of the triliteral سفح, on the pattern مفعول.

* Benefits:
1- The foods forbidden in Islam, as in this verse, are four: carrion, blood poured out and shed, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than Allah.
As for the Jews, other things were forbidden to them because of their transgression and their departure from what they were commanded; whoever wants the details should refer to the sources of jurisprudence and legislation.

safi-cedvel:146-147.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (على) a preposition. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حرمنا). (هادوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma .... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (حرّمنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (ونا) a pronoun, the fāʿil. (كلّ) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (ذي) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ. (ظفر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) a conjunction. (من البقر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the (حرّمنا) that follows. (الواو) a conjunction. (الغنم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to البقر, genitive. (حرّمنا) like the first. (عليهم) a preposition and a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the second (حرّمنا). (شحوم) a direct object, accusative, and (هما) a pronoun in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا) a particle of exception. (ما) a relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows (nakira mawṣūfa), in the position of accusative.], indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the excepted. (حملت) a past verb .... and (التاء) for the feminine. (ظهور) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هما) like the first. (أو) a conjunction. (الحوايا) conjoined to ظهورهما [Note: What the backs carry, what the entrails carry and what is mixed with bone was not forbidden.], nominative; the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif [Note: (الحوايا) may be conjoined to ما, so it is in the position of accusative, or to الشحوم, so that they too are forbidden.]. (أو) a conjunction. (ما اختلط) like ما حملت and conjoined to it; the fāʿil is "it", the referent pronoun. (بعظم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اختلط). (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object whose governing word is جزيناهم ... or it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is that".]; the reference is to the prohibition, (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (جزينا) like حرّمنا, and (هم) a pronoun, direct object. (ببغي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جزينا); the bāʾ is causal, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) resumptive. (إن) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (صادقون) the khabar of inna, nominative; the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «هادوا....»: no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «حرّمنا (the first): no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «حرّمنا (the second)»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «حملت ظهورهما»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first relative (ما). The clause «اختلط....»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «ذلك جزيناهم»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «جزيناهم ... »: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك); the linking pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "for it" (به) [Note: If the demonstrative is the object of the verb, the verbal clause is resumptive.].
The clause «إنّا لصادقون»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
(147) (الفاء) a conjunction. (إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (كذّبوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, direct object. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil is "you". (ربّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ذو) khabar, nominative; the sign of the nominative is the wāw. (رحمة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (واسعة) a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة, genitive. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) a particle of negation. (يردّ) a passive imperfect verb, nominative. (بأس) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (عن القوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يردّ). (المجرمين) a naʿt of القوم, genitive; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «كذّبوك»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the earlier resumptive clause [Note: قل لا أجد, in verse (145) of this surah; in that case what lies between them is a parenthesis.].
The clause «قل....»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ربكم ذو رحمة....»: in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا يردّ بأسه ... »: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the speech reported [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, resumptive, if the speech goes outside the scope of what the Messenger (ṣ) says.].

* Morphology:
(ظفر): a primitive (jāmid) noun; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas. It has other dialectal forms: ظفر with ḍamma then sukūn, ظفر with two kasras, ظفر with kasra then sukūn, and أظفور with ḍamma on the hamza. The plural of the triliteral is أظفار, and the plural of أظفور is أظافير and أظافر.
(الغنم): a generic noun (ism jins) whose singular is شاة; it has the form of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb غنم, of the فرح class; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(شحوم): plural of شحم, a primitive noun for fat; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; a piece of it is شحمة.
(الحوايا): plural of حاوياء or حاوية; حويّة, like هديّة, is also permissible. If the singular is حاويا or حاوية, the pattern of الحوايا is فواعل, and the original form is حواوي, like صواري: the second wāw was changed into a hamza with fatḥa, حواءي; the yāʾ was voweled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, حواءى; then the hamza was changed into a yāʾ because it fell between two alifs, giving حوايا.
If the singular is حويّة, the pattern of الحوايا is فعائل, like طرائق, and the original form is حوائي: the hamza was changed into a yāʾ with kasra, then that yāʾ was given fatḥa, then the second yāʾ, which is the final radical (lām) of the word, was changed into an alif, so it became حوايا.
[Translator's note: The source lists the singulars as حاوياء or حاوية and then says "if the singular is حاويا or حاوية"; translated as written.]
(عظم): a noun for the well-known body part, primitive; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; its singular (unit noun) is عظمة, on the measure فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted, «ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ»: there are several views on the i'rab of ذلك. It is said: a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that prohibition — We recompensed them with it". It is said: it is accusative as a maṣdar, since there is something similar in the speech of the Arabs, as in their saying ظننت ذلك, i.e. that supposition. And it is said: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that".
Each of these views has its opponents, so choose; for i'rab goes back to the taste and judgement of the one parsing, provided that it does not conflict with the intended meaning of the speech.
I say: the preferred view in my opinion is the first, and its implied form is: "that prohibition — We recompensed them with it", with the preposition and its genitive noun omitted, as it is understood from the context of the speech.

safi-cedvel:106-107.t:
* I'rab:
(اتبع) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت). (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: Some allowed (ما) to be a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the object of اتّبع; in that case the preposition and its genitive noun become the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).]». (أوحي) a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), and it is the referent (ʿāʾid) — i.e. the Qurʾan. (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحي). (من رب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوحي) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil.]», and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لا إله إلا هو) its i'rab has just been given «[Note: In āya (102) of this sūra.]». (الواو) conjunction. (أعرض) like اتّبع. (عن المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعرض), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «اتبع....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أوحي ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا إله إلا هو»: has no grammatical position, parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses, emphasizing the obligation to follow the revelation in the matter of tawḥīd (Divine Oneness) «[Note: It may be parsed as a ḥāl of (ربّك), i.e. from your Lord, alone (in His Oneness).]».
The clause «أعرض....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اتبع.
(107) (الواو) conjunction. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (شاء) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (ما) negative. (أشركوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (ما جعلنا) like ما أشركوا, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (حفيظا). (الواو) conjunction. (ما أنت عليهم بوكيل) the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded «[Note: In āya (104) of this sūra.]».
The clause «شاء الله....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause ...
The object of شاء is omitted, i.e. "Allah had willed their belief".
The clause «ما أشركوا»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما جعلناك....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause شاء الله «[Note: It may be conjoined to the clause ما أشركوا, and so it too has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «ما أنت.... بوكيل»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما جعلناك.

safi-cedvel:108-108.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive «[Translator's note: the source prints ناهبة, evidently a misprint for ناهية (prohibitive).]». (تسبوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn .... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) .... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted referent (ʿāʾid) or of the relative noun itself. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya). (يسبوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ «[Note: The verb may be jussive, coordinated and conjoined to the verb of prohibition (لا تسبّوا).]», and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (عدوّا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because ʿadw (transgression) coincides with sabb (reviling) in meaning ... It may also be an emphatic ḥāl, i.e. "they revile Allah, transgressing".]». (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an emphatic ḥāl, i.e. "being ignorant". (علم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسبوا) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no reviling of their gods on your part, lest there be reviling of Allah on theirs".
(الكاف) a preposition. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is (زيّنا), i.e. "We have adorned for every community an adorning like the adorning for these" «[Note: If the kāf is a noun, it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its description.]» ... and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (زيّنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and its fāʿil «[Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source; the fāʿil is (نا).]». (لكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (زينا). (أمة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (عمل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ثم) a conjunction. (إلى رب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (مرجع) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) conjunction. (ينبئ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of the genitive ... It may also be an indefinite noun qualified by a description, the clause after it being a naʿt (adjective) of it.]», indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينبئهم), and the referent is omitted. (كانوا) a deficient (nāqiṣ) abrogating past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (يعملون) like يدعون.
The clause «لا تسبوا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يدعون....»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يسبوا....»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «زيّنا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إلى ربهم مرجعهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to an omitted clause, i.e.:
"so they did it, then to their Lord is their return".
The clause «ينبئهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إلى ربهم مرجعهم.
The clause «كانوا يعملون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the referent is omitted, i.e. "they used to do it".
The clause «يعملون»: in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.

* Morphology:
(عدوا): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb عدا يعدو, of the pattern (bāb) of نصر; its wazn is فَعْل, with fatḥa then sukūn. The verb has other maṣdars: عُدُوّ with ḍamma on the ʿayn, عَداء with fatḥa on the ʿayn, عُدوان / عِدوان with ḍamma or kasra on the ʿayn, and عُدوى with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- Among the courtesies taught by the Qurʾan: Allah, Glorified is He, forbade the believers from reviling the disbelievers and their gods which they associate with Allah. He gave as the reason for this that the one who is upon falsehood, if you insult what he believes in, will return the insult to you; so if you are upon the truth, you will have caused the truth to be insulted, and the religion of truth.
This Qurʾanic courtesy was, and still is, one of the social necessities, imposing itself in refined relations between nations, however much their religions differ and their creeds diverge.
And none disowns this divine guidance except the fanatics who harm religion while they reckon that they are doing good ... !

safi-cedvel:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (أقسموا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسموا). (جهد) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is annexed to a synonym of the maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "striving" or "exerting themselves" .... See āya (53) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.]». (أيمان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). (إن) a jussive conditional particle. (جاء) a past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (آية) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (يؤمنن) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters ... and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil ... and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis. (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يؤمنن). (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you" (أنت). (إنّما) a restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle. (الآيات) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the interrogative is one of disapproval (inkārī). (يشعر) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), referring to ما. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna. (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of the conditional sense, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (يؤمنون). (جاءت) like the first, and the fāʿil is "it" (هي). (لا) redundant (zāʾida) «[Note: It may be non-redundant; in that case (أنّها) is taken in the sense of (لعلها) "perhaps it", the clause has no grammatical position as a resumptive statement of cause, and the second object of (يشعركم) is omitted, its implied form being "their belief", i.e. "and what makes you perceive their belief? Perhaps when it comes they will not believe in it" .... And if it is non-redundant, the interpreted maṣdar is then the second object, in negated form, as if it were an answer to someone who judged them to be disbelievers forever, i.e. "and what makes you perceive their not believing in it when it comes ..."]». (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and the linking pronoun (rābiṭ) is omitted, i.e. "in it" (بها).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنها ... لا يؤمنون) is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يشعركم, i.e. "and what makes you perceive their belief at the time of its coming".
The clause «أقسموا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن جاءتهم آية ...»: has no grammatical position, an explication of the content of the oath — or parenthetical.
The clause «يؤمنن بها»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنما الآيات عند الله»: in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of saying).
The clause «ما يشعركم....»: in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «يشعركم....»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (ما).
The clause «جاءت....»: in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يؤمنون»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (نقلّب) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "We" (نحن), for majesty. (أفئدة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (أبصار) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أفئدة, accusative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الكاف) a preposition of comparison. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (لم) a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past). (يؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنوا). (أول) an adverb of time, accusative «[Note: i.e. at the coming down of the earlier signs in response to their demands, such as the splitting of the moon ...]», attached to (يؤمنوا). (مرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما لم يؤمنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) ... i.e. "a turning like their disbelief before" «[Note: It may also be attached to an omitted element required by the context, i.e. "We turn their hearts and their eyes, so they do not believe, like their not believing before".]».
(الواو) conjunction. (نذر) like نقلّب, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (في طغيان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعمهون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يعمهون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «نقلب أفئدتهم»: has no grammatical position, resumptive «[Note: It may be conjoined to the clause يؤمنون in the previous āya, falling under the scope of وما يشعركم, i.e. "and what makes you perceive that We turn their hearts" (see al-Jamal in his gloss on al-Jalālayn).]».
The clause «لم يؤمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «نذرهم....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نقلب.
The clause «يعمهون»: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of (نذرهم) ..... or it is a second object if (نذرهم) is taken in the sense of one of the verbs of transformation, i.e. "We make them wander blindly in their transgression".

* Morphology:
(أفئدة): plural of فؤاد, a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the heart or the mind. From it is derived the verb فأده يفأده, of the pattern (bāb) of فتح, when one strikes his heart, and فئد يفأد, of the pattern of فرح, when one complains of his heart. Its wazn is فُعال, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
[End of Part Seven, followed by Part Eight] Part Eight
The remainder of Sūrat al-Anʿām
From āya 111 to āya 165

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أن) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna. (نزلنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent). (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزلنا). (الملائكة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أننا نزلنا....) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it were established" (ثبت).
(الواو) conjunction. (كلم) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الموتى) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. (الواو) conjunction. (حشرنا) like نزلنا. (عليهم) like إليهم, attached to (حشرنا). (كل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (قبلا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the object of حشرنا. (ما) negative. (كانوا) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating — indeclinable on the ḍamma:
and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), or of disapproval. (يؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤمنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna, i.e. "they were not fit for belief".
(إلا) a particle of exception. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (يشاء) an imperfect verb, accusative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء الله) is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) «[Note: Or it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), i.e. "they were not to believe in any state except the state of Allah's willing".]».
(الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating — for rectification (istidrāk). (أكثر) the noun of lākinna, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يجهلون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
The clause «(ثبت) نزول الملائكة....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نزلنا....»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause «كلمهم الموتى»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «حشرنا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ما كانوا....»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يؤمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يشاء الله»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «لكن أكثرهم....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يجهلون»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

* Morphology:
(قبلا): plural of قبيل in the sense of "guarantor", like رغيف and رغف, or in the sense of "group"; the first is a derived adjective, and the second is a collective noun (ism jamʿ). Its wazn is فعيل, and the plural فُعُل with two ḍammas ... There is also a view that it is the opposite of دبر (back), i.e. face to face and in plain sight.

safi-cedvel:148-148.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of the future. (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent). (أشركوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (لو) a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. (شاء) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (ما) a particle of negation. (أشركنا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation. (آباء) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the agent pronoun نا, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: It is said that (لا) made unnecessary the presence of the detached pronoun before the conjunction, as the rule requires.]. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا حرّمنا) like ما أشركنا. (من) a redundant preposition. (شيء) genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الكاف) a preposition [Note: Or a noun meaning "like", in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its qualifier.]. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governing word is the verb after it, i.e. "those before them denied with a denial like that denial which these did" ... the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. (كذّب) like شاء. (الذين) like the first. (من) a preposition. (قبل) a noun made genitive by the preposition, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition. (ذاقوا) like أشركوا. (بأس) a direct object, accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ذاقوا) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (كذّب).
(قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil is "you". (هل) an interrogative particle of disapproval. (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). (من) a redundant preposition. (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation. (تخرجوا) an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the fāʾ; the sign of the subjunctive is the omission of the nūn .... the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object. (اللام) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تخرجوه).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تخرجوه) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the maṣdar implied in the preceding speech, i.e. "is there any knowledge with you, and your bringing it out to us ..."
(إن) a particle of negation. (تتبعون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (الظنّ) a direct object, accusative. (الواو) a conjunction. (إن) like the first. (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (إلّا) like the first. (تخرصون) like تتّبعون.
The clause «سيقول الذين ... »: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أشركوا»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لو شاء الله»: in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما أشركنا»: no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لا حرّمنا ... »: no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما أشركنا.
The clause «كذّب الذين....»: no grammatical position, resumptive — or parenthetical. The clause «ذاقوا....»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «قل....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هل عندكم من علم»: in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «تخرجون....» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has فتخرجوه]: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إن تتبعون....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن أنتم إلّا تخرصون»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تتّبعون.
The clause «تخرصون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(ذاقوا): it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its original form is ذوقوا: the wāw was voweled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif. Its pattern is فعلوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in His saying, the Exalted, «قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنا».
The meaning of فتخرجوه لنا is "so that you make it manifest to us"; He expressed it with "bringing out" because that is a cause of making it manifest and establishing proof for it. So its relation is causality.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ... to the end of the verse.
This verse is a foreshadowing of those tendencies that appeared later among the philosophical sects in Islam: the Jabriyya, the Qadariyya, the Murjiʾa, the Muʿtazila, and other such currents, some of which may conflict with the tolerant Islamic creed, which is far from contradiction and complication.

safi-cedvel:149-149.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). (الحجّة) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (البالغة) a naʿt (adjective) of الحجّة, nominative. (الفاء) a conjunction. (لو شاء): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse.]. (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو. (هدى) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "He". (أجمعين) tawkīd (emphasis) of the second-person pronoun in (هداكم), accusative (manṣūb); the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: Emphasis with (أجمعين) is permissible without the word كلّكم preceding it, as is stated in its chapter.].
The clause «قل....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لله الحجّة ... »: in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the proof" .... and the conditional clause together with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لو شاء....»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the conditional clause that is the speech reported.
The clause «هداكم ... »: no grammatical position, the apodosis of the condition لو.

* Morphology:
(البالغة): feminine of البالغ, active participle of the triliteral بلغ; its pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
1- Emphasis is made with the words أجمعين, جمعاء, أجمع and جمع, either alone or after the word كلّ; these words are not put in the dual, because the words كلا and كلتا make their dual unnecessary.
Ibn Mālik says on this subject:
وبعد كلّ أكّدوا بأجمعا ... جمعاء أجمعين ثم جمعا
(And after كلّ they emphasised with أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعين and then جمع;)
ودون كل قد يجيء أجمع ... جمعا أجمعون ثم جمع
(and without كلّ there may come أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعون and then جمع.)

safi-cedvel:150-150.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) like the preceding [Note: In the previous verse.]. (هلمّ) a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) meaning "bring", and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you (plural)". (شهداء) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of شهداء. (يشهدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh). (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of anna, accusative. (حرّم) a past verb; the fāʿil is "He". (ها) a particle of alerting. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله حرّم ... ) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشهدون).
(الفاء) a conjunction. (إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (شهدوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لا) the prohibitive lā causing the jussive. (تشهد) an imperfect verb, jussive; the fāʿil is "you". (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تشهد), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا تتّبع) like لا تشهد. (أهواء) a direct object, accusative. (الذين) a relative, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (كذّبوا) like شهدوا, and it has no position. (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (الذين) a relative, conjoined to the first, in the position of genitive. (لا) a particle of negation. (يؤمنون) like يشهدون. (بالآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمنون). (الواو) a conjunction. (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (بربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعدلون), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يعدلون) like يشهدون.
The clause «قل ... »: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سلّم شهداءكم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has هلمّ شهداءكم]: in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يشهدون»: no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «حرّم هذا»: in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The clause «إن شهدوا ... »: no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا تشهد ... »: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تتّبع»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «كذّبوا ... »: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يؤمنون ... »: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «هم ... يعدلون»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause لا يؤمنون.
The clause «يعدلون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(هلمّ): a verbal noun of command; it has a single form in the dialect of the Ḥijāzīs, whereas in the dialect of Tamīm the pronouns are attached to it: هلما, هلموا, and هلمّي ... The mīm has fatḥa in both dialects when the noun is assigned to the pronoun of the masculine singular (هلمّ).

* Rhetoric:
1- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا», to indicate that whoever denies the signs of Allah the Exalted and sets up others as equal to Him is a follower of whim and nothing else, and that whoever follows the proof can only be one who affirms it.
2- His saying, the Exalted, «فَلا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ», i.e. do not believe them, for it is sheer falsehood, and make its corruption clear to them, because conceding it to them would be agreeing with them in the false testimony, and silence may suggest approval. The intending of this meaning by «لا تشهد» is either by way of a dependent metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya) or a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) of mentioning the concomitant and intending what it entails, because testimony is among the concomitants of conceding.

* Benefits:
2- هلمّ can be intransitive or transitive, and it is one of the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl). There are two views on its usage. The first, which is the more likely: it is not inflected, and the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine are all the same in it. The second: it is inflected, so it is a verb and the pronouns are attached to it, so one says هلما, هلموا, هلمي, هلممن ... etc.; and the heavy nūn of emphasis may be attached to it, so one says:
هلمّن يا رجل and هلمّن يا امرأة ... etc.
[Translator's note: The source numbers this benefit "2-" with no preceding "1-".]

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّن طِينٍ}: there are two views on it. The more evident of them: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَقكم», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Does this statement need the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) or not? There is a disagreement: a group, such as al-Mahdawī, Makkī and others, held that there is no omission, and that the human being is created from clay; and it is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «There is no child born except that some of the dust of his grave is sprinkled upon the sperm-drop.» It was also said: the sperm-drop's origin is clay. Most of the exegetes said: there is something omitted there, i.e. He created your origin, or your father, from clay — meaning Adam and his well-known story. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
185 - 9- إلى عِرْقِ الثَّرى رَسَخَتْ عُروقي ... وهذا الموتُ يَسْلُبُني شبابي
(My roots are firmly set down to the root of the moist earth, and this death is robbing me of my youth.)
They said: by "the root of the moist earth" he meant Adam, peace be upon him, because he is his origin.

His saying: {ثُمَّ قضى}: if «قضى» means "He made manifest", then «ثُمَّ» is for temporal sequence, according to its basic meaning, because that comes after our creation, and it is an attribute of action. If it means "He wrote and decreed", then it is for sequence in mention, because it is an attribute of essence, and that precedes our creation.

His saying: {وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Two things permitted beginning with it (an indefinite) here. One of them: its being qualified (by an adjective); the second: its being conjoined; and mere conjunction is among the things that permit it. [The poet] said:
186 - 0- عندي اصْطِبارٌ وشَكْوى عند قاتلتي ... فهل بأعجبَ مِنْ هذا امرؤٌ سَمِعا
(With me is patience, and complaint is with the woman who is killing me — has any man ever heard of anything more wondrous than this?)
The indefiniteness of the two terms (أجلين) is for vagueness (ibhām). There is another permitting factor here, which is subdivision (tafṣīl), as in his saying:
186 - 1- إذا ما بكى مِنْ خلفِها انصرفَتْ له ... بشِقٍ وشِقٌ عندنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(Whenever he cried behind her, she turned to him with one half, while one half remained with us, not turned away.)
Putting the khabar first was not obligatory here, even though the mubtadaʾ is indefinite and the khabar is an adverbial (ẓarf). Al-Zamakhsharī said: because it has been specified by the adjective, so it approaches the definite. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he mentioned — that its permitting the indefinite to be a mubtadaʾ is due to its being qualified — is not the only possibility, since the permitting factor could be the subdivision"; then he quoted the verse «إذا ما بكى». I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that this is the only possibility, so that he could be held to it; he merely mentioned the best-known of the permitting factors, for few mention conjunction and subdivision among the permitting factors.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the common usage is to say «عندي ثوب جيِّدٌ، ولي عبدٌ كيِّس» (I have a fine garment, and I have a clever slave) [with the khabar first], so what made the fronting [of the mubtadaʾ] necessary? I say: what made it necessary is that the meaning is: and what a term appointed with Him!, in magnification of the matter of the Hour; so since this meaning ran through it, it necessitated the fronting." The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible, because if the implied form is «وأيُّ أجل مسمَّى عنده», then «أيّ» would be an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being «وأجلٌ أيُّ أجلٍ مسمَّى عنده», and it is not permissible to omit the adjective when it is «أيّ», nor to omit its qualified noun and keep it: if you said «مررت بأيِّ رجل», meaning «برجلٍ أيِّ رجل», it would not be permissible." I say: I do not know how one can be held to account who explained a meaning with a wording without claiming that this wording is the underlying form of the explained speech; rather he said: its meaning is such-and-such. So how can he be bound to the claim that the speech he explained with is the underlying form of what is explained? Besides, the omission of the qualified noun of «أيّ» while keeping it has occurred, as in his saying:
186 - 2- إذا حارب الحَجَّاجُ أيَّ منافقٍ ... عَلاه بسيفٍ كلما هَزَّ يقطعُ
(Whenever al-Ḥajjāj fights some hypocrite — what a hypocrite! — he strikes him from above with a sword that cuts whenever he brandishes it.)

His saying: {ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ}: the discussion of this «ثم» has preceded. «تمترون» is of the form taftaʿūn from al-mirya (doubt), and its meaning preceded in al-Baqara at His saying {مِنَ الممترين} [verse 147]. The Shaykh made this a case of iltifāt (shift of person), I mean His saying «خَلَقَكم ثم أنتم تَمْتَرون»; he means that His saying {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ} is in the third person, so He turned from it to His saying «خلقكم ثم أنتم». Then it is as though he raised an objection against himself, that "your creation" and the decreeing of the term are not specific to the disbelievers; rather the believers are like them in that. He answered that He intended only the disbelievers, to alert them to His creating them, His power, and His decreeing of their terms. He said: "I made it a case of iltifāt only because this address, namely {ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ}, cannot include those whom Allah has chosen for prophethood and faith."

The origin of «مُسَمَّى» is «مُسَمَّوٌ», because it is from the root of «الاسم», and that has preceded; the wāw was changed into yāʾ, then the yāʾ into alif. «تمترون»: its origin is «تَمْتَرِيُون», and it underwent weakening (iʿlāl) like its counterparts that have preceded.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَهُوَ الله فِي السموات}: there are many views on this verse, all of which I have summarised in twelve aspects. That is because there are two views on «هو». One of them: it is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, referring to what the pronouns before it referred to. The second: that it is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa); Abū ʿAlī said this. The Shaykh said: "He fled to this only because, had he referred it to Allah, the implied form would become «الله الله», and the speech would be composed of two nouns identical in wording and meaning with no predicative relation between them." I say: the pronoun refers only to the One previously described with those majestic attributes, namely the creation of the heavens and the earth, the making of the darknesses and the light, and the creation of people from clay, to the end of them; so in predicating that there is a benefit without doubt. On the view of the majority, then, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الله» its khabar (predicate), and «في السماوات» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the very word of majesty (the name Allah), because of the meaning of worship that it contains, as if it were said: "and He is the One worshipped in the heavens." This is the view of al-Zajjāj, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«في السماوات» is attached to the meaning of the name of Allah, as if it were said: and He is the One worshipped in them — and of this is {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله} [al-Zukhruf: 84] — or He is the One known for divinity and alone in divinity in them, or He is the One who is called "Allah", no one else sharing this name with Him." I say: he said "or He is the One known… or He is the One who is called Allah" only because there has preceded for you a disagreement about this noble name: is it derived or not? If it is derived, the attachment of the preposition phrase to it is evident. If it is not derived, then it is either transferred (manqūl) or coined (murtajal), and on both assumptions it does not govern, because proper names do not govern. So he needed to interpret that according to each of these three views: his saying "the One worshipped" goes back to derivation; his saying "the One known" goes back to its being a transferred proper name; and his saying "the One who is called Allah" goes back to its being coined. It is as though he — may Allah have mercy on him — sensed the objection mentioned. The objection is transmitted from al-Fārisī, who said: "If you make the adverbial attached to the name of Allah, it is permissible in my view on the analogy of those who say that «الله» is originally «الإله»; but whoever treats this name as a proper name, it must, in his view, not be attached to it, unless you assume in it some kind of verbal meaning." So it is as though al-Zamakhsharī — and Allah knows best — took this from al-Fārisī's statement and expanded it. However, Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted from Abū ʿAlī that «في» is not attached to the name of Allah, because through the entry of the alif and lām, and the change that entered it, it has become like a proper name; and for this reason the Exalted said: {هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً} [Maryam: 65]. The apparent sense of this transmission is that he prevents attachment to it, even if it is originally derived.

Al-Zajjāj said: "It is attached to the meanings that the name of Allah contains, as when you say: «أميرُ المؤمنين الخليفة في المشرق والمغرب» (the Commander of the Faithful is the caliph in the East and the West)." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view this is the best of the views and the one that most secures the eloquence of the wording and the weightiness of the meaning. Its explanation is that He wished to indicate His creation, the traces of His power, His encompassing, His dominion and similar attributes, so He gathered all of these in His saying {وَهُوَ الله}, i.e. the One to whom all of these belong in the heavens and in the earth; as if He said: and He is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Encompasser in the heavens and the earth — as you say «زيد السلطان في الشام والعراق» (Zayd is the sultan in Syria and Iraq). If you intended Zayd's person, it would be absurd; but if the intent of your saying is: [Zayd] is the one who commands and forbids, who appoints and dismisses, it is eloquent and correct; you have put "sultanship" in place of these attributes. Likewise in the noble verse, you have put «الله» in place of those attributes."

The Shaykh said: "What al-Zajjāj mentioned and Ibn ʿAṭiyya clarified is correct in terms of meaning, but the craft of grammar supports it [Translator's note: so in the text; the sequel indicates the intended sense is "does not support it"]; because the two of them claimed that «في السماوات» is attached to the name of Allah because of those meanings it contains, and had those meanings been stated explicitly, not all of them would govern it; rather the governing, in terms of wording, would belong to one of them, even if «في السماوات» is attached to all of them in terms of meaning. Rather, it is better that it be attached to the word «الله» because of the meaning of divinity it contains, even though it is a proper name, because a proper name governs an adverbial because of the meaning it contains, as in his saying:
186 - 3- أنا أبو المِنْهالِ بعضَ الأحيانْ ...
(I am Abū al-Minhāl at certain times.)
«بعضَ» is made accusative by the proper name because it has the meaning of "I am the famous one"." I say: his saying "had they been stated explicitly they would not govern" is not conceded; rather they would govern, and their governing would be by way of contention (tanāzuʿ) — besides, had he kept silent about the answer it would be clear. And when the Shaykh mentioned what al-Zamakhsharī said, he said: "So look how he assumed the governing element in it to be one, not all of them," meaning that he sought support from it for his rebuttal of al-Zajjāj and Ibn ʿAṭiyya.

The second aspect: that «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element which is an adjective of Allah the Exalted, omitted because the meaning is understood. Some assumed it as: "and He is Allah, the One worshipped", and some: "and He is Allah, the Disposer". Omission of the adjective is very rare; only a few places have come of it, and those are open to scrutiny, among them {وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ} [al-Anʿām: 66], i.e. the obstinate ones, and {إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} [Hūd: 46], i.e. those saved. So this should not be construed on it.

The third aspect: al-Naḥḥās said — "and it is the best that has been said about it" — that the speech is complete at His saying {وَهُوَ الله}, and the genitive phrase is attached to the object of «يَعْلَم», which is «سِرَّكم وجَهْرَكم», [i.e.] He knows your secret and your open [speech] in them. This is very weak, because it involves putting the governed element of the maṣdar (verbal noun) before it, and what is wrong with that is known.

The fourth aspect: that the speech is likewise complete at the word of majesty, and the adverbial is attached to «يعلم» itself. This is evident, and on these two aspects «يعلم» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

The fifth aspect: that the speech is complete at His saying {فِي السموات}, so {فِي السموات} is attached to the name of Allah, as preceded, and «في الأرض» is attached to «يعلم». This is the view of al-Ṭabarī. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak, because Allah the Exalted is worshipped in the heavens and in the earth, and knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, so neither of the two attributes is specified by one of the two adverbials." It is a fine rebuttal.

The sixth aspect: that «في السماوات» is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «سرَّكم», and then the ḥāl was put before the one it describes and before its governing element.

The seventh: that it is attached to «يَكْسِبون». This is corrupt in that it entails putting the governed element of the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative, because «ما» is a nominal or particle relative. Also, how would those addressed earn in the heavens? Had this proponent held that the speech is complete at His saying «في السماوات» and attached «في الأرض» to «يَكْسِبون», the matter would be easier in terms of meaning, though not in terms of the craft.

The eighth: that «الله» is a first khabar and «في السماوات» a second khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense that He is Allah and that He is in the heavens and in the earth, and in the sense that He knows what is in them, nothing being hidden from Him, as if His essence were in them." The Shaykh said: "This is weak because what is governed by «في» does not indicate a restricted (specific) being, it only indicates an absolute (general) being." This is easy to answer, as it has preceded many times.

The ninth: that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «الله» a badal (substitute) of it, «يَعْلَمُ» its khabar, and «في السماوات» as preceded.

The tenth: that «الله» is likewise a badal, and «في السماوات» is the khabar in the sense al-Zamakhsharī stated.

The eleventh: that «هو» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the word of majesty is a second mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «في السماوات» in the aforementioned sense, or «يَعْلَمُ» — and the clause is the khabar of the first, explicating it — and this is the twelfth.

As for «يَعْلَمُ», you have learned the details of what preceded: that it may be resumptive, so it has no [grammatical] position, or in the position of nominative as a khabar, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. As for «سِرَّكم وجهرَكم»: they may be in their proper sense as maṣdars, being annexed to the agent. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed them to stand in the place of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "what you keep secret and what you make public", and he adduced as evidence His saying, Exalted is He: {يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ} [al-Baqara: 77]. But there is no evidence [in it], because «ما» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival). And «ما» in «ما تكسبون» may be maṣdariyya — which is more fitting, matching the two maṣdars before it — or may mean "that which".

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ}: Regarding the two pronouns — I mean «هم» and the hāʾ of «عنه» — there are several views. The first: the nominative one refers to the disbelievers and the genitive one refers to the Qur'an, which is also what the accusative pronoun in «يَفْقهوه» referred to, and what is pointed to by their saying «إنْ هذا». The second: «هم» refers to the disbelievers mentioned before, and the pronoun in «عنه» refers to the Messenger; on this view there is an iltifāt (shift of address) from the second person to the third person, for His saying {جَآءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ} is an address to the Messenger, and it moved out of this address to the third person. It has also been said: the nominative one refers to Abū Ṭālib and his followers.
In His saying {يَنْهَوْنَ} and {وَيَنْأَوْنَ} there is tajnīs al-taṣrīf (paronomasia of inflection), which means that each word differs from the other by one letter: يَنْهَوْن is distinguished by the hāʾ and يَنْأَوْن by the hamza. Like it is His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ} [al-Kahf: 104], {بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ. . . . . . وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ} [Ghāfir: 75], and his saying, upon him be peace: «الخيلُ معقودٌ في نواصيها الخيرُ» (goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses). Some call it «tajnīs al-taḥrīf» (paronomasia of alteration), which is the difference between two words by one letter, and they cited:
188 - 4- إنْ لم أشُنَّ على أبن حرب غارةً ... لم تَخْلُ يوماً من نِهاب نفوسِ
(If I do not launch a raid on Ibn Ḥarb, a raid never empty, any day, of the plundering of souls.)
Someone else mentioned that tajnīs al-taḥrīf is when the vowelling is the difference between two words, and counted among it «اللُّهى تفتح اللَّهى» (gifts open uvulas); its full treatment has preceded. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «ويَنَوْن», casting the vowel of the hamza onto the nūn and dropping the hamza; this is a regular (qiyāsī) lightening. النَّأيُ means distance; the poet said:
188 - 5- إذا غيَّر النأيُ المُحِبِّين لم يَزَلْ ... رَسِيسُ الهوى مِنْ حُبِّ مَيَّةَ يبرحُ
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering touch of passion from love of Mayya never ceases to torment.)
And another said:
188 - 6- ألا حَبَّذا هندٌ وأرضٌ بها هندُ ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونها النأيُ البعدُ
(How lovely is Hind, and a land in which Hind is — and Hind, between whom and me has come distance, remoteness.)
— conjoining a thing to itself because of the difference in wording. One says: نأى زيد يَنْأى نأياً, and it is made transitive by the hamza, so one says أَنْأيْتُه; it is not made transitive by doubling, and likewise every verb whose middle radical is a hamza. Al-Wāḥidī reported that one says نَأَيْتُه in the sense of نَأَيْتُ عنه; al-Mubarrad cited:
188 - 7- أعاذِلُ إن يُصْبحْ صَداي بقَفْرَةٍ ... بعيداً نآني صاحبي وقريبي
(O blamer, if my remains lie one morning in a desert, far away, my companion and my kinsman will have gone far from me.)
i.e. نأى عني. Al-Layth related «نَأَيْت الشيء», meaning: I removed it far, and cited:
188 - 8- إذا ما التَقَيْنا سالَ من عَبَراتنا ... شآبيب يُنْآى سَيْلُها بالأصابع
(Whenever we meet, showers of our tears flow, whose stream is pushed away with the fingers.)
So he built it for the object (passive), i.e. it is moved aside and put away. In sum, this root denotes distance; from it is أَتَنَأَّى, i.e. I undertake distancing. المَنْأى is a distant place; al-Nābigha said:
188 - 9- فإنَّك كالموتِ الذي هو مُدْرِكي ... وإنْ خِلْتُ أنَّ المُنْتأى عنك واسعُ
(For you are like death, which will overtake me, even if I imagine that the place of refuge far from you is wide.)
تناءَى means to move apart from one another; from it is النُّؤيُ for the little trench around the tent to keep water away from it. It has been read: {وناءَ بجانبه}, which is a metathesis of نأى; what indicates this is that the origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is النَّأْيُ, with the hamza before the weak letter.
His saying: {وَإِن يُهْلِكُونَ}: «إنْ» is negative, like the one in His saying {إِنْ هاذآ} [al-Anʿām: 25]; «أنفسهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The object of «يَشْعرون» is omitted, either by restriction (iqtiṣār) or by abbreviation (ikhtiṣār), i.e. "and they do not perceive that they are destroying themselves".

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَلْ بَدَا}: «بل» here is for moving from one story to another, not for cancellation (ibṭāl). The wording of some suggests that it contains a cancellation of the disbelievers' speech, for he said: "«بل» is a rejection of what they wished for, i.e. the matter is not as they said, because they did not say that out of desire for faith; rather they said it out of fear of the punishment and in hope of mercy." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "I do not know what this statement is." I say: and I do not know the reason for his not knowing! It is a sound statement in itself: when they said «يا ليتنا», it is as if they said "we wished", but this wish is not genuine, because they only said it as a precaution (taqiyya); a person may wish for something with his tongue while his heart is empty of it. Al-Zajjāj said: «بل» here is istidrāk (rectification) and the affirmation of a negation, as in their saying: ما قام زيد بل قام عمرو (Zayd did not stand; rather ʿAmr stood). The Shaykh said: "I do not know what negation preceded so that «بل» would affirm it." I say: what is apparent is that the negation al-Zajjāj meant is the one in His saying {وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا} when we make it resumptive (mustaʾnaf), with the implied form "and we do not deny", and the meaning is: rather, they are deniers.
The fāʿil (agent) of «بدا» is His saying {مَّا كَانُواْ}. «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, which is the apparent view, i.e. there appeared to them that which they used to conceal; the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted. It may also be maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. their concealing appeared to them, meaning its consequence; or the maṣdar is applied to the meaning of the passive participle, which is far-fetched. The apparent view is that the two pronouns — I mean the genitive and the nominative in His saying {بَدَا لَهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يُخْفُونَ} — refer to one thing, namely the disbelievers, or the Jews and Christians specifically. It has also been said: the genitive one is for the followers and the nominative one for the chiefs, i.e. rather, there appeared to the followers what the notable, followed men used to conceal.
His saying: {وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ}: the majority read it with a pure ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿmash, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm read «رِدُّوا» with a pure kasra. You already know that the doubled triliteral verb (whose second and third radicals are the same) allows, when built for the object (passive), the same three options in its first radical that are mentioned for the first radical of the hollow verb when passive, such as قيل and بيع; that has preceded. The poet said:
189 - 7- وما حِلَّ مِنْ جهلٍ حُبا حُلمائِنا ... ولا قائلُ المعروف فينا يُعَنَّفُ
(The sitting-cloths of our wise men are never loosened out of folly, nor is the one who speaks what is right rebuked among us.)
with kasra on the ḥāʾ.
His saying: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}: discussion of this clause has preceded: is it resumptive, or does it go back to His saying {يا ليتنا}?

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وقالوا}: Is this clause conjoined to the answer of «لو», the implied form being "and if they were returned they would revert and would say", or is it resumptive (mustaʾnafa), not falling within the scope of «لو», or is it conjoined to His saying {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}? Three views. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned the first and the last, for he said: "«وقالوا» is conjoined to «لعادوا», i.e. if they were returned they would disbelieve and would say: there is nothing but our worldly life, as they used to say before witnessing the Resurrection. It may also be conjoined to His saying {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ}, in the sense: and they are a people who lie in everything." The first view is reported from Ibn Zayd, except that Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected it, saying: "Allah's making them stand, in the verse after it, before the resurrection, and the reference to it in His saying {أَلَيْسَ هذا بالحق} [Āl ʿImrān: 30], refutes this interpretation." [Translator's note: the verse reference «آل عمران: 30» is as printed; the words {أَلَيْسَ هذا بالحق} are in al-Anʿām 6:30.] This may be answered by the difference of two states: their acknowledgement of the resurrection in reality is only in the Hereafter, while their denial of it is only in this world, on the supposition of their return to this world; so their acknowledging it in the abode of the Hereafter does not conflict with their denying it in this world.
His saying: {إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا}: «إنْ» is negative, «هي» is mubtadaʾ (subject) and «حياتُنا» its khabar (predicate). They were not content with merely stating this, but presented it as restricted by negation and affirmation. «هي» is a vague pronoun explained by its khabar, i.e. we do not know what is meant by it except by the mention of its khabar; it is one of the pronouns explained by what comes after them both in wording and in rank. I treated this earlier at His saying {فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ} [al-Baqara: 29]. That this is among what is explained by what follows in wording and rank is open to question, since someone may say that «هي» refers to something indicated by the context of speech, as if they said: the continuing custom, or our state and what we have known, is nothing but our worldly life. This speaker relied on al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "This is a pronoun whose intended meaning is not known except by mentioning what follows it"; al-Zamakhsharī gave as examples the Arabs' sayings: «هي النفس تتحمَّل ما حَمَلَتْ» (it is the soul: it bears what it is made to bear) and «هي العرب تقول ما شاءت» (they are the Arabs: they say what they will).
There is no proof for him in what al-Zamakhsharī said, because he means that what the pronoun refers to is not known except by the mention of what follows it, and there is nothing in this indicating that the khabar explains the pronoun. The meaning may be: there is no life but our worldly life; so His saying {إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا الدنيا} indicates what explains the pronoun, namely life in general. Thus it is true of it that what is meant by it is not known [Translator's note: the printed text has «لا يعمل», evidently for «لا يُعلم»] except by the mention of what follows, from this angle, not from the angle of explanation. What I have said is supported by the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "«هي» is an allusion to life; it may also be the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa)."
I say: as for the first part of his statement, it is correct; as for its last part, namely his saying that «هي» is the pronoun of the story, it is nothing, because the pronoun of the story is only explained by a clause with both of its parts expressed. If you say: the Kufan permits its explanation by a single word, so he may have followed their approach — the answer is that the Kufan only permits it with a single word that operates like a verb, such as «إنه قائم زيد» and «وظنتُه قائِماً زيدٌ», because it has the form of a clause, since the expression contains a predicand (musnad) and a subject of predication (musnad ilayhi). As for something like «هو زيد», no one permits it with «هو» being a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) or of the story. «الدنيا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الحياة», and it is not an adjective removing an incidental shared reference — meaning that there is some life other than the worldly one which they acknowledge — because they know only this one; so it is an adjective for mere tawkīd (emphasis); so it has been said, and they mean by that that it has no implied contrary meaning (mafhūm); otherwise, actual emphasis is not apparent, unlike {نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 13]. The bāʾ in His saying «بمبعوثين» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasising the negated khabar; its genitive noun may be accusative in position, on «ما» being Ḥijāzī, or nominative, on its being Tamīmī.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {على رَبِّهِمْ}: There are two views on it. The first: it is a case of omission, its implied form being "before the questioning of their Lord", or "the dominion of their Lord", or "the recompense of their Lord". The second: it is a case of figurative usage (majāz), because it is an allusion to detention for rebuke, just as a slave is made to stand before his master so that he may reproach him. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this and preferred the figurative usage to the omission, since he began with the figurative usage and then said: "And it has been said: [they were made to stand] before the recompense of their Lord." People disagree over preferring one of them to the other. The sum of the matter is that there are three positions: the best known is preferring figurative usage over implication (iḍmār); the second is its reverse; and the third is that they are equal.
His saying: {قَالَ أَلَيْسَ}: There are two views on this clause. The first: it is "istifhāmiyya", i.e. the answer to an implied question. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the sense, as the following quotation shows, is "istiʾnāfiyya" (resumptive).] Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«قال» is a reply to the saying of one who says: what did their Lord say to them when they were made to stand before Him? And it is answered: He said to them: is this not the truth?" The second: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is «ربُّهم», as if it were said: they were made to stand before Him while He was saying: is this not the truth? As for what is pointed to, it has been said: it is the resurrection which they used to deny; and it has been said: it is the punishment, indicated by {فَذُوقُواْ العذاب}.
His saying: {بِمَا كُنتُمْ}: «ما» may be a nominal relative noun, the implied form being "تكفرونه", originally "تكفرون به"; the pronoun was attached to the verb after the intermediary [preposition] was dropped. It is not permissible for it to be omitted while still in the genitive, even though it is governed by a preposition like the one governing the relative noun, because what they are attached to differs; this has been explained more than once. It is preferable to make «ما» maṣdariyya (infinitival) with the object of disbelief omitted, the implied form being: because you used to disbelieve in the ʿabath [Translator's note: so printed, «بالعبث»; evidently for «بالبعث», the resurrection] or in the punishment, i.e. in meeting it — that is, because of your disbelief in that.

semin-durr:95-95.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَالِقُ الحب}: It is permissible/ for the iḍāfa (genitive construct) to be pure (maḥḍa), on the view that it is an active participle in the sense of the past, because that has already happened; this is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «فلق» as a past verb.
