So when He says "ten like it", or says ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أمْوالَهم في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنابِلَ في كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 261], together with His saying ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 245], the meaning of all this is that the recompense of Allah, exalted is His praise, for good deeds is by multiplication of the single like, which is the utmost of estimation in [people's] souls; and Allah multiplies that by between tenfold and seven hundredfold, up to many multiples. The exegetes are agreed on His saying ﴿وَمَن جاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلا يُجْزى إلا مِثْلَها﴾, because the evil deed here is associating partners with Allah; and they said: "whoever comes with the good deed" — it is saying "There is no god but Allah". The root of good deeds is the affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd), and the worst of evil deeds is disbelief in Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

zajjaj:161-161.t:
﴿قُلْ إنَّنِي هَدانِي رَبِّي إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: ”اَلصِّراطُ“ is the religion; [i.e.] "who has directed me to the religion that is the religion of truth". Then He explained that and said: ﴿دِينًا قِيَمًا﴾; ”اَلْقِيَمُ“ is the upright. It has also been read ”دِينًا قَيِّمًا“. ”قِيَمٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like ”اَلصِّغَرُ“ (smallness) and ”اَلْكِبَرُ“ (greatness), except that He did not say ”قِوَمٌ“, as in His saying ﴿لا يَبْغُونَ عَنْها حِوَلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 108], because your saying ”قامَ قِيَمًا“ is as though it were based on ”قَوُمَ“ or ”قَوِمَ“; when [the verb] became weak (iʿtalla) and became ”قامَ“, ”قِيَمٌ“ became weak too. As for ”حِوَلٌ“, it is on the basis that it runs on no verb.

As for the accusative of ﴿دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفًا﴾, it is construed by meaning, because when He said ﴿هَدانِي رَبِّي إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾, that indicated "He made known to me an upright religion" (”عَرَّفَنِي دِينًا قِيمًا“). And it is possible that it is a badal (substitute) from the meaning of "He guided me to a straight path"; the meaning: "He guided me [on] a straight path, an upright religion", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِراطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 2]. ”مِلَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ“ is a badal from ”دِينًا قِيَمًا“, and ”حَنِيفًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ”إبْراهِيمَ“; the meaning is: "He guided me and made known to me the creed of Ibrāhīm in the state of his being ḥanīf". Here it is better [taken] for Ibrāhīm than for another. ﴿وَما كانَ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾. We have already explained the meaning of ”اَلْحَنِيفِيَّةُ“: that it is inclining towards Islam with an inclination that has no turning back.

zajjaj:162-162.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ صَلاتِي ونُسُكِي ومَحْيايَ ومَماتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾: they said: ”اَلنُّسُكُ“ is sacrificial slaughter, and ”اَلنُّسُكُ“ is whatever is offered to draw near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. ﴿وَمَحْيايَ ومَماتِي﴾: the yāʾ is the yāʾ of annexation (possessive yāʾ); it takes fatḥa because its origin is fatḥa, and it may be given sukūn when what precedes it is vowelled. ”مَماتِي“ is permissible: if you wish, you read ”مَماتِيَ لِلَّهِ“ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and if you wish, you give it sukūn. As for the yāʾ of ”مَحْيايَ“, it must take fatḥa, because what precedes it is quiescent.

The meaning of the verse is that he informs that one draws near through prayer and all the rites only to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, not to other than Him, as the idolaters used to slaughter for their idols. So He made known that it is Allah alone, by His saying: ﴿لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وبِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 163].

zajjaj:164-164.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أبْغِي رَبًّا وهو رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, that is: He originated all things; no one is able to originate anything of them.

And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾, that is: no sinful soul is taken to account for the sin of another; no one is taken to account for another's wrongdoing.

zajjaj:165-165.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكم خَلائِفَ الأرْضِ﴾: it is said: "the successors of the earth" are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, because the Prophet ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, so his community has succeeded all the other communities. Some said: "successors of the earth" means some of you succeed others. ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكم فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكم في ما آتاكُمْ﴾: by this He indicated that He has favoured some people in order to test them in what He has provided them; and He, exalted is His praise, knows what will come from them before that, except that He tests them so that what reward and punishment are based on becomes manifest from them.

And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ العِقابِ وإنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: if someone says: How is it said "swift in punishment", when His punishment is only on the Day of Resurrection, even though some of it has occurred in this world? That is only because the matter of the Hour is swift, since everything that passes away, even if it is long drawn out, is in the position of what is not perceived, for swiftness. Likewise His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ أوْ هو أقْرَبُ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 77], and likewise His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنَّهم يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 6] ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 7].

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: «يوم» is accusative on two aspects. One of them is on the meaning «واتقوه، ويوم يقول …» ("and fear Him, and the day He says …"), so that it is co-ordinated (nasaq) with the hāʾ [of «اتقوه»], as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 48]. The better is that it be on the meaning «واذكر يقول كن فيكون» ("and mention [the day] He says: Be, and it is"), because after it comes ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ لأبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 74].
[Translator's note: «يوم» is missing from the printed paraphrase «واذكر يقول كن فيكون»; the sense requires «واذكر يومَ يقول».]
There is a third aspect in it, which is conjunction with ﴿السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ﴾, the meaning being: "and He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and created the day He says: Be, and it is".

If someone says: "The Day of Resurrection has not yet come", [the answer is that] whatever Allah has informed us will come to be, its reality is occurring without doubt.

And His words: ﴿كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: some said the address here is to the forms (al-ṣuwar), the meaning being "and the day He says to the forms: Be, and it is", and the mention made of «الصور» indicates it. It has also been said that His word «كن» contains the names of all that is created at that time, the meaning being "and the day He says to the thing: Be, and it is". This is mentioned to indicate the speed of the matter of the resurrection and the Hour, as if He said: "and the day He says to creation: Die, and they die; and Spread out, and they spread out" — as if He commands life and it comes to be in them, and death, and it descends first, [and] all creation perishes.

It has also been said: «ويوم يقول كن فيكون» — ﴿قَوْلُهُ﴾, i.e. "He commands, and His command takes place", and ﴿الحَقُّ﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوله», just as you say «قد قلتَ فكان قولُك» ("you said, and your word came to be"): the meaning is not that you spoke and the speech came to be; the meaning is only that what the speech indicated came to be. On the first view, «قوله» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

And His words: ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾: the accusative of «يوم» may be on ﴿وَلَهُ المُلْكُ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾, explaining His words «ويوم يقول كن فيكون». It may also be accusative by «قوله الحق», the meaning being: "and His word is the truth on the day the trumpet is blown".

If someone says: "Dominion belongs to Allah at all times, so why are the Day of Resurrection and the day the trumpet is blown singled out?", the answer to this is that it is the day in which no benefit or harm from anyone to anyone appears, as He said: ﴿والأمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 19], while the command at every time belongs to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

They have two views on «الصور»: it is said in the exegesis that «الصور» is the name of a horn that is blown into; and it is said that «الصُّوَر» is the plural of «صورة» (form). Both are permissible, and the more firmly established of them in ḥadīth and transmission is that «الصور» is a horn; and «الصور» as the plural of «صورة» — the people of the language hold to this.

zajjaj:74-74.t: And His words: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ لأبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾: with the accusative (fatḥa) and with ḍamma. Whoever reads with ḍamma does so as a vocative (nidāʾ), the meaning being: "O Āzar, do you take idols?". There is no disagreement among the genealogists that the name of Ibrāhīm's father is "Tāriḥ", while what is in the Qurʾān indicates that his name is "Āzar". It has been said that "Āzar" was, among them, a term of blame in their language, as if [He said]: "And when Ibrāhīm said to his father: O you who err, do you take idols?"; if it is so, the choice is the nominative. It may also be a description of him, as if He said: "And when Ibrāhīm said to his father, the one who errs". It has also been said that "Āzar" is the name of an idol; if it is the name of an idol, its position is accusative on an implied verb, as if He said: "And when Ibrāhīm said to his father: Do you take Āzar as a god? Do you take idols as gods?".

zajjaj:75-75.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِي إبْراهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, i.e. and like what We have described of the story of Ibrāhīm — of what he said to his father — We show him the dominion (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth, i.e. the power by which his proof of the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is strengthened. In speech you say to someone who has done you good or evil: «كذلك أجزيك» ("thus do I repay you"). The meaning of His words ﴿وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ المُوقِنِينَ﴾ is: We show him the dominion of the heavens and the earth because of what he did, and so that he may remain firm in certainty.

«الملكوت» is like «الملك» (dominion), except that «الملكوت» is more intensive in the language than «الملك», because the wāw and the tāʾ are added for intensiveness (mubālagha). Like «الملكوت» are «الرغبوت» and «الرهبوت»; its pattern in terms of the verb is «فَعَلُوت». In the proverb: «رهبوتي خير من رغبوتي» ("being feared is better for me than being desired"), and this is like their saying «أو فرقًا خيرًا من حبّ» ("or fear [is] better than love"). Whoever relates it as «رهبوتي خير من رحموتي» ("being feared is better for me than being pitied"), it is a sound meaning: it establishes from the language that for one to have an awe by which one is feared is better than being pitied.
[Translator's note: «يحقق من اللسان» is as printed; its rendering here is tentative.]

zajjaj:76-76.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَمّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَبًا﴾: one says «جنّ عليه الليل» and «أجنّه الليل» when it becomes dark so that he is concealed by its darkness; and of everything that conceals one says «قد جنّ» and «قد أجنّ». One also says «جنّه الليل», but the choice is «جنّ عليه الليل» and «أجنّه الليل».

It has been said that the people of Ibrāhīm used to worship idols, the sun, the moon and the stars. When Ibrāhīm reached the stage at which reflection becomes obligatory and the proof becomes binding upon the servant, he looked into the things his people worshipped. When he saw the star which they worshipped, he said to them: ﴿هَذا رَبِّي﴾, i.e. according to your claim — as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 62], attributing them to Himself in reporting their saying. ﴿فَلَمّا أفَلَ﴾, i.e. when it set; one says «أفل النجم يأفِل ويأفُل أفولًا» when it sets. ﴿قالَ لا أُحِبُّ الآفِلِينَ﴾, i.e. I do not love one whose state is that it rises and moves in a manner which makes clear that it is originated (muḥdath), moving from place to place, as all the other things do which you have agreed with me are not gods; i.e. I do not take as a god that whose state is this, just as you do not take as gods all the other things that are of this kind. It is not that he made his argument against them that whatever sets is not a god, because the heaven and the earth are visible, not absent, and this claim is not made about them; he only wanted to make clear to them what is near at hand, because its setting is the nearest thing by which they could be debated, in what was apparent to them — as he said: ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ المَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِها مِنَ المَغْرِبِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 258].

It has also been said that he said this while reflecting for himself; on this view it is like His words: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضالا فَهَدى﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 7]. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has told of Ibrāhīm in His words: ﴿إذْ جاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 84], so there is no doubt that he was safe from doubt entering him concerning the matter of Allah; and Allah knows best.

It may also be on an implied «القول» (saying), as if He said: ﴿فَلَمّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَبًا قالَ هَذا رَبِّي﴾, as if he said: "You say: This is my lord", i.e. "you are the ones saying: This is my lord" — as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإذْ يَرْفَعُ إبْراهِيمُ القَواعِدَ مِنَ البَيْتِ وإسْماعِيلُ رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنّا﴾ [al-Baqara: 127], the meaning being: "the two of them say: Accept from us". Allah knows best the reality of this. What I hold regarding this saying is that he said to them: "You say: This is my lord", i.e. this governs me — because, as is related, they were people of the stars (astrologers); so he argued against them that what you claim to be a governor shows in it only the trace of something governed, nothing else.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأى الشَّمْسَ بازِغَةً﴾, and «فلما رأى القمر بازغًا»: one says «قد بزغ القمر» when it begins to rise, and likewise the sun. The argument regarding the sun and the moon is like the argument regarding the star.

Those who said that he said «هذا ربي» by way of conjecture and reflection argued from his words: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنِي رَبِّي لأكُونَنَّ مِنَ القَوْمِ الضّالِّينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 77]. But this does not necessitate that, because the prophets ask Allah to keep them firm upon guidance, and they know that were it not for Allah's guidance they would not be guided; and Ibrāhīm says: ﴿واجْنُبْنِي وبَنِيَّ أنْ نَعْبُدَ الأصْنامَ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 35].

zajjaj:79-79.t: And His words: ﴿إنِّي وجَّهْتُ وجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ حَنِيفًا﴾, i.e. inclining to Islam with an inclination from which there is no return. «الحنف» is for there to be an inclination in the foot, namely that the big toe of one foot inclines towards the big toe of the other foot, so that this foot turns towards that foot, and this is congenital. «الحنيف» is the one whose inclination to Islam is sound, firm in it. The meaning of ﴿وَجَّهْتُ وجْهِيَ﴾ is: I have made the aim of my worship my affirming the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:80-80.t: His words, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿وَحاجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ﴾: the meaning is: they disputed with him concerning Allah, so he said: ﴿أتُحاجُّونِّي في اللَّهِ﴾. Their disputing with him was — and Allah knows best — about what they worshipped alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of the stars, the sun, the moon and the idols. So he said: ﴿أتُحاجُّونِّي في اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. concerning the oneness of Allah, ﴿وَقَدْ هَدانِي﴾, and He has made clear to me that by which I have been guided. ﴿وَلا أخافُ ما تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ﴾, i.e. these things which you worship neither harm nor benefit, and I do not fear them. ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئًا﴾: unless He wills to punish me for a sin, if one should come from me. The position of «أن» is accusative, i.e. I fear nothing but the will of Allah.
